$comment: GENERATED by scripts/build-manifest.mjs — machine-readable context for AI agents and tools. Do not edit.
name: @danitesler/ayywi
description: The AI-first design system (say "AY-wee": AI + UI). One CSS class contract for HTML, Vue, Svelte, Angular, server templates, plus typed React components, a linter and an MCP server.

entrypoints.@danitesler/ayywi/css: Full stylesheet (tokens + base + all components) in cascade layers ayywi.tokens < ayywi.base < ayywi.components < ayywi.utilities < ayywi.brand — any unlayered app CSS wins. @danitesler/ayywi/ayywi.min.css is the minified file.
entrypoints.@danitesler/ayywi/ayywi.unlayered.css: Same without cascade layers. Use it when an unlayered CSS reset would otherwise override components.
entrypoints.@danitesler/ayywi/css/<file>.css: Per-file layered CSS: tokens.css, base.css, one file per component (button.css, card.css…), then focus.css (focus rings for keyboard use only, with trackInputModality()).
entrypoints.@danitesler/ayywi/brands/<name>.css: Ready-made brands (violet), applied with data-brand="<name>" or setBrand("<name>"). Make your own with `npx @danitesler/ayywi brand`.
entrypoints.@danitesler/ayywi/fonts.css: Self-hosted brand fonts (Sora, Unbounded, Caveat; woff2, unicode-range subsets). @danitesler/ayywi/fonts-google.css loads them from Google instead.
entrypoints.ayywi: Framework-free JS: tokens, class helpers (buttonClass…), controllers that wire behaviour onto your markup and return a cleanup (connectActionBar, connectAppShell, connectBlockEditor, connectCarousel, connectColorPicker, connectCombobox, connectCommand, connectDatePicker, connectDateRange, connectDateTimePicker, connectDragDrop, connectGrid, connectIconPicker, connectInlineEdit, connectMentions, connectMenu, connectNavbar, connectPinInput, connectPopover, connectRecordPicker, connectShortcutRecorder, connectSwipe, connectTable, connectTableColumnReorder, connectTableColumns, connectTableDragSelect, connectTableEdit, connectTableResize, connectTableRowReorder, connectTagInput, connectTimePicker, connectToc, connectToolbar, connectTransferList, connectTree, enhanceTooltip), toast(), iconSvg(), paginationRange(), setTheme/setDensity/getColorScheme, themeInitScript, createBrand/brandCss/setBrand, cssVar(). Server-safe.
entrypoints.@danitesler/ayywi/react: React components (re-exports everything from ayywi). Marked "use client".
entrypoints.@danitesler/ayywi/elements: Custom elements for any framework or plain HTML: <ayy-toolbar>, <ayy-action-bar>, <ayy-menu>, <ayy-command>, <ayy-navbar>, <ayy-app-shell>, <ayy-toc>, <ayy-tree>, <ayy-pin-input>, <ayy-mentions>, <ayy-block-editor>, <ayy-inline-edit>, <ayy-combobox>, <ayy-tag-input>, <ayy-record-picker>, <ayy-transfer-list>, <ayy-date-picker>, <ayy-date-range>, <ayy-time-picker>, <ayy-date-time-picker>, <ayy-color-picker>, <ayy-icon-picker>, <ayy-shortcut-recorder>, <ayy-tabs>, <ayy-carousel>, <ayy-drag-drop>, <ayy-dialog>, <ayy-popover>, <ayy-tooltip>, <ayy-swipe>, <ayy-table>, <ayy-grid>, plus the card spotlight. dist/elements.global.js registers them from a <script> and exposes window.ayywi (toast, configureToaster, trackInputModality, getInputModality, setTheme, getTheme, getResolvedTheme, getColorScheme, setDensity, getDensity, setIconPack, getIconPack, THEME_PRESETS, setThemeCustomization, createThemeCustomization, createThemeText, setBrand, createBrand, brandCss, brandPresets, chartColors, chartTheme).
entrypoints.@danitesler/ayywi/tokens.json: DTCG-style token source ($value = dark, extensions hold light/density). Extra themes are defined in tokens/themes/*.json.
entrypoints.@danitesler/ayywi/tokens/<file>: Exports for other platforms: dark.json, light.json, dark-contrast.json, light-gray.json, density/*.json (plain DTCG, for Style Dictionary / Figma), brands/<name>/<theme>.json (a brand's overrides to layer over its theme), ayywi.scss, Ayywi.swift (SwiftUI), Ayywi.kt (Jetpack Compose).
entrypoints.npx @danitesler/ayywi: CLI: `lint` (checks app code against this manifest), `brand` (a brand stylesheet from a seed colour, contrast checked), `init` (sets up AI agent files + MCP), `mcp` (MCP server over stdio).

conventions.naming: BEM: .ayy-block, .ayy-block__element, .ayy-block--modifier. Modifiers combine: class="ayy-button ayy-button--outline ayy-button--sm".
conventions.state: State lives in native/ARIA attributes (disabled, :checked, aria-selected, aria-invalid, [open], :popover-open) so every framework drives it the same way.
conventions.theming: No attribute = follow OS (dark or light). data-theme="dark" | "light" | "dark-contrast" | "light-gray" forces a theme on any element and its subtree (.dark/.light classes work too). See "themes" for what each one does; every theme keeps text at WCAG AA. setTheme() switches and persists; getColorScheme() says "dark" or "light".
conventions.density: Controls default to compact (touch on touch-first devices). data-density="compact" | "comfortable" | "touch" on any element resizes buttons, inputs, tabs, switches, checkboxes and menu items below it.
conventions.branding: A brand is one seed colour plus optional fonts and a shape. createBrand() (or `npx @danitesler/ayywi brand`, or the MCP create_brand tool) turns it into an 11-step scale (--ayy-brand-50…950, the seed itself at its nearest step) and, for dark and for light themes, a primary, primary-fg and ring taken from the scale step nearest the seed that keeps 4.5:1 text on the button and 3:1 against every surface in every theme. Fonts get ayywi's fallbacks (system fonts for body text); shape pill | round | soft | sharp (or exact radius) sets --ayy-radius-control, -card and -button. brandCss() writes it in the ayywi.brand layer for [data-brand="<name>"]; setBrand(brand) adds it to the page and sets the attribute. Components never change, only tokens.
conventions.direction: All layout uses logical properties; set dir="rtl" on any ancestor and components mirror. Icons that point along the reading direction (arrows) need directional (ayy-icon--directional) to mirror too.
conventions.elements: Custom elements are light DOM (no shadow root): write the same ayy- markup inside them; they add behaviour. Vue: compilerOptions.isCustomElement = (t) => t.startsWith("ayy-"); Angular: CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA.
conventions.highContrast: Every stateful component has a forced-colors (Windows High Contrast) style using system colours.
conventions.icons: Hugeicons is the icon library: install @hugeicons/core-free-icons (an optional peer; ayywi renders its data, so there's still no runtime dependency). React: <Icon icon={Search01Icon} />. Elsewhere: iconSvg(Search01Icon), or the SVG pasted from hugeicons.com with class="ayy-icon" and no fixed colour attributes. Icons use currentColor and 1.25em (the text size); size sm/md/lg/xl is 16/20/24/32px (--ayy-size-icon-*). Icon packs: the icons ayywi draws itself, and any icon given a name (<Icon icon={…} name="search" />, iconSvg(icon, { name })), can be drawn by Lucide, Tabler Icons, Material Symbols or Feather instead: import "@danitesler/ayywi/icons/<pack>.css" and call setIconPack(pack) (or set data-ayy-icons on any element; the nearest wins). Packs keep their own stroke, so strokeWidth only affects Hugeicons; a glyph a pack lacks stays Hugeicons.

setup: Install from npm: `pnpm add @danitesler/ayywi` (or npm/yarn), then `npx @danitesler/ayywi init`. Import only from "@danitesler/ayywi" and its subpaths ("/react", "/elements", "/css", "/fonts.css", "/brands/*", "/fonts/*", "/icons/*"). Never from "ayywi": that name is only the CLI. Never reach into node_modules/@danitesler/ayywi/dist by path.
Never vendor ayywi: no copy of its dist/ in the repo, no .tgz, no file: or link: dependency in a committed package.json. A fresh clone must install with the package manager alone.

To change ayywi while building an app, point the app's bundler at a local ayywi checkout only for that session (a Vite resolve.alias read from an AYYWI_DIR environment variable, with resolve.dedupe for react and react-dom), and run `pnpm build` in the checkout after each change. Never commit that link.

Upgrade with `pnpm up @danitesler/ayywi`, then `npx @danitesler/ayywi init --force` so the skill, rules and AGENTS.md section match the installed version, and read the CHANGELOG between the two versions.

When ayywi has no component or variant for something, compose it from ayywi pieces in the app, mark it with a `// ayywi-candidate: <what it is>` comment, and add it to ayywi itself when a second screen or app needs it. Never fork, copy or restyle an ayywi component inside the app.
rules: Use existing ayywi classes/components and their variants before writing any custom CSS. Never rebuild one under your own name (a .x-chip, .x-card, a <button> styled by hand) or restyle one: your class next to its ayy- class sets only layout (margin, size, position). If nothing fits, compose ayywi pieces. Never add a second UI kit. Never write a raw native control (<button>, <select>, <input>, <textarea>, <table>, <dialog>, <details>) or a <div>/<span> with a click handler: each is an ayywi component. Before writing a screen, name the component for every piece by what it has to do (the Need → component map, or the MCP pick_component tool).

Never hardcode colours (hex, rgb, hsl, named) — in stylesheets or in inline styles. Use var(--ayy-color-*) tokens; for tints use color-mix(in srgb, var(--ayy-color-text) N%, transparent) or the wash/line tokens.
Use logical properties only: margin-inline-start, padding-inline, inset-inline-end, text-align: start, inline-size. Never left/right/margin-left/padding-right, so RTL works.

Spacing, sizes, radius, type and motion come from tokens (--ayy-space-*, --ayy-size-*, --ayy-radius-*, --ayy-text-*, --ayy-weight-*, --ayy-leading-*, --ayy-control-*, --ayy-shadow-*, --ayy-ease-*, --ayy-duration-*). Control sizes follow data-density — don't hardcode heights.

Theme with data-theme="dark|light|dark-contrast|light-gray" (or nothing = follow OS). Never write separate dark-mode colours; tokens already switch. To restyle, override semantic tokens rather than editing components.

Brand a product with a generated brand, never hand-picked colours: `npx @danitesler/ayywi brand <#seed> --name <name>` (or createBrand()/setBrand() from "@danitesler/ayywi", or the MCP create_brand tool) makes the colour scale, primary, primary-fg and ring for every theme with contrast checked, plus fonts and corners (--shape pill|round|soft|sharp). Load its CSS and set data-brand. Colour beyond primary comes from --ayy-brand-50…950 (the scale) for illustrations and brand moments, never on navigation or page backgrounds.

Every interactive element keeps its visible :focus-visible ring. Icon-only buttons need aria-label. Form controls need a label. State lives in native/ARIA attributes (disabled, checked, aria-selected, aria-current, aria-expanded, aria-invalid, aria-busy, open).

Toolbar items and icon-only buttons get a Tooltip explaining their action on hover and keyboard focus, paired with a keyboard hint element (<Shortcut keys="..." /> in React, .ayy-shortcut in HTML) whenever a shortcut exists. Never use native title="" attributes.

Every component's spec lists its states (default, hover, pressed, focus, disabled, selected, error, loading, plus its own such as open) and its sizes, in manifest/components.json, llms/<slug>.md and get_component. Reach a state only through the attribute or prop its spec names. Where a state says it doesn't apply, do what it says instead; never style a state a component doesn't have.
Stateful styles need a @media (forced-colors: active) fallback (Windows High Contrast erases fills).

Prefer animating transform and opacity (use a logical property like inset-inline-start only when the motion must follow text direction). Everything must still work under prefers-reduced-motion — base.css collapses ayy animations. Scroll-in motion comes from .ayy-reveal, not a script; nothing loops unless it shows a live state. Movement on :hover (lifts, zooms, spins) goes inside @media (hover: hover), because a tap leaves :hover stuck on touch screens.

The frame is monochrome; colour comes from the content. Set --ayy-spot (to an --ayy-accent-* token) on the card or page that shows the content, and the spotlight, contents bar, icon tiles and .ayy-accent-text inside pick it up. Never tint the navbar, sidebar, buttons or page background per page.

Websites follow one anatomy: .ayy-skip-link, a Navbar (with a NavbarToggle so its links fold into a menu on phones), then <main> at .ayy-container width (fading Separators between marketing sections), then the Footer. The page's call to action is a ring button (the navbar's repeats the same action); everything else outline or ghost.

Apps (anything signed-in) follow one frame: .ayy-skip-link, then the App shell — a sidebar on wide screens; on phones an __bar (brand plus one or two actions) and a Bottom nav with the sidebar's top destinations, same icons and order (four and a More tab when there are more). Each screen in its main starts with a Page header: the one h1, a line of description, at most one primary button; on phones a screen pushed from a list starts with a Top bar (back, title, actions) instead, and a screen's one main create action can be a Floating action button. Lists of rows on phones get Swipe actions for their two or three most common actions, which are also reachable elsewhere. Settings open over the app in a near-full-screen Dialog (size="full") holding the App shell in settings mode (the Settings pattern: a Settings title and the sections in its sidebar; one section of Settings rows in its main; on phones the dialog fills the screen and the section list and a section are two screens), never in a small or side dialog; desktop apps add a Command palette on ⌘K. Never put a Navbar in an app.

An app screen fills the main. Don't wrap it in .ayy-container or a max-inline-size — a max-inline-size on an example only sizes that example in the docs, it is not page layout. Long text (a description, .ayy-prose) may stop at --ayy-size-measure. Settings mode already centres its column; don't add a second cap.

Every list, table and page has three more states: loading (Skeleton in the shape of the content with aria-busy; a Spinner or <Button loading> for an action), empty (an Empty state with the action that fills it) and error (an Alert with a retry for a failed load or save; FieldError next to a field).

Data views use ayywi's own pieces: Chart (BarChart, LineChart, DonutChart, ScatterChart, HeatmapChart, FunnelChart and the rest), Bar list and Sparkline for charts, coloured from --ayy-chart-1… in order; filters as Chips (with counts) above the results and the active ones as removable chips; sortable Table columns with a .ayy-table__sort button and aria-sort on the <th>. With a chart library, colour it with var(--ayy-chart-N) (SVG) or chartColors() and chartTheme() (canvas); never its default palette.

Pick form controls by the choice: a Segmented control for two to five short options, Choice cards when each option needs a sentence or a price (compact for time slots), a Select for a short list, a Combobox for many known values, a Transfer list to move items between available and chosen lists, a PIN input for verification codes or PINs, Mentions for inline @mentions or #references inside a textarea, a Rating for 1–5 star scores, a Number field for small counts, a Slider for a rough amount, a DatePicker or DatePickerGrid for a date near today (DateRange / DateRangePicker for a date span, TimePicker / TimePickerTrigger for stepped times, DateTimePicker / DateTimePickerTrigger for date and time, native type="date" for a birth date, type="time" for rapid typing), ColorSwatches for a fixed palette or ColorPicker for any custom colour, a Tag input for free-text tags or recipients, a Search bar to filter a list, a Shortcut recorder for key bindings, File upload for files.

Don't write breakpoints for navigation or layout: App shell, Navbar and Pagination switch at 48rem on their own, and .ayy-grid and .ayy-split adapt to their container. If you truly need one, use 48rem (phone) or 64rem (tablet).
Every gets width and height (its real size) so nothing jumps while it loads. Product screenshots go in a Frame. Draw small product visuals as SVG with tokens instead of images with text baked in.
No :dir() selectors — minifiers rewrite them into :lang() lists that ignore dir="rtl". Logical properties make direction checks unnecessary.
Body text must fall back to system fonts — never remove the system-ui stack from --ayy-font-body (CJK/Arabic/Cyrillic rely on it).

Icons come from Hugeicons (@hugeicons/core-free-icons): <Icon icon={Search01Icon} /> in React, iconSvg(Search01Icon) or the pasted SVG with class="ayy-icon" elsewhere. Don't add another icon set: to draw ayywi's own icons, and the common ones you name, in Lucide, Tabler, Material Symbols or Feather, import @danitesler/ayywi/icons/<pack>.css and call setIconPack() (or set data-ayy-icons). Icons are decorative (aria-hidden) unless you give them a label; arrows that point along the reading direction take directional.

In React import from "@danitesler/ayywi/react"; in other frameworks and plain HTML use the class names, the class helpers from "@danitesler/ayywi" (buttonClass…) and the custom elements from "@danitesler/ayywi/elements" (<ayy-app-shell>, <ayy-navbar>, <ayy-tabs>, <ayy-combobox>, <ayy-date-picker>, <ayy-date-range>, <ayy-time-picker>, <ayy-date-time-picker>, <ayy-color-picker>, <ayy-icon-picker>, <ayy-toolbar>, <ayy-action-bar>, <ayy-shortcut-recorder>, <ayy-command>, <ayy-tag-input>, <ayy-record-picker>, <ayy-pin-input>, <ayy-mentions>, <ayy-block-editor>, <ayy-transfer-list>, <ayy-inline-edit>, <ayy-swipe>, <ayy-drag-drop>, <ayy-dialog>, <ayy-menu>, <ayy-popover>, <ayy-tooltip>, <ayy-toc>, <ayy-tree>, <ayy-carousel>, <ayy-table>, <ayy-grid>).

Run `npx @danitesler/ayywi lint` after UI changes and fix every finding it reports, warnings included: raw-control, bare-control, clickable-element and rebuilt-component mean an ayywi component was skipped.

needs.need: Run an action (save, create, delete, open)
needs.how: Button: one primary per view, outline/ghost for the rest, destructive for delete, size icon + aria-label for icon-only; SplitButton + DropdownMenu when one default action has secondary alternatives.
needs.not: <button> with your own classes or none, a <div>/<span> with onClick, a link styled as a button for an action

needs.need: Choose one value from a list (theme, country, role, sort order)
needs.how: Select for a list (it opens ayywi's own options list; touch screens keep the OS picker), Segmented control for two to five short options shown at once, Combobox for many values people type to find.
needs.not: a raw <select>, a button that opens a hand-built <div> of choices, a Dropdown menu used as a picker

needs.need: Choose between options that each need a sentence, an icon or a price (plans, delivery, time slots)
needs.how: ChoiceGroup of ChoiceCards (compact for time slots, scroll for a day strip).
needs.not: Cards with onClick and a selected class

needs.need: Switch between views or ranges of the same content (list/grid, 7d/30d)
needs.how: SegmentedControl, two to five options.
needs.not: a row of buttons with aria-pressed or an active class

needs.need: Show one of several panels of content
needs.how: Tabs (TabsList, TabsTrigger, TabsContent).
needs.not: a Segmented control or buttons that swap panels

needs.need: Turn a setting on or off (a toggle: notifications, dark mode, auto-save)
needs.how: Switch when it applies at once; Checkbox in a form that's submitted, or to agree to something.
needs.not: <input type="checkbox"> unstyled, a toggle drawn with divs

needs.need: Pick one of a few options in a form
needs.how: Radio group; a Segmented control when the options are short.
needs.not: raw <input type="radio">

needs.need: Filter a list or tag things
needs.how: Chips (checkbox, radio or ChipButton, with counts) above the results, the active ones as removable chips; Tag input for free-text tags or recipients.
needs.not: pills built from <span>s or buttons with an active class

needs.need: Move items between two lists (available vs assigned permissions, columns or members)
needs.how: TransferList (<ayy-transfer-list> in HTML) with searchable Available and Selected panes and Move selected / Move all buttons.
needs.not: two custom list boxes with hand-wired state and arrow buttons

needs.need: Filter a list, table or feed (status tabs, faceted dropdowns, active chips)
needs.how: FilterBar with quick filter tabs (FilterBarTabs), faceted dropdown triggers (FilterBarTrigger) with count badges, and active filter chips with a Clear all button.
needs.not: a row of custom buttons with active classes, hand-built filter bars

needs.need: Sort a list, table or feed by field and direction
needs.how: Sorting with SortingTrigger opening a DropdownMenu of sort options, or sortable Table column headers.
needs.not: a button that flips a state with no accessible label, hand-drawn sort arrows

needs.need: Type text, an email, a number or a password
needs.how: Field + Label + Input (Input group for an icon or a unit, Textarea for long text, Number field for small counts), FieldHint and FieldError under it.
needs.not: a raw <input>/<textarea>, a placeholder instead of a label

needs.need: Enter a verification code, OTP or PIN
needs.how: PinInput (<ayy-pin-input> in HTML) inside a Field, with group for a split 3+3 code and mask for secret PINs.
needs.not: six separate <input maxlength="1"> elements wired by hand or a single plain text input

needs.need: Write or edit a rich document: notes, a page, a description with headings, lists, to-dos, images and embeds
needs.how: BlockEditor (<ayy-block-editor> in HTML): Notion-style blocks with / for block types, Markdown shortcuts, a formatting bar, @ mentions and drag handles; store its value (blocks) or convert with blockEditorToMarkdown / blockEditorToHtml.
needs.not: a <textarea> with a Markdown preview, execCommand on one big contenteditable, or a third-party rich text library

needs.need: Mention people or reference issues inline in a comment (@user, #issue)
needs.how: Mentions (<ayy-mentions> in HTML) wrapping a textarea and suggestion listbox.
needs.not: contenteditable rich-text hacks or an unanchored dropdown under a textarea

needs.need: Give or display a star rating or review score
needs.how: Rating (interactive radio stars with optional half and clearable, or readOnly for fractional scores).
needs.not: buttons or spans of ★ characters with custom click handlers

needs.need: Search or filter by typing
needs.how: Search bar to filter what's on screen, Combobox to pick a value, Command palette (⌘K) to jump anywhere.
needs.not: an <input> with a hand-drawn magnifier

needs.need: Pick a date or time
needs.how: DatePicker or DatePickerGrid for one date near today; DateRange or DateRangePicker for a start and end span; TimePicker or TimePickerTrigger for discrete hours and minutes; DateTimePicker or DateTimePickerTrigger for combined date and time; Input type="date" for a birth date, type="time" for rapid keyboard entry.
needs.not: a hand-built month grid or time dropdown

needs.need: Pick an icon or emoji
needs.how: IconPicker (<ayy-icon-picker>) in a Popover or a menu's submenu panel: search, a grid of Hugeicons and emoji, and a remove button.
needs.not: a menu with one item per icon, a hand-built emoji grid

needs.need: Pick a colour
needs.how: ColorSwatches for a fixed set of choices, ColorSwatchCustom or ColorPicker for any custom colour with hue/alpha/hex.
needs.not: a raw <input type="color">, coloured buttons

needs.need: Set an amount or a range
needs.how: Slider / SliderRange for a rough amount or a price range, Number field for exact small counts.
needs.not: a raw <input type="range">

needs.need: Upload files
needs.how: Dropzone (compact in a form), then a List divided of the files with a Progress each.
needs.not: a raw <input type="file">, a dashed div

needs.need: Drag and drop reordering, board or kanban
needs.how: Sortable with SortableItem and DragHandle (or DragDropArea with DropTargets and <ayy-drag-drop> in HTML).
needs.not: a third-party dnd library, raw HTML5 dragstart handlers

needs.need: Record a keyboard shortcut or show one
needs.how: Shortcut recorder to set one; Kbd / Shortcut to show one.
needs.not: a <kbd> or <span> styled by hand

needs.need: Show a code snippet, command or config file
needs.how: CodeBlock with CodeBlockHeader, CodeBlockFilename, CodeBlockCopy, CodeBlockPre and CodeBlockCode (numbered for line numbers, .ayy-token-* for syntax tokens).
needs.not: a raw <pre> with custom background and copy button

needs.need: Show activity history, audit log or chronological events
needs.how: Timeline of TimelineItems (TimelineMarker with pulse on live events, TimelineTime, TimelineTitle, TimelineBody; alternate for wide milestone pages).
needs.not: divs with a border-left line and absolute dots

needs.need: Show more actions behind a button (⋯, a user menu)
needs.how: DropdownMenu of items; destructive item last.
needs.not: a hand-built absolutely positioned <div>

needs.need: Ask to confirm, or collect a few fields over the page
needs.how: Dialog (DialogContent, title, body, footer with the primary action last).
needs.not: window.confirm(), a fixed <div> with a backdrop

needs.need: A side panel, drawer or bottom sheet
needs.how: Dialog with side="end", "start" or "bottom".
needs.not: a custom fixed div that slides in

needs.need: Settings for an app
needs.how: The Settings pattern: a full-size Dialog holding the App shell in settings mode, Settings groups of SettingsRow / SettingsLink.
needs.not: a settings page with Tabs, a small dialog, rows built from divs

needs.need: Small extra content on click (details, a mini form)
needs.how: Popover.
needs.not: a hand-positioned div

needs.need: Explain an icon button on hover or focus
needs.how: Tooltip (the button keeps its aria-label); add a Shortcut inside for its keyboard hint.
needs.not: title="" or a CSS-only bubble

needs.need: Confirm something happened, or offer undo
needs.how: toast.success() / toast() with an action.
needs.not: a hand-built fixed banner

needs.need: Show a capture, video or file preview with quick corner actions
needs.how: toast.card() or CardToast for screen captures, video thumbnails and quick actions.
needs.not: a custom corner popup, fixed floating card without a toaster stack

needs.need: Tell people about a problem or a state on the page
needs.how: Alert (destructive with a retry for a failed load or save).
needs.not: a coloured <div>

needs.need: Show loading
needs.how: Skeleton in the shape of the content (aria-busy on the region), Spinner for a small area, Button loading for an action, Progress for a known amount.
needs.not: "Loading…" text, a hand-drawn spinner

needs.need: Nothing to show yet, or no results
needs.how: Empty state with the action that fills it (compact inside a card or table).
needs.not: a centred muted paragraph

needs.need: Group content in a box
needs.how: Card with CardHeader / CardTitle / CardDescription, CardContent, CardFooter; CardLink when the whole card opens something.
needs.not: a <div> with a border, radius and padding

needs.need: Rows of things (members, files, threads, settings)
needs.how: List (ListLink for clickable rows, divided for settings-style rows); Settings for preference rows; Swipe actions on phones.
needs.not: <ul>/<div> rows with your own borders and hover, <li onClick>

needs.need: Records compared across columns
needs.how: Table (sortable headers, a select column, TableRowActions with inline quick buttons and a ⋯ DropdownMenu), ActionBar when rows are selected, Pagination under it.
needs.not: a raw <table>, a CSS grid of divs

needs.need: Captures, recordings or pictures to open, with their details and actions on hover (a screenshot history, a media library)
needs.how: Cards of the view type (Card view) in a .ayy-grid: CardViewMedia (a button or link that opens it) with CardViewImage letterboxed over a blurred copy, CardViewBadge for a recording's length, CardViewBody for title, details and badges, and grouped HoverActions with a ⋯ DropdownMenu. Use Grid instead when people select several.
needs.not: a plain Card with CardMedia and an , a hand-built gradient caption, absolutely positioned buttons that appear on hover

needs.need: Icon actions over a picture, a video frame or a card (copy, annotate, pin, delete)
needs.how: HoverActions in a corner (position) of the picture's box, reveal to show them on hover and focus, group to put them on one glass bar; each HoverAction has a label that is also its tooltip.
needs.not: ghost buttons restyled with a translucent background, title="" tooltips, buttons that only appear on :hover with no keyboard way to reach them

needs.need: Selectable cards of media assets, screenshots, social posts, projects or user records
needs.how: Grid of GridItems (GridItemSelect checkbox, GridItemActions with inline quick actions and a ⋯ DropdownMenu, GridItemMedia for previews), ActionBar when items are selected.
needs.not: Cards with custom onClick selection state or hand-built floating checkboxes

needs.need: Run bulk actions on selected table rows or grid items (edit, duplicate, copy, archive, delete)
needs.how: ActionBar (open when selection count > 0) with ActionBarSelection, ActionBarCount, ActionBarClose and ActionBarActions of ActionBarButtons (destructive last).
needs.not: a hand-built fixed bottom bar or static buttons above the table

needs.need: A number that matters (KPI)
needs.how: Card + Stat + a status Badge, a Sparkline beside it.
needs.not: big bold text in a div

needs.need: A chart
needs.how: BarChart (grouped, stacked, 100%, horizontal, with lines), LineChart (area, stacked, step), HistogramChart, WaterfallChart, ScatterChart (bubbles), DonutChart (pie), GaugeChart, RadarChart, HeatmapChart, FunnelChart, BarList, Sparkline, coloured from --ayy-chart-1… in order.
needs.not: a chart library's default palette, divs as bars

needs.need: A status, count or label on something
needs.how: Badge (status variants).
needs.not: a coloured <span> pill

needs.need: Show live status, online presence or server health as a compact dot
needs.how: StatusDot (neutral, success, warning, destructive, info variants; pulse for live activity).
needs.not: a coloured <span> or <div> with border-radius: 50%, hand-drawn ping keyframes

needs.need: A person or a team
needs.how: Avatar (image with initials fallback), AvatarGroup.
needs.not: a round or initials in a div

needs.need: Collapsible sections or FAQ
needs.how: Accordion (single to keep one open).
needs.not: a raw <details>, a div toggled by a button

needs.need: A multi-step flow
needs.how: Steps above the form, one primary Continue per step.
needs.not: numbered circles drawn by hand

needs.need: The frame of an app
needs.how: App shell (sidebar, a bar and a Bottom nav on phones), each screen starting with a Page header.
needs.not: a hand-built sidebar, header or bottom tab bar

needs.need: The top of a website
needs.how: Navbar with a NavbarToggle so links fold into a menu on phones.
needs.not: a <header> of links with a hand-built burger menu

needs.need: Where you are, or which page of results
needs.how: Breadcrumb for nested pages, Pagination for pages of results.
needs.not: links separated by slashes, numbered buttons

needs.need: A screen pushed from a list on a phone
needs.how: Top bar (back, title, actions).
needs.not: a hand-built header with a back arrow

needs.need: A screenshot or picture of the product
needs.how: Frame around it.
needs.not: an with a border and shadow

needs.need: Preview UI across responsive viewports with device switcher
needs.how: Showcase with ShowcaseHeader, ShowcaseTitle, ShowcaseActions, ShowcaseStage, and ShowcaseViewport (desktop, tablet, mobile).
needs.not: hand-built iframe wrappers or ad-hoc responsive preview containers

needs.need: Light/dark switch
needs.how: Dropdown menu of themes (radio items) that calls setTheme(); an icon trigger shows the current one. Inside settings, use the theme picker of the Appearance need instead.
needs.not: a button that flips a class

needs.need: Appearance settings: mode (light or dark), theme, reduce motion, language or direction
needs.how: In the Settings pattern's Appearance section: Mode (System, Light, Dark) as a Select with SettingsScreen pictures, applied with setTheme(); Theme as a Select of THEME_PRESETS with SettingsScreen variant="brand" pictures, applied with setBrand(), setThemeCustomization() and setIconPack(); a Select with SettingsScreen pictures for Text direction; Switch for reduce motion (data-motion="reduce"); Select for language; a destructive SettingsLink to reset.
needs.not: separate rows for brand colour, surfaces, contrast, corners, fonts, icons, density or text size (the theme and its cog dialog hold them), a plain radio list, hand-drawn theme thumbnails or screenshots, a button opening a popover of choices, a SegmentedControl for direction

patterns.name: Settings
patterns.summary: Settings open in a large dialog over the app, the way they do in Notion and Claude. The sidebar lists the sections, the main area shows the one you picked, and on phones it goes full screen. Don't use a small or side dialog, or tabs inside a page.
steps: Entry: a Settings link in the sidebar's AppShellFooter (an icon and "Settings"). On phones, the same link in the More drawer, or a settings icon button in the AppShellBar. Desktop apps also open it on ⌘, (Ctrl+, elsewhere).

Open: a Dialog with <DialogContent size="full" aria-labelledby="<the title's id>"> (class ayy-dialog--full) over the page the user was on, holding an AppShell with settings (class ayy-app-shell--settings). Its AppShellSidebar holds, in order: AppShellTitle ("Settings", with the id the dialog points at) and an AppShellNav aria-label="Settings" of AppShellGroups ("Account": profile, preferences, notifications; "Workspace" or "App": the app's own areas; "About" last). Its main is <AppShellMain as="div"> (the page keeps its one <main>). No AppShellBack, AppShellBar, BottomNav or brand: the dialog's close button is the way out.

Sections: the open section's AppShellLink has current (aria-current="page"); a link click switches the section in place. On wide screens settings open on the first section; on phones on the section list.

Section: the main starts with a TopBar (title = the section's name, its <h1>; onBack returns to the section list, backLabel = "Settings"; its back button shows on phones only), then one Settings group per topic (title, optional description) holding SettingsRows (a Switch, Select, SegmentedControl, Shortcut recorder or Button at the end) and SettingsLinks (rows that open a sub-page or run an action). The content column is --ayy-size-measure wide, centred; the shell does that.

Saving: switches, selects and segmented controls apply at once; confirm with a Toast only when the effect isn't visible. Free text (a name, a folder path) saves on blur or Enter. Anything that must be submitted together (a password change) is a Dialog opened from a SettingsLink.

Appearance: an Appearance section has two controls in every product, each a Select with pictures (one per option, the chosen one before the text, each in the list): Mode (System, Light, Dark; SettingsScreens; setTheme()) and Theme (THEME_PRESETS; SettingsScreen variant="brand" with the theme's accent as --ayy-color-primary; setBrand(), setThemeCustomization() with the active brand colour, and setIconPack()). A theme carries the accent, surfaces, corners, fonts and icons, so they are not separate settings: a cog button beside Theme opens a dialog with them and density, beside a live preview, filled in with the current theme, and saving a change selects Custom, the Theme select's last option. Text direction (Auto, which follows the language, Left to right, Right to left) is a Select with SettingsScreen pictures, dir on the screen and on the app. Reduce motion: a Switch that sets data-motion="reduce". Language: a Select. Reset appearance: a destructive SettingsLink in its own group.
Danger: Sign out, Reset and Delete account go last, in their own Settings group, as destructive SettingsLinks; destructive ones confirm in a Dialog.
Leave: the dialog's close button, Esc or a click on the backdrop. The dialog puts focus back on the Settings link the user came from.
phone: Below 48rem the dialog fills the screen and the settings shell is two screens, picked by aria-current: with no section current, the sidebar is the screen (a large "Settings" title, the sections as rows with chevrons); with one current, the section fills it and its TopBar's back returns to the list. Move focus to the section when it opens and back to its link when it closes.
Settings rows wrap the control under the label when there isn't room; never shrink a control below its size.
For a choice with more than five options on a phone, use a SettingsLink with the current value that opens a sub-page with a radio list, instead of a long Select.
Touch density (data-density="touch") raises sidebar items and rows to 52px; nothing is sized by hand.

specs.Sidebar item (.ayy-app-shell__link, in t: --ayy-size-control-lg high (40px compact, 48px comfortable, 52px touch), padding-inline --ayy-space-3, a --ayy-size-icon-md (20px) icon then --ayy-space-2, --ayy-control-text-lg, medium weight, --ayy-radius-pill. Muted text; hover: --ayy-color-wash and the text colour; current (aria-current="page"): --ayy-color-wash-hover, the text colour, semibold. Items --ayy-space-0-5 apart. Groups: an uppercase --ayy-text-s label, and a hairline with --ayy-space-4 margin and --ayy-space-5 padding above every group after the first.
specs.Settings group (.ayy-settings): A <section> labelled by its <h2> (--ayy-text-md, semibold), an optional muted --ayy-text-sm description, then the rows in a card: a 1px --ayy-color-line border, --ayy-radius-card, --ayy-color-surface. Groups are --ayy-space-6 apart. .ayy-settings--plain (no card) only in a sheet or dialog that already has a surface.
specs.Settings row (.ayy-settings__row): At least --ayy-size-control-lg high, padding --ayy-space-3 block and --ayy-space-4 inline, --ayy-space-4 between the text and the control. Label --ayy-text-sm medium; hint --ayy-text-xs muted, one line. The control sits at the inline end. A 1px --ayy-color-hairline between rows only: none above the first or below the last.
specs.Section header (.ayy-top-bar in the sett: Sticky, the page colour with a hairline under it; title semibold (--ayy-text-xl in the dialog on wide screens, --ayy-text-md on phones), lined up with the content column. One <h1> per section.
specs.Settings dialog (.ayy-dialog--full): Up to 72rem by 50rem, 4rem clear of the viewport on each axis, no padding: the settings shell fills it, the sidebar 15rem. The whole screen below 48rem, without border or radius. The close button sits in the top-end corner over the section's Top bar.

do: Use this pattern for every settings, preferences or account screen in an app, however few settings there are.
Name sections with one noun (General, Appearance, Notifications, Shortcuts, Data, About) and give each a Hugeicons icon in the sidebar.
Keep every setting's label short and put the why in its hint.
Use the Appearance controls above for theme, density, text size, brand colour, corners, font, motion, language and direction, so these settings look and work the same in every product.
dont: Don't put settings in a small or side Dialog, a Popover or Tabs inside a page: they can't hold a growing list of sections, and they end up looking different in every app.
Don't put the app's destinations, bar or bottom nav inside the settings dialog; its close button is the way out.
Don't restyle sidebar items or settings rows (radius, padding, dividers) in app CSS: the specs above are the contract, and they follow density on their own.
Don't add a Save button for settings that apply at once.

patterns.name: Data explorer
patterns.summary: A searchable, filterable, sortable view of records or media, with multi-select and bulk actions. It's built from a page header, a filter bar, a table or card grid with quick actions, and a floating action bar that appears while items are selected. It also covers the loading, empty and error states.
steps: Header: start the screen with a PageHeader (PageHeaderTitle as the one <h1>, PageHeaderDescription, and PageHeaderActions with at most one primary create Button and optional export/view controls).

Controls: place a FilterBar below the header. Its FilterBarMain holds FilterBarTabs (quick status tabs with counts), a FilterBarGroup of faceted FilterBarTriggers (opening DropdownMenus with DropdownMenuSelectedItem checkboxes), a SearchBar to filter by text, and a Sorting trigger (opening a DropdownMenu of sort fields and directions). When faceted filters are active, render FilterBarActive with ChipRemovable pills and a FilterBarClear button.

Records: render a Table (when comparing attributes across columns) or a Grid (when browsing media assets, screenshots, social posts or cards). Include a select-all Checkbox in the header/toolbar and a selection Checkbox on each row (TableCell select) or card (GridItemSelect).

Item actions: put 1–2 common inline icon Buttons (Edit, Copy) and a ⋯ DropdownMenu trigger (Duplicate, Archive, Delete last as destructive) inside TableRowActions (in a trailing TableCell actions) or GridItemActions (with reveal on desktop so actions show on hover, focus-within or selection).

Bulk actions: mount an ActionBar (open={selected.size > 0}) with ActionBarSelection (ActionBarCount + ActionBarClose for Esc/clear) and ActionBarActions of ActionBarButtons (Edit, Duplicate, Copy, Archive, and destructive Delete last).

States & paging: render Skeleton rows or cards with aria-busy="true" while loading, an EmptyState (with a "Clear filters" action when filters match nothing, or a primary create action when the collection is empty), an Alert variant="destructive" with a retry Button when loading fails, and Pagination below the table.
phone: FilterBarMain and FilterBarActive wrap naturally; when a chip strip sits alone on a phone, use ChipGroup scroll so it scrolls horizontally without wrapping into a tall block.
Table scrolls horizontally inside .ayy-table-wrap; Grid drops columns automatically down to a single column below 48rem.
Reveal actions (.ayy-table__row-actions--reveal and .ayy-grid__actions--reveal) stay visible on touch screens (@media (hover: none)) so every item's actions remain tappable without hover.
The floating ActionBar stays anchored at the bottom of the viewport above safe areas; keep its action labels concise.

specs.Filter bar (.ayy-filter-bar): Vertical stack (--ayy-space-2 gap) with --ayy-space-3 padding, 1px --ayy-color-line border, --ayy-radius-card, --ayy-color-surface (or .ayy-filter-bar--flush inside a card). Tabs sit in a wash track; faceted triggers use --ayy-size-control-md height (--ayy-size-control-sm in sm).
specs.Table row & Grid card selection: Selected table rows (tr[aria-selected="true"]) get --ayy-color-wash-hover; selected grid cards (.ayy-grid__item[aria-selected="true"]) get a 2px --ayy-color-text border, 1px ring and 4% text tint.
Inline-flex cluster (--ayy-space-1 gap). With --reveal, opacity is 0 at rest on hover-capable devices and 1 on row/card :hover, :focus-within, [aria-selected="true"], or when a menu trigger inside has [aria-expanded="true"].
specs.Action bar (.ayy-action-bar): Fixed bottom-center pill (--ayy-space-6 from the bottom, z-index 40), --ayy-color-surface-raised, 1px --ayy-color-line-hover border, --ayy-radius-card, --ayy-shadow-lg. Selection count pill at the start, hairline divider, action buttons (--ayy-control-pad-md) with 8px gap.

do: Use this pattern for every table, directory, asset library, inbox list or record manager in an app.
Keep the same actions in the per-item ⋯ DropdownMenu and the bulk ActionBar so single and multi-item workflows match.
Distinguish an empty collection (offer the create button) from an empty filter result (offer "Clear filters").
dont: Don't build custom filter rows out of raw selects or unstyled buttons — use FilterBar, SearchBar and Sorting.
Don't place static bulk action buttons above the table that sit disabled when nothing is selected — use the floating ActionBar.
Don't hide row or card actions with display: none on hover, which removes them from keyboard Tab order and touch screens.

patterns.name: Marketing page
patterns.summary: A public website or landing page: a sticky header, a hero, feature and pricing sections, an FAQ and a footer. Sections are divided by soft separators, and the header folds into a menu on phones.
steps: Top of page: start <body> with an .ayy-skip-link pointing to #main (and an empty .ayy-scroll-progress div for long reads), followed by a Navbar (NavbarBrand, NavbarNav of NavbarLinks with current on the active page, NavbarActions with a theme DropdownMenu and one small ring Button for the primary CTA, and a NavbarToggle last).

Hero: inside <main id="main">, open with a hero section wrapped in .ayy-bg-grid and .ayy-container: a status or announcement Badge, a heading in .ayy-display or .ayy-h1 (with .ayy-gradient-text or .ayy-accent-text on the key phrase), an .ayy-lede intro paragraph (capped at --ayy-size-measure), a cluster with one ring Button and one outline Button, and the product visual inside a Frame.

Sections: separate major blocks with <Separator fade /> inside .ayy-container. Give each section an .ayy-eyebrow label, an .ayy-h2 heading, and an .ayy-lede description before its content grid, and add .ayy-reveal to blocks so they fade and lift in on scroll.

Features & spotlights: lay out features in an .ayy-grid of Cards (interactive and spotlight when clickable, with --ayy-spot set to a distinct --ayy-accent-* token per card) holding an IconTile, CardTitle and CardDescription.

Pricing & FAQ: build pricing with a SegmentedControl (Monthly / Yearly) above an .ayy-grid of plan Cards (the recommended plan gets featured and a Badge; perks use a List compact with check icons). Build the FAQ with an Accordion single centered at --ayy-size-measure.
Footer: close the page with a Footer containing FooterBrand (logo, tagline), FooterNav of FooterGroups (Product, Docs, Company, Legal), and FooterBottom (copyright and secondary links).
phone: Below 48rem the Navbar automatically hides inline links and opens them in a surface panel below the header when NavbarToggle is pressed; NavbarBrand and NavbarActions stay visible in the bar.
.ayy-container switches its inline gutter from 24px to 16px below 64rem, and .ayy-display scales fluidly down to 44px on phones without custom media queries.
Feature and pricing .ayy-grid layouts collapse to a single column automatically when the viewport is narrower than two --ayy-min tracks.

specs.Site header (.ayy-navbar): Sticky top 0, --ayy-size-header (72px) tall, --ayy-color-glass backdrop with 16px blur, 1px --ayy-color-hairline bottom border. Inner row centred at --ayy-size-container (1400px) with 24px gutter (16px below 64rem).
specs.Hero & section typography: Hero title uses .ayy-display (fluid 2.75rem to 12.5rem, tight leading) or .ayy-h1 (3rem). Section titles use .ayy-eyebrow (14px, muted, sentence case) above .ayy-h2 (2.25rem) and .ayy-lede (1.125rem, --ayy-color-text-soft, max-inline-size --ayy-size-measure).
specs.Primary call to action (.ayy-button--rin: Marketing pages use the ring variant for the primary CTA in the hero and repeat it (size sm) in NavbarActions; supporting actions use outline or ghost.
specs.Footer (.ayy-footer): 1px --ayy-color-hairline top border, --ayy-space-12 block padding, inner content at --ayy-size-container width.

do: Use this anatomy for every landing page, marketing site, documentation home or portfolio.
Keep the chrome (Navbar, Footer, page background) monochrome and let colour come from content via --ayy-spot (--ayy-accent-*) on cards, icon tiles and section highlights.
Include a NavbarToggle in every Navbar so phone navigation works without custom CSS.
dont: Don't use a Navbar in a signed-in product or dashboard — use AppShell with BottomNav.
Don't tint the Navbar, Footer or page background per section.
Don't put more than one ring CTA button in the Navbar or hero.

attributes.data-theme: "dark" | "light" | "dark-contrast" | "light-gray" — force a theme on this element and its subtree. None = follow the OS (dark or light). dark-contrast is a pure-black theme (a #000000 page, #0a0a0a cards, white text); light-gray puts white cards and panels on a grey page.
attributes.data-density: "compact" | "comfortable" | "touch" — control sizes for this subtree. None = compact, or touch on touch-first devices.
attributes.data-brand: A brand's name — its colours, corners and fonts for this subtree, in every theme. Needs the brand's stylesheet (@danitesler/ayywi/brands/<name>.css, or brandCss() / `npx @danitesler/ayywi brand` output); setBrand() sets both. None = ayywi's monochrome default.
attributes.data-ayy-icons: An icon pack's id ("lucide" | "tabler" | "material-symbols" | "feather" | "hugeicons") — draws the named icons (the ones ayywi itself uses: close, chevrons, toast and status icons…, and common app icons such as settings or user) in that pack for this subtree; the nearest one wins. Needs that pack's stylesheet (@danitesler/ayywi/icons/<id>.css); "hugeicons" only matters inside another pack's subtree and needs icons/hugeicons.css. setIconPack() sets it and remembers the choice. None = Hugeicons.
attributes.data-ayy-icon: A glyph's name ("x", "chevron-right", "settings"…) on an .ayy-icon <svg> — what an icon pack replaces. ayywi's own components and iconSvg(icon, { name }) / <Icon name="…" /> write it; leave it off for icons that should stay as drawn.
attributes.data-motion: "reduce" — turns ayywi's animations and transitions off for this subtree, as prefers-reduced-motion does; for an app's own Reduce motion setting. None = follow the OS.
attributes.data-ayy-input: "keyboard" | "pointer" on <html>, set by trackInputModality() (started by @danitesler/ayywi/elements; React apps call it once at startup). Pointer hides focus rings, except on text fields, until the next Tab or arrow key; a tooltip then opens on hover only. None = the browser's own :focus-visible.

themes.name: dark
themes.description: The default: near-black background, white text.

themes.name: dark-contrast
themes.description: Pure black dark theme with higher contrast: a #000000 page, #0a0a0a cards with a step up for popovers, white text and crisp highlights. Every text colour still meets WCAG AA.

themes.name: light-gray
themes.description: Light on a grey page: white cards, panels and popovers stand out from a #ebebeb background, and text stays at full strength. More separation between surfaces than the all-white theme; every text colour still meets WCAG AA.

categories.Actions: Things people click to do something.
categories.Navigation: Getting around a site and a page.
categories.Layout: Containers and ways to organise content.
categories.Overlays: Content that floats above the page.

states.default: At rest: nothing hovered, focused or set.
states.hover: The pointer is over it. Touch screens have no hover, so never put information only there.
states.focus: It has keyboard focus (:focus-visible): the 2px --ayy-color-ring outline. With trackInputModality() running, hidden after mouse or touch use until the next Tab or arrow key.
states.disabled: It can't be used: disabled on native controls, aria-disabled="true" on links and on buttons that must keep focus.
states.selected: On, checked, current or chosen: :checked, aria-selected, aria-current, aria-pressed="true", aria-checked.
states.error: Its value is invalid or its action failed: aria-invalid="true" with a FieldError, or a destructive variant.
states.loading: Waiting on work: aria-busy="true" with a Spinner, a Skeleton, or an indeterminate Progress.

publicCustomProperties.--ayy-spot: The content's accent colour, inherited by everything inside (usually an --ayy-accent-* token). Set it on a card or page: it lights card spotlights, the active contents item, icon tiles, the scroll-progress bar and .ayy-accent-text.
publicCustomProperties.--ayy-scrollbar-size: Width of a Scrollbar's gutter (default 0.5rem). The thumb is 4px thinner than the gutter.
publicCustomProperties.--ayy-mx: Card spotlight pointer X in px (set by React Card or @danitesler/ayywi/elements).
publicCustomProperties.--ayy-my: Card spotlight pointer Y in px (set by React Card or @danitesler/ayywi/elements).
publicCustomProperties.--ayy-value: A unitless number 0–100: the Progress bar's or ring's value, a Slider's position, a chart bar's height or tick's position, a ring slice's length, a heatmap cell's shade, a funnel step's or bar-list row's length.
publicCustomProperties.--ayy-start: Where a chart bar starts (a waterfall's floating bar) or a ring slice begins, 0–100 of the scale or the ring (default 0).
publicCustomProperties.--ayy-x: A scatter dot's, chart label's, line hover strip's or ring tooltip's position along the plot, 0–100 from the inline start.
publicCustomProperties.--ayy-count: How many hover strips a line or area chart has (one per label), on its __hits.
publicCustomProperties.--ayy-y: A scatter dot's or chart label's height in the plot, 0–100 from the floor.
publicCustomProperties.--ayy-z: A bubble's size, 0–100 (100 = the largest; pass the share of the square root so areas stay honest).
publicCustomProperties.--ayy-columns: How many columns of cells a heatmap has (default 7).
publicCustomProperties.--ayy-chart-color: Colour of a chart bar, series, slice, legend item, heatmap, funnel, bar list or sparkline, instead of the next --ayy-chart-* token.
publicCustomProperties.--ayy-chart-height: Height of a chart's plot (default 12rem); the width of a donut, pie or gauge (12rem) or a radar (16rem).
publicCustomProperties.--ayy-from: Start of a slider range's fill, 0–100 (kept in sync by React and @danitesler/ayywi/elements).
publicCustomProperties.--ayy-to: End of a slider range's fill, 0–100.
publicCustomProperties.--ayy-sidebar-w: App shell sidebar width (default 15rem), set on the .ayy-app-shell. An __resize handle sets it in px while dragging; start the next session with the saved value.
publicCustomProperties.--ayy-detail-w: App shell detail pane width (default 22rem), set on the .ayy-app-shell. The detail __resize handle sets it in px.
publicCustomProperties.--ayy-check-color: A checkbox's colour, set on the .ayy-checkbox (a token: var(--ayy-accent-brand)…): the border when empty, the fill when checked.
publicCustomProperties.--ayy-check-fg: The tick on a checkbox with --ayy-check-color, when primary-fg doesn't read on that colour.
publicCustomProperties.--ayy-progress-color: Progress bar and ring fill colour override.
publicCustomProperties.--ayy-swatch: A swatch's colour, set on the .ayy-swatch (a token: var(--ayy-chart-1), var(--ayy-accent-brand)…).
publicCustomProperties.--ayy-table-bg: What a table sits on, which its pinned columns and sticky header paint so rows don't show through them. Default the page colour; set it on the table when it sits on another surface (var(--ayy-color-surface) in a card).
publicCustomProperties.--ayy-table-truncate: Widest a table's .ayy-table__truncate text gets before it ends in … (default 16rem).
publicCustomProperties.--ayy-swipe-bg: Background of a swipe row's content, which must hide the action trays under it. Default the page colour; set it to the surface the list sits on (var(--ayy-color-surface) in a card).
publicCustomProperties.--ayy-font-body-adjust: The font-size-adjust of body text (default none). A brand or theme with its own body font sets it to Sora's x-height (BODY_FONT_ADJUST), so that font reads as large as Sora; headings, code and signatures keep their own size.
publicCustomProperties.--ayy-gap: Gap for .ayy-stack / .ayy-cluster / .ayy-grid / .ayy-spread / .ayy-split and the carousel track.
publicCustomProperties.--ayy-min: Narrowest column of .ayy-grid (default 16rem) before it drops a column; the aside width of .ayy-split (default 18rem).
publicCustomProperties.--ayy-ratio: A picture's shape, width ÷ height (1.6, or 1440 / 900), set on a card toast or a view Card's .ayy-card__view-media: the card follows it, within its own minimum and maximum height. Default 16 / 10.
publicCustomProperties.--ayy-slide: Width of each carousel slide (default min(22rem, 85%)).

utilities.ayy-callout: A short note set apart from the text (a tip, caveat or aside): wash background, accent bar on the inline start, 14px.
utilities.ayy-eyebrow: Small muted label above a heading, in the same style as the app shell's group names.
utilities.ayy-display: Hero title: heading font at the fluid display size (44px on a phone to 200px), tight leading.
utilities.ayy-text-outline: Hollow letters stroked in the text colour. For big display words and numbers; combine with .ayy-muted to dim.
utilities.ayy-accent-text: Text in the local accent (--ayy-spot), darkened on light themes so accent tokens keep 4.5:1.
utilities.ayy-gradient-text: Text clipped to a gradient from text colour to accent/soft text.
utilities.ayy-link: Inline text link: underlined, text colour, focus ring.
utilities.ayy-text-highlight: Subtle inline text highlight with clean underline. Mark elements take this by default.
utilities.ayy-code: Inline code: monospace at 0.85em, hairline border, wash background and tight padding. For token names, file paths and shortcuts in running text.
utilities.ayy-prose: Long-form reading (articles, case studies): 18px soft text at a readable measure; styles the headings, lists, links, quotes, code and images inside.
utilities.ayy-container: Centred page width (--ayy-size-container, 1400px) with a 24px gutter, 16px on tablets and phones.
utilities.ayy-grid: Responsive grid: as many columns of at least --ayy-min (16rem) as fit; gap via --ayy-gap (16px).
utilities.ayy-stack:
Vertical flex stack; gap via --ayy-gap (default 12px). Children lose their block margins (true of every layout helper), so a

or heading inside needs no margin reset.
utilities.ayy-spread: Wrapping row with its items pushed to both ends: a title and its meta, a label and a value, a toolbar's filters and actions. Gap via --ayy-gap (default 8px).
utilities.ayy-split: Main content (first child) and an aside (last child) side by side; the aside drops below once the main would be narrower than 60%. Aside width via --ayy-min (default 18rem). No media query, so it adapts to the box it's in.
utilities.ayy-center: Centered layout container aligning items horizontally and vertically.
utilities.ayy-bleed: Bleeds out into container gutter by negative gap margin.
utilities.ayy-surface: Surface background container with default text color.
utilities.ayy-glow: Glow box shadow on featured cards or elements.
utilities.ayy-sr-only: Visually hidden, still read by screen readers.
utilities.ayy-truncate: One line, cut with an ellipsis (also inside a flex row).
utilities.ayy-clamp-2: Multi-line text clamp to 2 lines with ellipsis.
utilities.ayy-clamp-3: Multi-line text clamp to 3 lines with ellipsis.
utilities.ayy-scroll: Thin, quiet scrollbars on a scroll container.
utilities.ayy-skip-link: "Skip to content" link: hidden above the viewport until it gets keyboard focus. Make it the first thing in <body>.
utilities.ayy-bg-grid: Decorative ambient grid behind a hero or closing section, fading out towards the edges. Sets position: relative.
utilities.ayy-scroll-progress: Reading-progress bar fixed to the top of the viewport, in --ayy-spot. Put an empty aria-hidden <div> with it at the start of <body>. CSS scroll timelines only; hidden where unsupported.
utilities.ayy-reveal: Fades and lifts the element in as it scrolls into view. CSS only; off under reduced motion.

components.name: Button
components.description: The control for starting an action, like saving, submitting or opening something. It comes in a few weights, from a strong primary button to quieter ones for secondary actions.

classes.ayy-button: Root. Alone it is the primary button.
classes.ayy-button--secondary: Quiet filled button for secondary actions.
classes.ayy-button--outline: Bordered, transparent. Neutral alternative to secondary.
classes.ayy-button--ghost: No border or fill until hover. Toolbars, icon buttons.
classes.ayy-button--ring: Showcase call to action: quiet fill inside a gradient ring that spins on keyboard focus and mouse hover (not after a tap). For marketing and portfolio pages; one per view.
classes.ayy-button--sm: Small control step: --ayy-size-control-sm tall (28px compact, 32 comfortable, 40 touch), --ayy-control-text-sm, --ayy-size-icon-sm (16px) icon, 6px gap.
classes.ayy-button--lg: Large control step: --ayy-size-control-lg tall (40px compact, 48 comfortable, 52 touch), --ayy-control-text-lg, --ayy-size-icon-md (20px) icon, 8px gap. Matches large App shell links.
classes.ayy-button--icon: Square at the md control height (32px compact, 40 comfortable, 44 touch), for a single 16px icon.
classes.ayy-button--icon-sm: Square at the sm control height (28px compact, 32 comfortable, 40 touch), for a single 16px icon.
classes.ayy-button--icon-lg: Square at the lg control height (40px compact, 48 comfortable, 52 touch), for a single 20px icon beside a large button.
classes.ayy-button--block: Fills its container's width: a card footer, a phone form, a dialog's only action.
classes.ayy-button--start: Icon and label sit at the inline start of a wide button, laid out like an App shell row of the same size: the icon is centred in a square as wide as the button is high, so a sm, md or lg button lines up with a sm, md or lg menu item. Use with block.
classes.ayy-button--end: Icon and label sit at the inline end of a wide button, with the same edge spacing as --start (mirrored). Use with block. Centered is the default, no class.
classes.ayy-button-split: Group joining a main action .ayy-button and a trailing icon .ayy-button (opening a menu) into a single split button with a shared seam.
classes.ayy-button-split--block: Full-width split button: the main action stretches and the menu trigger stays square.

default.looks: Primary: --ayy-color-primary fill, --ayy-color-primary-fg label, semibold. Secondary: wash fill and line border. Outline: transparent with a line-strong border. Ghost: transparent, no border. Destructive: 10% red tint, red label. Link: plain text. Ring: wash inside a gradient ring.

hover.looks: Lifts 2px. Primary adds the glow shadow at 90% opacity; secondary, outline, ghost and ring move to wash-hover, wash or highlight with a stronger border; destructive deepens to a 15% tint. Link underlines instead of lifting; ring's border spins.

pressed.looks: Drops back to its resting position while held; colours stay as on hover.

focus.looks: 2px --ayy-color-ring outline, 2px offset. Ring also spins its border.

disabled.looks: --ayy-opacity-disabled, ignores the pointer. Forced colours: GrayText border and label.

selected.none: Not a toggle. For on/off use a Chip button (aria-pressed), for one of a few a Segmented control, for a setting a Switch.

error.none: Errors belong to the form: a FieldError under the field, or an Alert for a failed action.

loading.when: aria-busy="true" with an aria-hidden .ayy-spinner as the first child (React: loading)
loading.looks: Spinner before the label; clicks and form submits are ignored; stays focusable. Keep the label (or "Saving…") so the width barely moves.

scale.sm: Control sm step: --ayy-size-control-sm tall (28px compact, 32 comfortable, 40 touch), --ayy-control-pad-sm inline padding, --ayy-control-text-sm (13/13/14px), --ayy-size-icon-sm (16px) icon, 6px gap.
scale.md: Control md step: --ayy-size-control-md tall (32px compact, 40 comfortable, 44 touch), --ayy-control-pad-md inline padding, --ayy-control-text-md (13/13/14px), --ayy-size-icon-sm (16px) icon, 8px gap.
scale.lg: Control lg step: --ayy-size-control-lg tall (40px compact, 48 comfortable, 52 touch), --ayy-control-pad-lg inline padding, --ayy-control-text-lg (14/15/16px), --ayy-size-icon-md (20px) icon, 8px gap. Matches lg App shell links.
scale.icon: Square at the md control height (32/40/44px) with a 16px icon (needs aria-label).
scale.icon-sm: Square at the sm control height (28/32/40px) with a 16px icon.
scale.icon-lg: Square at the lg control height (36/44/48px) with a 20px icon.

sizes.density: Height, inline padding and label size follow data-density across all steps (sm/md/lg); icons stay fixed at 16px (sm/md) and 20px (lg).
sizes.width: Hugs its label. block (ayy-button--block) fills its container: a phone form, a card footer, a dialog's only action.

components.js: buttonClass({ variant?, size?, block?, align?, className? }) → string; splitButtonClass({ block?, className? }) → string. Loading in HTML: aria-busy="true" plus as the first child.

props.align: "start" | "center" | "end" — where the icon and label sit in a wide button; center is the default.
props.loading: boolean — a Spinner before the label and aria-busy="true"; clicks and form submits are ignored while it's set. Stays focusable.
props.tooltip: ReactNode | boolean — custom tooltip text or element; icon-only buttons show their aria-label on hover by default (pass false to disable).

props.block: boolean — full width (ayy-button-split--block); the main action grows, the menu trigger stays square.

a11y: Icon-only buttons need aria-label and should always have a visible Tooltip on hover/focus.
In a SplitButton, give the trailing menu trigger an explicit aria-label naming what it opens ("More deploy options").
Use disabled on <button>; on <a> use aria-disabled="true" (the class handles both).
Visible focus ring on :focus-visible is built in — never remove it.
While it works, set aria-busy="true" and put an aria-hidden .ayy-spinner first inside (React: loading). Don't disable it: focus would jump away.
do: Use a button for any action the user can take: submit, open, save, delete.
Use a SplitButton when a primary action has closely related alternatives in a DropdownMenu ("Deploy" + "Deploy to preview").
Apply buttonClass() to an <a> when a link should look like an action.
Always pair icon-only buttons (size="icon*", without a text label) with a Tooltip so sighted mouse and keyboard users can identify the action.
Keep one primary button per view or section; make everything else secondary, outline or ghost.
On a marketing or portfolio page, the one call to action can be ring instead of primary, with an outline button beside it.
Put the icon (<Icon> or an .ayy-icon <svg>) before the label; the button sizes it (16px on sm/md, 20px on lg).
dont: Don't use a button for navigation inside running text — use a plain link.
Don't use a button to toggle a setting on/off — use Switch.
Don't restyle colours per button — add a variant to the design system instead.
Don't use destructive for non-destructive emphasis.

components.name: Hover actions
components.description: Small buttons that appear over a picture, a video or a card when someone points at it, for quick actions like copy, annotate or pin. They stay out of the way until needed, and a tooltip names each one.

classes.ayy-hover-actions: Row of hover actions. In the normal flow unless a position modifier floats it in a corner of the positioned parent.
classes.ayy-hover-actions--top-start: Floats in the top start corner of the positioned parent.
classes.ayy-hover-actions--top-end: Floats in the top end corner.
classes.ayy-hover-actions--bottom-start: Floats in the bottom start corner.
classes.ayy-hover-actions--bottom-end: Floats in the bottom end corner.
classes.ayy-hover-actions--group: One glass bar (blurred, hairline border, pill corners) holds the buttons, which drop their own backgrounds.
classes.ayy-hover-actions--reveal: Hidden until the element it sits directly in is hovered, has focus inside, carries data-hover or holds an open menu. Always shown on touch screens.
classes.ayy-hover-action: Icon button at the small control size, frosted so it reads over a picture. Put an icon inside and an aria-label on it.

default.looks: Each button is a frosted square (surface at 55% over a 10px blur) with a 16px icon in the text colour. Grouped, the bar is frosted instead and the buttons are clear.

hover.looks: The frosting thickens to 85% surface; in a group the button gets the wash-hover fill.

focus.looks: 2px --ayy-color-ring outline, 2px offset. Focus inside also reveals a --reveal row.

disabled.looks: 45% opacity and a not-allowed cursor.

selected.none: Hover actions run something once; they have no on state. Use a Toolbar toggle (aria-pressed) for one that stays on.

error.none: Report a failed action in a toast or the card's status, not on the button.

loading.none: Show progress where the result appears (a card toast status, a Spinner); keep the button as it is.

revealed.when: .ayy-hover-actions--reveal inside a parent that is :hover, :focus-within, [data-hover] or :has([aria-expanded="true"])
revealed.looks: Fades in and settles from 4px above (below for bottom corners). Hidden rows ignore the pointer.

sizes.density: Buttons are --ayy-size-control-sm square: 28px compact, 32px comfortable, 40px touch. Icons stay 16px.
sizes.width: As wide as its buttons. Positioned rows sit 8px in from the corner of their parent.

components.js: hoverActionsClass({ position?, group?, reveal?, className? }) → string; hoverActionClass({ className? }) → string

props.group: boolean — one glass bar for all the buttons
props.reveal: boolean — hidden until the parent is hovered or focused

props.label: string (required) — accessible name and tooltip text
props.hint: ReactNode — after the label in the tooltip, e.g. <Shortcut keys="Mod+C" />
props.tooltip: boolean — false drops the tooltip (the label stays the accessible name). Default true

a11y: Every button needs an aria-label (React's label sets it); the icon is decorative.
Revealed rows are still in the tab order: focusing a button shows the row, so keyboard users reach every action.
Touch screens have no hover, so --reveal rows always show there; never hide the only way to do something behind hover.
do: Use hover actions for the few icon actions on a picture, a video frame or a media card: Copy, Annotate, Pin, Trim, and a ⋯ menu for the rest.
Group them on one bar (group) when there are three or more in one corner; keep them separate when each corner holds one or two.
Put a --reveal row directly inside the element whose hover should show it (the card, the picture's box).
End a group with a ⋯ DropdownMenu for anything that doesn't earn its own button.
dont: Don't use hover actions for a page's or a toolbar's buttons — use Button, or a Toolbar for a row of tools.
Don't put text buttons in a hover-actions row; they're icon-only. A card toast's centre buttons (Copy, Save) are regular Buttons.
Don't use title="" for their names; the label is the tooltip.
Don't put more than five in one corner — move the rest into the ⋯ menu.

components.name: Toolbar
components.description: A row or column of tools for one surface, like an editor, a canvas or a text selection. It's a single tab stop with arrow keys between the tools, and can be fixed, floating or vertical.

classes.ayy-toolbar: Root, role="toolbar" with an aria-label ("Annotate"). A row of items with a small gap.
classes.ayy-toolbar--vertical: A column (a side rail). Add aria-orientation="vertical" so the up and down arrows move.
classes.ayy-toolbar--floating: A raised pill with a border and a shadow, floating over a canvas, a photo or a text selection.
classes.ayy-toolbar--scroll: One line that scrolls sideways when the tools don't fit (phones).
classes.ayy-toolbar--sm: Smaller buttons and icons (--ayy-size-control-sm), for a floating bar over text.
classes.ayy-toolbar__group: Tools that belong together: role="group", with an aria-label when it has a name. With data-exclusive, <ayy-toolbar> keeps one of its aria-pressed buttons on (the current tool).
classes.ayy-toolbar__separator: A hairline between groups: role="separator". Horizontal in a vertical toolbar.
classes.ayy-toolbar__spacer: Takes the free space, pushing what follows to the far end (actions after tools). aria-hidden.
classes.ayy-toolbar__button: A tool: <button type="button">. Square with only an icon (then it needs an aria-label), wider with an icon and a short label. Height follows data-density. aria-pressed for a tool that stays on, aria-expanded while its menu is open.

default.looks: A row of square icon buttons in the soft text colour, split into groups by separators; floating puts them on a raised pill with the overlay shadow.

hover.looks: Wash-hover background, full text colour.

pressed.none: No pressed look; a tool that stays on is selected (aria-pressed).

focus.looks: 2px ring, 1px offset. The toolbar is one Tab stop; arrow keys move between buttons.

disabled.looks: --ayy-opacity-disabled, not-allowed cursor; the arrow keys skip it (Redo with nothing to redo).

selected.looks: The current tool or an applied format: a wash tile with a line-strong hairline and the full text colour. Forced colours: Highlight fill.

error.none: Tools don't fail visibly; say so in a toast if an action can't run.

loading.none: Tools act at once. A long export shows a Spinner in its own dialog or a toast.

open.looks: Its menu or popover is open: drawn like selected.

scale.sm: Buttons at the sm control height (28px compact, 32 comfortable, 40 touch), 16px icons.
scale.md: Buttons at the md control height (32px compact, 40 comfortable, 44 touch), 20px icons.

sizes.density: Button size follows data-density (above).
sizes.width: Hugs its buttons. vertical makes a column; scroll keeps one line that scrolls sideways on phones; a spacer pushes later items to the far end.

components.js: toolbarClass({ vertical?, floating?, scroll?, size?, className? }) → string; toolbarButtonClass, toolbarGroupClass, toolbarSeparatorClass, toolbarSpacerClass constants; connectToolbar(el) → { refresh, destroy } wires the keyboard pattern on plain markup.

element.description: Wraps an .ayy-toolbar and wires the keyboard pattern (one Tab stop, arrow keys, Home/End). Clicking a button with aria-pressed toggles it; inside a data-exclusive group it becomes the only pressed one.

events.ayy-press: { button, pressed } before a button's aria-pressed changes; preventDefault() keeps the old state.

react.import: import { Toolbar, ToolbarButton, ToolbarGroup, ToolbarSeparator, ToolbarSpacer } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";

props.floating: boolean — a raised pill with a shadow
props.scroll: boolean — one line that scrolls sideways

props.pressed: boolean — aria-pressed, for tools that stay on; omit for one-off actions
props.tooltip: ReactNode | boolean — custom tooltip text or element; buttons with aria-label show their tooltip on hover by default

a11y: role="toolbar" with an aria-label. Tab reaches it once (the last tool used, else the pressed one, else the first); Left/Right (Up/Down when vertical) move between tools, mirrored in RTL; Home/End jump to the ends. Disabled tools are skipped.
Every icon-only tool needs an aria-label ("Rectangle"), and the name shouldn't change with its state — aria-pressed says whether it's on.
Text fields and radio groups (swatches, a segmented control) inside keep their own arrow keys; the radio group is one stop.
On is a wash tile with a hairline, not colour alone; High Contrast fills it with the system highlight.
do: Use a toolbar for the tools of one surface: an image or canvas editor, a text selection, a media viewer, a table's bulk actions.
Put the tools that switch modes in a group where one is pressed (the current tool), then separators, then one-off actions (Undo, Redo), then a ToolbarSpacer and the labelled actions (Copy, Save).
Use vertical for a side rail on wide screens and scroll on phones; floating over a canvas or next to a selection.

Use PopoverTrigger asChild around an icon-only ToolbarButton with aria-label to open a subtoolbar; its label also supplies the tooltip. Give the popup Toolbar its own aria-label and use side=end beside a vertical rail.
Put a Swatch group (size sm, track) in it for colours, and a DropdownMenu trigger (a ToolbarButton) for overflow.
Wrap toolbar items in a Tooltip with a keyboard hint element (<Shortcut keys="..." /> in React, .ayy-shortcut in HTML) to show their action and shortcut on hover and focus.
dont: Don't use a toolbar for page navigation — use Tabs, the App shell or a Bottom nav — or for a page's one or two actions — use Buttons in a Page header.
Don't wrap a toolbar onto several lines; scroll it, or move rare tools into a menu.
Don't make every tool icon-only when there's room: the main action reads better with a label ("Copy").
Don't use native title="" tooltips on toolbar buttons — use Tooltip with a keyboard hint element (<Shortcut keys="..." /> / .ayy-shortcut) instead.
