components.name: Action bar
components.description: A bar that appears at the bottom of the screen once someone selects rows or cards in a table, grid or list. It shows how many are selected and offers actions that apply to all of them, such as archive or delete. It goes away when the selection is cleared.

classes.ayy-action-bar: Root floating pill bar, role="toolbar". Hidden until the open attribute is present, then animates in with a spring lift, and plays the same animation in reverse on exit.
classes.ayy-action-bar--fixed: Pins the bar to the bottom center of the viewport instead of sticky inside its scroll container.
classes.ayy-action-bar__selection: Start section grouping the selected count and the clear selection button.
classes.ayy-action-bar__count: Tabular-numeral count of selected items (e.g. "3 selected").
classes.ayy-action-bar__close: Icon button (×) that clears the current selection (also triggered by Escape).
classes.ayy-action-bar__separator: Vertical hairline divider between the selection count and actions, or before destructive actions.
classes.ayy-action-bar__actions: Scrollable group of bulk action buttons (role="group").
classes.ayy-action-bar__button: Compact action button inside the bar, with an optional leading icon and label.
classes.ayy-action-bar__button--primary: Primary bulk action button filled with the primary token.
classes.ayy-action-bar__button--secondary: Secondary bulk action button with a wash fill and subtle border.
classes.ayy-action-bar__button--destructive: Destructive bulk action button (e.g. Delete) in the destructive colour.
classes.ayy-action-bar__button--icon: Square icon-only action button for common bulk actions (e.g. Copy, Archive, Delete).

default.looks: Hidden until [open] is set; when open, a blurred glass pill with a line-strong border, overlay shadow, semibold count, clear button and standard action buttons.

hover.looks: Buttons tint with a wash fill; primary dims; destructive gets a 18% tint and border; close button turns text colour.

focus.looks: 2px ring, 2px offset. The bar is one Tab stop; Left/Right arrows move between buttons.

disabled.looks: --ayy-opacity-disabled, not-allowed cursor; arrow keys skip it.

selected.none: Bulk actions execute on click; use open for a button whose overflow menu is open.

error.none: Use variant="destructive" (.ayy-action-bar__button--destructive) for Delete; report a failed bulk action with a toast.

loading.none: Bulk actions act immediately or report progress in a toast.

open.looks: The bar smoothly lifts and fades in with spring easing, and plays the same animation in reverse on close; a menu trigger button keeps the wash-hover fill and line-strong border.

sizes.density: Buttons and the clear control follow --ayy-size-control-sm (28px compact, 32px comfortable, 40px touch) and --ayy-control-text-sm.
sizes.width: Hugs its buttons (fit-content) up to 100% of its container (or viewport when fixed), scrolling sideways if actions overflow on a phone.

components.js: actionBarClass({ fixed?, className? }) → string; actionBarButtonClass({ variant?, primary?, secondary?, destructive?, icon?, className? }) → string; actionBarSelectionClass, actionBarCountClass, actionBarCloseClass, actionBarSeparatorClass, actionBarActionsClass constants; connectActionBar(bar, { onClear? }) → { refresh, syncCount, destroy } wires keyboard navigation, Escape/close clearing, and count updates.

element.description: Wraps an .ayy-action-bar and wires toolbar keyboard navigation (one Tab stop, Left/Right arrows, Home/End), Escape and close button selection clearing, and automatic count syncing when a sibling <ayy-table> or <ayy-grid> fires ayy-selection-change.

events.ayy-clear: Fired when the clear button or Escape clears the selection; call preventDefault() to keep it.

react.import: import { ActionBar, ActionBarSelection, ActionBarCount, ActionBarClose, ActionBarSeparator, ActionBarActions, ActionBarButton } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";

props.open: boolean — shows the bar with its entrance animation when true
props.fixed: boolean — pins to the bottom center of the viewport
props.label: string — aria-label for the toolbar (default "Bulk actions")
props.onClear: () => void — called when the clear button or Escape is pressed

props.label: string — accessible label for the clear button (default "Clear selection")
props.tooltip: ReactNode | boolean — custom tooltip text or element (defaults to label)

props.icon: boolean — square icon-only button without label padding (must provide aria-label)
props.open: boolean — aria-expanded when used as a DropdownMenuTrigger
props.tooltip: ReactNode | boolean — custom tooltip text or element; icon buttons show their aria-label on hover by default

a11y: role="toolbar" with an aria-label ("Bulk actions"): one Tab stop, Left/Right arrow keys (mirrored in RTL) and Home/End move between the clear button and actions.
Pressing Escape or clicking ActionBarClose clears the selection and dismisses the bar.
Icon-only buttons inside the bar must have an aria-label (e.g. aria-label="Delete selected") and always be wrapped in a Tooltip.
High Contrast mode borders the bar in CanvasText and highlights primary or open buttons with Highlight.
do: Use an Action bar with a selectable Table or Grid so bulk actions appear at the bottom as soon as one or more items are selected.
Show the selected count first, followed by the clear button, a separator, and the actions with destructive Delete last.

When an Action bar has many actions, keep text labels for unique or context-specific actions (e.g. "Assign reviewer", "Change status") and use icon-only buttons (`icon`, `aria-label`) for universally recognized bulk actions (Duplicate, Copy link, Archive, Delete).
Place an ActionBarSeparator between labelled buttons and icon buttons to visually divide distinct action groups.
Always pair icon-only action buttons with a Tooltip so users can identify the action on hover and keyboard focus.
Fold less common bulk actions into a DropdownMenu triggered from a trailing ActionBarButton.
dont: Don't leave an Action bar visible with 0 selected items — hide it by omitting open (open={selected.length > 0}) instead of disabling every button.
Don't use an Action bar for permanent page actions or navigation — use PageHeader actions, Toolbar or BottomNav.
Don't cram more than five labelled actions into the bar without switching common actions to icon-only buttons or moving extras into a ⋯ DropdownMenu.

components.name: Dropdown menu
components.description: A list of actions that opens from a button. It supports submenus and works fully from the keyboard.

classes.ayy-menu: On the element with popover and role="menu".
classes.ayy-menu--static: Static menu rendered inline in a page or window without popover behavior.
classes.ayy-menu__row: Split row: a wrapper holding a normal item and a __more button side by side, so the item runs its action and the button opens a menu for it.
classes.ayy-menu__more: Square icon button at the end of a __row that opens the row's menu (role="menuitem", aria-haspopup="menu"; put its panel next to the row).
classes.ayy-menu__item--selected: Selectable menu item with checkmark indicator.
classes.ayy-menu__item--sub: Submenu parent row with an inline-end chevron.
classes.ayy-menu__item--expand: Inline accordion row that expands its items below itself.
classes.ayy-menu__item--described: Two-line row with an aligned label and soft description.
classes.ayy-menu__item-text: Text container for a described row's label and description.
classes.ayy-menu__description: Soft description text under a described row's label.
classes.ayy-menu__value: Muted text or badge before the chevron or shortcut.
classes.ayy-menu__chevron: Chevron icon pointing towards the inline end or down when expandable.
classes.ayy-menu__group--inline: Indented role="group" of items revealed by an expandable row.
classes.ayy-menu__shortcut: Keyboard shortcut keys at the end of an item, as keycaps (an .ayy-shortcut of .ayy-kbd, adapted to the device).
classes.ayy-menu__label: Small muted group label, in the same style as the app shell's group names.

default.looks: Raised surface panel with a line-strong border and the overlay shadow; items are transparent rows with muted icons.

hover.looks: Item, or a split row's trailing button, gets the wash-hover background; the button's icon goes from muted to text colour.

pressed.none: Items have no pressed look: activating one runs it and closes the menu.

focus.looks: Focused item gets the wash-hover background; keyboard focus adds a 2px ring inset by 2px. Forced colours: Highlight fill.

disabled.looks: Item dims to --ayy-opacity-disabled with a not-allowed cursor; arrow keys skip it.

selected.looks: Semibold with a check at the inline start, drawn in currentColor with space reserved so trailing values stay aligned. For view options in a menu (density, sort, show/hide columns); to choose a form value, use Select.

error.none: A menu has no error state; report a failed command with a toast.

loading.none: Build the items before opening; if they load, put the trigger Button in loading until they're ready.

open.when: :popover-open or [aria-expanded="true"] on a parent row or split row's __more
open.looks: Fades in and scales up from 97%; parent rows and a split row's trailing button keep the hover background while their menu is open.

sizes.density: Items are the md control height (32px compact, 40 comfortable, 44 touch) with control md text.
sizes.width: At least 11rem, at most 20rem (or the viewport minus 1rem); grows with its longest item.

props.selected: boolean — reserves space on inline start for checkmark indicator
props.shortcut: string — shortcut keys like "Mod+D" (shown as keycaps, ⌘D on a Mac, Ctrl+D elsewhere)

props.selected: boolean — reserves space on inline start for checkmark indicator

DropdownMenuSubContent.renders: <div popover role="menu">, <div popover role="dialog"> (placed after the DropdownMenuContent) or <div role="group"> (inline)

a11y: Opening moves focus to the first item; arrows move, Home/End jump, letters jump to matching items.
ArrowRight / ArrowLeft open and close submenus (mirrored in RTL); Esc inside a submenu closes only that panel.
Esc or Tab closes the menu and focus returns to the trigger.

A submenu panel holding more than items (an Icon picker) is role="dialog" and sits outside the menu, which may only hold items: in HTML right after it, named by its row's aria-controls; in React, the DropdownMenuSub wraps the DropdownMenuContent and the DropdownMenuSubContent follows it.
Icon-only triggers (⋯) need aria-label.
A split row is two menu items: the action and its trailing More button, which arrows reach like any other item. Label the button with its row ("More options for Duplicate project"), not just "More".
do: Use a menu for an item's secondary actions (rename, duplicate, delete) and for overflow “⋯” menus in toolbars and table rows.
Show an item's shortcut with shortcut="Mod+…" so Mac and Windows users each see their own keys as keycaps.
Nest one level at most, for variants of one action. Don't hide frequent actions in a submenu.

Use a split row (DropdownMenuRow with DropdownMenuMore) when one item has a second, related set of choices: the row runs the action, its ⋯ opens on click (not hover) with variants like "Duplicate as template".
Put destructive actions last, after a separator.
Keep item labels to a verb + noun: "Rename project".
dont: Don't use a menu to choose a value in a form — use Select or Radio.
Don't use a menu to navigate between pages — use links.
Don't put form fields or rich content in a menu — use Popover.
Don't hard-code "⌘" or "Ctrl" in a shortcut — pass "Mod+…" and let it adapt.
Don't nest submenus more than one level.

import { useState } from "react";

          </DropdownMenuSubContent>
        </DropdownMenuSub>

        <DropdownMenuSub>
          <DropdownMenuRow>
            <DropdownMenuItem icon={<Icon icon={Share08Icon} name="share-2" />} value={<Badge variant="muted">3</Badge>} shortcut="Mod+S" onSelect={() => toast("Share settings")}>
              Share
            </DropdownMenuItem>
            <DropdownMenuMore aria-label="More options for Share" icon={<Icon icon={MoreHorizontalIcon} name="ellipsis" />} />
          </DropdownMenuRow>
          <DropdownMenuSubContent>
            <DropdownMenuItem icon={<Icon icon={Link01Icon} name="link" />} onSelect={() => toast("Link copied")} shortcut="Mod+C">
              Copy link
            </DropdownMenuItem>
            <DropdownMenuItem icon={<Icon icon={Mail01Icon} name="mail" />} onSelect={() => toast("Invite sent")}>
              Invite by email
            </DropdownMenuItem>
          </DropdownMenuSubContent>
        </DropdownMenuSub>

        <DropdownMenuItem disabled>
          <Icon icon={UserSwitchIcon} name="user-switch" />
          Transfer ownership
        </DropdownMenuItem>
        <DropdownMenuItem
          icon={<Icon icon={CropIcon} name="crop" />}
          description="Drag to select part of the screen"
          onSelect={() => toast("Capture area")}
          shortcut="Mod+4"
        >
          Capture area

        <DropdownMenuSub>
          <DropdownMenuSubTrigger
            icon={<Icon icon={Clock01Icon} name="clock" />}
            value={timer === "off" ? "Off" : `${timer}s`}

          <DropdownMenuSubContent>

              <DropdownMenuRadioItem value="5">In 5 seconds</DropdownMenuRadioItem>
              <DropdownMenuRadioItem value="10">In 10 seconds</DropdownMenuRadioItem>

        </DropdownMenuSub>

              <DropdownMenuRadioItem value="jpg">JPG (compressed)</DropdownMenuRadioItem>

components.name: Command palette
components.description: A search box above a list of actions and places, so people can find and run things from the keyboard. It can sit inline on a page or in a popover, or open as a dialog from a shortcut.

classes.ayy-command: Root: a card with the search field, the list and an optional footer. On a <div> inline, or with ayy-dialog on a <dialog> for the ⌘K palette (top-aligned, no padding).
classes.ayy-command__search: The row with the magnifier icon and the input, over a hairline. A ring under it while the input has keyboard focus.
classes.ayy-command__input: <input type="search" role="combobox" aria-expanded="true" aria-controls="<list id>" aria-autocomplete="list" aria-label>. Keeps focus; aria-activedescendant points at the highlighted item.
classes.ayy-command__list: role="listbox" with an id and aria-label; scrolls when long.
classes.ayy-command__group: role="group" aria-labelledby its label. Hidden when none of its items match.
classes.ayy-command__label: A group's name ("Go to"), muted, role="presentation" with an id.
classes.ayy-command__item: role="option" with an id: an icon, the text, then a __meta. aria-selected="true" on the highlighted one; data-value is what it runs, data-keywords more words that find it.
classes.ayy-command__content: Vertical stack for an item's title and optional description.
classes.ayy-command__title: The primary label of an item.
classes.ayy-command__description: One-line muted summary under the title, truncated with ellipsis.
classes.ayy-command__meta: At an item's end: a .ayy-shortcut, a list name or a count, muted.
classes.ayy-command__empty: "No results", shown only when nothing matches (hidden otherwise).
classes.ayy-command__footer: Under the list after a hairline: key hints (↑↓ to move, ↵ to run) or a link.

default.looks: A raised card: a search field with a magnifier over a hairline, then labelled groups of items with an icon, a label and muted meta at the end.

hover.none: Items have no separate hover look: moving the pointer over an item selects it (see selected), so the pointer and the arrow keys never show two items at once.

pressed.none: No pressed look: clicking or Enter runs the item and usually closes the palette.

focus.looks: A 2px ring under the field. Focus stays in the input while the arrow keys move the selection. Forced colours: Highlight outline.

disabled.looks: Dimmed to --ayy-opacity-disabled with a not-allowed cursor; the arrow keys skip it.

selected.looks: The item under the arrow keys or the pointer gets the wash-hover background and a full-colour icon. Forced colours: Highlight fill.

error.none: Nothing to validate. If running an item fails, close the palette and say so in a toast.

loading.none: No loading look. While results load, show .ayy-command__empty with "Searching…".

empty.looks: A muted, centred "No results" line when the filter hides every item.

filtered.looks: Items that don't match the typed text are hidden, and so is a group with none left.

sizes.density: Items are the md control height (32px compact, 40 comfortable, 44 touch); the field is the lg height.
sizes.width: Inline it fills its container. As a dialog (ayy-dialog ayy-command) it's 36rem wide, at most the viewport less 2rem, near the top of the screen; the list scrolls past 24rem.

components.js: connectCommand(root, { onSelect?, filter?, reorder? }) → { refresh(activateFirst?), reset, destroy } wires filtering, the arrows, Enter and the pointer on plain markup; Enter clicks the highlighted item. Better matches move up (reorder: false when a framework owns the items; React Command ranks its children itself). commandMatches(text, query) is the matching rule (every typed word starts a word, or one word anywhere); commandItemText(item); commandItemDetails(item); commandScore(title, description, keywords, query). commandClass, commandInputClass, commandListClass, commandItemClass, commandSearchIcon (SVG markup).

element.description: Wraps an .ayy-command (a div, or a <dialog class="ayy-dialog ayy-command"> plus the buttons that open it, marked [data-ayy-open]) and wires it. A dialog palette opens with the shortcut, closes after an item runs, on Esc (the first Esc clears the field) or on the backdrop, and is empty each time it opens. Methods: show(), refresh().

attributes.shortcut: Opens and closes the dialog palette from anywhere. Default "Mod+K" (⌘K, Ctrl+K); "" for none.
attributes.manual: Don't filter: you change the items yourself on "input" (a search API), then call refresh().

events.ayy-select: { value, item } when an item runs: its data-value and the element.

react.import: import { Command, CommandDialog, CommandGroup, CommandItem } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";

props.label: string — the field's and list's accessible name. Default "Search commands"
props.placeholder: string — default "Type a command or search…"
props.emptyText: ReactNode — when nothing matches. Default "No results"
props.footer: ReactNode — key hints under the list
props.filter: boolean — filter by the typed text. Default true
props.onSearchChange: (text: string) => void — every keystroke (fetch results here with filter={false})
props.onRun: (value?: string) => void — after an item runs, with its value

CommandDialog.renders: <dialog class="ayy-dialog ayy-command" aria-label> with the same parts; closes when an item runs

props.shortcut: string | null — toggles it from anywhere. Default "Mod+K"

CommandItem.renders: <div class="ayy-command__item" role="option" data-value data-keywords data-title data-description>

props.onSelect: () => void — runs on Enter or a click
props.keywords: string — more words that find it
props.description: ReactNode — optional one-line summary under the title
props.icon: ReactNode — an Icon before the text
props.shortcut: string — its shortcut at the end ("Mod+N")
props.meta: ReactNode — other text at the end: a count, a list name
props.disabled: boolean — dimmed, skipped by the arrows

a11y: The WAI-ARIA combobox pattern with a listbox that is always shown: focus stays in the input, aria-activedescendant names the highlighted item, and the first match is highlighted as you type.
Up/Down move (wrapping), PageUp/PageDown move five, Enter runs the highlighted item, Esc clears the field and a second Esc closes the dialog.
Groups are role="group" named by their heading, so screen readers say "Go to" when the highlight enters one.
Shortcuts in items are read as words ("Command N"); icons are hidden.
The dialog palette is a modal <dialog> named by aria-label; focus goes to the input when it opens and back to the trigger when it closes.
do: Offer one in any app with more than a handful of screens or actions, on ⌘K / Ctrl+K, and show the shortcut on a Search button so people find it.
Group items by what they do (Create, Go to, Appearance) and keep labels verb-first ("New task", "Switch theme").
Add keywords for the words people might type instead ("preferences" for Settings).
Show each item's own shortcut at its end so the palette teaches them.
Use TextHighlight (<TextHighlight> in React, <mark class="ayy-text-highlight"> in HTML) to highlight matching terms in titles and descriptions.
Show descriptions conditionally when matches occur in item descriptions, or keep descriptions always visible for items that need extra context.
dont: Don't make it the only way to reach something; it's a shortcut, not navigation.
Don't put form controls inside items; an item runs one thing.
Don't use it to pick a value for a field — that's a Combobox.

components.name: Floating action button
components.description: A round floating button for the main action of a phone screen, like composing or adding something. It stays in the corner over the content and can show a label when extended.

classes.ayy-fab: A <button> (or <a>) with an icon and an aria-label: primary fill, a lifted shadow, size from data-density. position: fixed at the bottom inline-end corner. In an .ayy-app-shell, place it after __main and before the bottom nav.
classes.ayy-fab--extended: Icon and a visible label: a wider pill ("Compose"). Needs no aria-label.
classes.ayy-fab--secondary: A raised surface with a border instead of the primary fill: less emphasis.
classes.ayy-fab--lg: Larger (the lg control height plus 24px) with a 24px icon, for the one thing a screen is for.
classes.ayy-fab--sm: Smaller (the control-lg size), for a second action stacked above the main one.
classes.ayy-fab--inline: Not floating: in the flow, placed by its container (an empty state, a toolbar, a docs page).

default.looks: A round primary-colour button with a 20px icon and the lift shadow, fixed to the bottom inline-end corner clear of the home indicator.

hover.looks: The fill mixes 12% toward the label colour.

focus.looks: 2px ring, 3px offset.

disabled.looks: --ayy-opacity-disabled, not-allowed cursor.

selected.none: A FAB runs an action; it has no on state. For a tool that stays on, use a Toolbar button with aria-pressed.

error.none: No error look. If the action fails, say so in a toast and leave the FAB as it was.

loading.none: Don't spin a FAB. Run the action and show progress where its result appears (a new row's Skeleton, a toast).

scale.sm: The lg control height: 40px compact, 48 comfortable, 52 touch. A second action stacked above the main one.
scale.md: The lg control height plus 12px: 52px compact, 60 comfortable, 64 touch.
scale.lg: The lg control height plus 24px (60px compact, 68 comfortable, 72 touch), with a 24px icon.

sizes.density: Its diameter follows data-density through the lg control height (the sizes above).
sizes.width: Square, a circle. extended (ayy-fab--extended) hugs its icon and label as a pill. Takes no room: it floats over the content (inline puts it back in the flow).

components.js: fabClass({ variant?, size?, extended?, inline?, className? }) → string; fabVariants, fabSizes.

props.extended: boolean — icon and a label; otherwise give it aria-label

a11y: An icon-only FAB needs an aria-label that says the action ("New task"), not the icon ("Plus").
Put it after the main content in the DOM so it comes after what it acts on in the tab order, not before the page.
It must not cover content for good: the App shell keeps it out of the bottom nav, and lists need room at their end (padding-block-end of the FAB's height) so the last row can scroll clear of it.
do: Use one FAB for the screen's main, constructive action: create, compose, scan, add.
Use extended when the action isn't obvious from an icon, or on the first screens of an app.
Hide it on screens where the main action is already on screen (a form's Save) or while a sheet is open.
dont: Don't use more than one main FAB; stack a small secondary one at most.
Don't put destructive or minor actions (Delete, Share, Settings) in a FAB — use a Top bar action or a Menu.
Don't use it on desktop layouts where a toolbar button fits better.

components.name: Navbar
components.description: The header at the top of a website, with the brand on one side and links and actions on the other. It stays in view as the page scrolls, and on phones the links fold into a menu.

classes.ayy-navbar: Root, usually a <header>. Sticky, 72px tall (--ayy-size-header), glass background with a hairline under it. Anchor jumps land below it.
classes.ayy-navbar__inner: Centred row at page width (--ayy-size-container) with the page gutter.
classes.ayy-navbar__brand: Logo / name link at the start.
classes.ayy-navbar__nav: <nav> of links. It and everything after it sit at the end. Without a __toggle it scrolls sideways if the links don't fit; with one, below 48rem it becomes a panel under the bar, shown while the toggle has aria-expanded="true".
classes.ayy-navbar__link: Top-level link. Hover adds a wash; aria-current="page" marks the page you're on with a stronger tint (High Contrast: the system highlight).
classes.ayy-navbar__actions: Group of buttons (a theme menu, the call to action). Next to the brand, or at the end after the nav. Stays in the bar on phones, so keep it to one or two items.
classes.ayy-navbar__toggle: The phone menu button, last in the inner row (combine with ayy-button ayy-button--ghost ayy-button--icon and a menu icon). Hidden from 48rem. Its aria-expanded is the menu's state; connectNavbar() / <ayy-navbar> / React Navbar manage it.

default.looks: Sticky glass bar (--ayy-color-glass, 16px blur) with a hairline underneath; links are muted pills.

hover.looks: Link gets a wash fill and the text colour.

pressed.none: Links have no pressed look.

focus.looks: 2px ring, 2px offset.

disabled.none: A navbar link is never disabled: leave out a page the user can't open.

selected.looks: Current page: wash-hover fill, text colour. Forced colours: Highlight.

error.none: No error state.

loading.none: No loading state; the bar is static.

open.looks: The links drop into a surface panel under the bar with the overlay shadow; links grow to the lg control height.

sizes.density: The bar is --ayy-size-header (4.5rem) tall at every density; links are the md control height (32px compact, 40 comfortable, 44 touch), lg in the phone panel.
sizes.width: Full width; content centred at --ayy-size-container with a 24px gutter (16px below 64rem). Below 48rem, with a __toggle, the links fold into a panel.

components.js: navbarClass, navbarInnerClass, navbarBrandClass, navbarNavClass, navbarLinkClass, navbarActionsClass, navbarToggleClass constants; connectNavbar(header) wires the phone menu and returns a cleanup; navbarMenuIcon (the Hugeicons menu icon as SVG markup).

react.import: import { Navbar, NavbarBrand, NavbarNav, NavbarLink, NavbarActions, NavbarToggle } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";

Navbar.renders: <header class="ayy-navbar"><div class="ayy-navbar__inner">; wires the phone menu when it holds a NavbarToggle

NavbarToggle.renders: <button class="ayy-button ayy-button--ghost ayy-button--icon ayy-navbar__toggle"> with a menu icon

a11y: Use <header> for the bar and <nav aria-label="Main"> for the links; one main nav per page.
Mark the current page with aria-current="page", not only with colour.
Put a .ayy-skip-link before the navbar so keyboard users can jump past it.

The menu button is a real <button> with aria-expanded and aria-controls pointing at the nav (set for you). Focus stays on it when the panel opens; Tab moves into the links, Esc closes the panel and returns focus to the button.
The closed panel is display: none, so its links are out of the tab order until it opens.
do: Use a navbar as the top bar of a website: logo, two to five top-level links, one call to action.
Keep one call to action in the actions group (a ring button for marketing pages, size sm).
Add a NavbarToggle (last) once the links don't fit a phone: they fold into a panel under the bar, and the brand and call to action stay visible.
Put the theme switch (a DropdownMenu of themes that calls setTheme()) in the actions group.
dont: Don't use a navbar in a signed-in app — use the App shell (sidebar, and a Bottom nav on phones).
Don't use it to switch views inside a page — use Tabs.
Don't fill it with long lists of links — move the extras into a DropdownMenu or the footer.
Don't hide links on phones with your own media query — add a NavbarToggle.
Don't give the navbar its own background colour; the glass token keeps every theme right.
Don't nest a second navbar inside the page.

components.name: App shell
components.description: The frame around a web app: a sidebar for navigation next to a main area where the content lives. On phones the sidebar turns into a bottom tab bar or a drawer. The same frame also holds settings screens.

classes.ayy-app-shell: Root. A viewport-high (100dvh) grid: sidebar column (15rem) and a main column. Neither column grows the page; each scrolls on its own. Sets position: relative (the drawer and its scrim are placed inside it). To embed the shell in a box with a fixed height, set block-size: 100% on it. Below 48rem its phone layout follows its children: a .ayy-bottom-nav child shows as the tab bar and the sidebar hides; a __bar makes the sidebar a drawer; with neither, the sidebar becomes a sideways row.
classes.ayy-app-shell__sidebar: The <aside>: surface background, hairline on its inline-end edge, brand at the top, nav below, footer pinned to the bottom. Scrolls vertically when its content is taller than the viewport. On phones it's hidden (bottom-nav layout) or a drawer, and keeps its full tree either way.
classes.ayy-app-shell__brand: The logo link at the top of the sidebar: a mark (a direct-child svg, img or avatar) with the product name beside it, or with a __logotype. The mark takes the icon box of the size step, so its centre is on the same axis as the link icons, expanded and in the rail. A brand with no mark shows nothing in the rail.
classes.ayy-app-shell__logotype: Modifier for a wide wordmark inside the __brand (an img, svg or text span) that only shows while the sidebar is open: in the rail it fades out and the mark stays. Without it an img or svg in the brand is taken for the mark.
classes.ayy-app-shell__nav: <nav> holding the links, stacked vertically (side by side in the phone row).
classes.ayy-app-shell__link: Destination link. aria-current="page" marks the page you're on: it gets a tint and a heavier weight.
classes.ayy-app-shell__row: A row with its own menu, on the <li>: the __link keeps the row and a __more button sits at its end. The button is a sibling of the link, never inside it.
classes.ayy-app-shell__more: Square icon button at the end of a __row that opens the link's menu (⋯). Give it an aria-label naming the row ("Project options"); it shows on hover and focus, always on touch screens, and hides in the rail.
classes.ayy-app-shell__group: A headed section of the nav: a __group-label over a __list. Groups after the first get a hairline above them.
classes.ayy-app-shell__group-label:
The group's heading: a small muted

. Give it an id and point the list's aria-labelledby at it.
classes.ayy-app-shell__group--collapsible: Makes a group optional to collapse: the group is a <details> and its label a <summary class="ayy-app-shell__group-label"> (give it an id; the list's aria-labelledby points at it). A chevron follows the label on hover and focus, and stays while the group is closed (always on touch screens). Add `open` to start open, and open it when it holds the current page. In the rail a closed group's links stay hidden.
classes.ayy-app-shell__link--action: An action row such as "New": the link's icon sits in a filled circle (a spread shadow, so it stays in the icon column).
classes.ayy-app-shell__list: The <ul> of a group. Each <li> holds a link, a link followed by a __sublist, or a __collapse.
classes.ayy-app-shell__sublist: A nested <ul> of child links, indented along a guide line. One level only. Follows a parent link, or sits inside a __collapse. Give it an aria-label when it follows a link.
classes.ayy-app-shell__collapse: A native <details> for a group of child links that opens and closes. Its <summary class="ayy-app-shell__link"> is the toggle, with a chevron at the inline end; put the links in a __sublist inside it. Add `open` when it holds the current page.
classes.ayy-app-shell__link--sub: Modifier for a child link inside a __sublist: a smaller control and a lighter weight.
classes.ayy-app-shell__footer: Pinned to the bottom of the sidebar (the end of the row on phones): settings, account, help link. Keep it short.
classes.ayy-app-shell__main: The <main> content column. Scrolls on its own and has the page gutter. In a settings dialog it's a <div>: the page behind already has the one <main>.
classes.ayy-app-shell__bar: Phone top bar, first child of the shell, hidden from 48rem: the brand, then one or two actions (search, account), which sit at the inline end. Add a __toggle to it when the sidebar should open as a drawer. With a bar or a bottom nav the phone sidebar is off-screen; it slides in from the inline-start edge over a scrim while a toggle has aria-expanded="true".
classes.ayy-app-shell--settings: Settings mode, on the root of a shell inside a <dialog class="ayy-dialog ayy-dialog--full">, which it fills; the dialog's close button is the way out. The sidebar holds an __title and a nav of settings sections (groups of links, one aria-current="page"); the main holds the open section, starting with a Top bar whose title names it and whose back button shows on phones only; the section's content sits in a column of --ayy-size-measure, centred. On wide screens the top is roomy: "Settings" and the section title, both xl, sit on one line with space above them, and the section's Top bar has no divider. No __bar and no bottom nav. (On a page of its own instead of a dialog, start the sidebar with an __back.) Below 48rem: with no section link current the sidebar is the whole screen (a large title and rows with chevrons) and the main is hidden; with one current, the main is the screen and the sidebar is hidden.
classes.ayy-app-shell__back: Only for a settings shell on a page of its own (in a dialog, the close button is the way out). First in the sidebar: an <a href> back to the page settings were opened from (or a <button>), with a directional arrow icon and "Back to <app name>". In settings mode, Esc follows it.
classes.ayy-app-shell__head: The sidebar's top row for a collapsible sidebar: the __brand first, then any actions, and the __toggle, which is placed over the inline end of the row. In the rail the row is one icon wide: the brand's mark shows, and resting the pointer on it (or focusing the toggle) swaps it for the toggle, which expands the sidebar. A brand with no mark leaves the toggle showing. Mark and toggle icon sit on the same axis as the link icons. A Tooltip around the toggle takes its place at the end of the row.
classes.ayy-app-shell__title: A settings sidebar's heading, an <h2> "Settings" that names the dialog (aria-labelledby). Large on the phone's section list.
classes.ayy-app-shell__toggle: The button that opens the sidebar as a drawer on phones: in the __bar (with ayy-button ayy-button--ghost ayy-button--icon and a menu icon), or as the "More" tab of the bottom nav (<button class="ayy-bottom-nav__link ayy-app-shell__toggle">). Its aria-expanded is the drawer's state. In the sidebar (last in an __head, with a directional sidebar icon) it is a row-sized square at the inline end that collapses and expands the sidebar on wide screens, and its aria-expanded is whether the sidebar is open. There it shows a tooltip naming the action (Collapse / Expand) on hover and focus. connectAppShell() / <ayy-app-shell> / React AppShell manage it.
classes.ayy-app-shell--collapsed: Collapsed sidebar mode on wide screens: the sidebar narrows to an icon rail, animating its width with the main column. Rows stay on one line and in place, so icons keep their spot while labels and group labels fade and clip (wrap a link's label in a <span> to fade it); links without an icon fade out and leave the tab order; sub-lists hide. The toggle's aria-expanded reflects the state.
classes.ayy-app-shell--hover-preview: With --collapsed: resting the pointer on the rail (after a short pause) or moving keyboard focus into it widens the sidebar to full width over the main area with the overlay shadow, without moving the main content; it closes a moment after the pointer leaves, unless a menu or popover inside it (an account or settings menu) is open: then it stays open until that closes. A mouse click inside doesn't keep it open. Right after the sidebar's toggle collapses it, connectAppShell sets data-ayy-hold on the sidebar so it doesn't reopen under the pointer, until the pointer leaves or focus moves on.
classes.ayy-app-shell--drawer: Root modifier: below 48rem the sidebar is a drawer even with no __bar and no bottom nav (instead of the sideways row), and the __toggle may sit in the main area, in an app's own top bar. Wide screens are unchanged.
classes.ayy-app-shell__detail: A third column at the inline end (an <aside>), for what's picked in the main area: a task, a message. Surface background, hairline on its inline-start edge, scrolls on its own, --ayy-detail-w wide (22rem). Show and hide it with the hidden attribute: hidden, the shell is two columns again. Below 48rem it covers the screen, so start it with a Top bar and a back button.
classes.ayy-app-shell__resize: A drag handle on the sidebar's inline-end edge, a direct child of the shell with role="separator" aria-orientation="vertical" tabindex="0" (added for you). Dragging, the arrow keys (Shift for big steps), Home and End set --ayy-sidebar-w on the shell; a double click resets it. Limits come from aria-valuemin / aria-valuemax in px (default 192 and 384), and the main area always keeps 320px. Hidden below 48rem and while the sidebar is collapsed.
classes.ayy-app-shell__resize--detail: Modifier: the handle for the detail pane's inline-start edge, setting --ayy-detail-w (limits default 288 and 640). Shown only while the detail pane is.
classes.ayy-app-shell--resizing: Set by connectAppShell while a handle is being dragged: columns follow the pointer without animating. Don't set it yourself.
classes.ayy-app-shell--md: Medium size: 32px compact rows with 16px icons, 8px from the row edge to the icon.
classes.ayy-app-shell--sm: Small size, for long navigation such as a docs tree: sm-height links with no gap between them, regular weight, sm icons and the control radius. Big (lg, no modifier) is the default for apps.

default.looks: A 15rem surface sidebar with a hairline at the inline end, and the main area on the page background; each scrolls on its own. Links are muted pills.

hover.when: .ayy-app-shell__link:hover; a row's .ayy-app-shell__more:hover; on a collapsed shell with hover preview, .ayy-app-shell__sidebar:hover expands the sidebar as an overlay
hover.looks: Link gets a wash fill and the text colour; a row's More button gets a wash-hover square and shows for the whole row. In hover preview, the sidebar animates to its full width with the overlay shadow over the content.

pressed.none: Links have no pressed look.

focus.when: links, brand, a row's __more, sidebar and main :focus-visible
focus.looks: Links, brand and a row's More button: 2px ring, 2px offset; focusing the More button also reveals it. A focused scroll area (sidebar or main with tabindex="0") gets the ring inset.

disabled.none: Sidebar links are never disabled: leave out pages the user can't open.

selected.looks: Current page: wash-hover fill, text colour, semibold (not colour alone). A closed collapse holding it shows its summary in text colour and semibold. Forced colours: Highlight. In settings mode the current section link is the open section; below 48rem it decides whether the section list or the section fills the screen.

error.none: Errors belong in the main content (Alert).

loading.none: The frame renders at once; show Skeletons in the main area while a screen loads.

open.when: __toggle[aria-expanded="true"] (below 48rem, with a __bar or a Bottom nav); <details open> for a collapse; a row's __more[aria-expanded="true"]
open.looks: Phone: the sidebar slides in from the inline-start edge as a drawer (at most 18rem) over a scrim, with the overlay shadow. A collapse's chevron turns up. A row's More button keeps its wash fill while its menu is open and stays visible.

scale.sm: Small: links at the sm control height (28px compact), sub-links sm, no gap between rows, regular weight, 16px icons (6px from the row edge), the control radius.
scale.md: Medium: links at the md control height (32px compact), sub-links sm, 16px icons.
scale.lg: Big (default): links at the lg control height (40px compact), sub-links md, --ayy-space-0-5 between rows, medium weight, 20px icons (10px from the row edge), pill radius.

sizes.density: Big links are at least the lg control height (40px compact, 48 comfortable, 52 touch) with lg control text, Medium ones md (32, 40, 44) with md control text, Small ones sm (28, 32, 40) with sm control text; sub-links one step down. Grows with data-density. Links, sidebar buttons, the logo row and the toggle share one row height, and every icon sits centred in a square that wide at the start of the row, so icons, the brand's mark and the toggle's icon line up in a column, in the full sidebar and in the rail alike. The sub-list's guide line runs down that column too. A row's __more button is the sm control size (28, 32, 40) with a 16px icon, so it fits inside the row at every size.
sizes.width: Fills the viewport (100dvh) or its box (block-size: 100%). Wide screens: 15rem sidebar or collapsed icon rail. Below 48rem: a top __bar, a Bottom nav and a drawer, or one scrolling row when it holds neither.

props.collapsible: boolean — renders a <details> with the label as its <summary> (ayy-app-shell__group--collapsible); a chevron shows on hover.
props.defaultOpen: boolean — with collapsible, whether it starts open. Default true.

AppShellToggle.renders: <button class="ayy-button ayy-button--ghost ayy-button--icon ayy-app-shell__toggle"> with a menu icon; in an AppShellHead it is wrapped in a Tooltip (opening below) that names the collapse action

props.aria-label: Defaults to "Menu" in the phone bar, and to the action ("Collapse sidebar" / "Expand sidebar") in an AppShellHead (translate it).
props.tooltip: Tooltip text. In an AppShellHead it defaults to the action ("Collapse" / "Expand"); the phone drawer's menu has none. false disables it.

a11y: The sidebar is an <aside> (a complementary landmark) and the content is a <main>: one <main> per page, and no other element with that landmark.

Keep one <nav aria-label="Main"> in the sidebar. The bottom nav repeats its top destinations and only one of the two shows at a time, so it can use the same label. Give any other nav (a settings menu) its own label.

Mark the current page with aria-current="page" in both the sidebar and the bottom nav. The link also gets a tint and a heavier weight, so colour is not the only cue; High Contrast mode fills it with the system highlight.
Put a .ayy-skip-link before the shell, pointing at an id on <main>, so keyboard users can jump past the sidebar.
A row's __more is a real button after the link, not inside it (buttons can't nest), and its aria-label names the row ("Project options") so a list of identical "More" buttons isn't ambiguous.

Group with a heading and a list: the

label names the

    through aria-labelledby, so a screen reader announces "Workspace, list, 3 items".
A collapse is a native <details>: Enter and Space toggle it, and the open state is exposed for you. Don't add aria-expanded to the <summary>.
Mark the current child with aria-current="page" and open its collapse. A closed collapse that holds the current page is drawn bolder, so the location isn't hidden.
Both columns are scroll containers. If a column can scroll but holds nothing focusable, give it tabindex="0" so keyboard users can scroll it.

The drawer's toggle is a real <button> with aria-expanded and aria-controls pointing at the sidebar (set for you). Opening moves focus to the first link in the drawer and makes the rest of the shell inert; Esc closes it and returns focus to the toggle.

Settings mode: name the dialog by the sidebar title (aria-labelledby on the <dialog>), give the sections' nav its own label ("Settings"), mark the open section with aria-current="page", and make the section's Top bar title its <h1> (the sidebar title is an <h2>). Render the main as a <div> so the page keeps one <main>. On phones, opening a section moves focus to the main, and its back button returns it to the section's link.

A collapsed sidebar with hover preview opens when keyboard focus moves into it (:focus-visible), so every link is reachable and readable from the keyboard; links without an icon are only in the tab order while it's open. Give rail links a title for a tooltip with the pointer.

The sidebar's collapse toggle says what it does: in React, its aria-label and tooltip change between "Collapse sidebar" and "Expand sidebar" with the state, so the icon is never a guess. In plain markup, write the label and an <ayy-tooltip> for the state shown.

In a dialog, Esc closes settings and focus returns to what opened them. A settings shell on a page of its own leaves through its __back on Esc, except when focus is in a text field or an open menu, popover or dialog has it.
A resize handle is a separator you can focus: arrow keys move the edge by 16px (Shift 64), Home and End jump to the limits, and aria-valuenow / min / max are kept in px.
The detail pane is an <aside>: label it (aria-label) for what it shows, and move focus into it when you open it from the main area.
The phone sidebar (closed drawer) is visibility: hidden, and the bottom nav is display: none from 48rem, so hidden links are out of the tab order and the accessibility tree.
do: Use it as the outer layout of a signed-in app or dashboard.
Keep the same destinations, icons and order on every screen.
Use size="sm" for long navigation such as a docs tree.
With more than five destinations, put the four most used in the bottom nav and end with a "More" tab that opens the drawer.
Group destinations under headings once there are more than about six.
Keep each link to one line: an icon and a short label. Put account and help in the footer.
Give a destination that people manage (a project, a page, a folder) an ayy-app-shell__row with an AppShellMore at its end: the link still opens it, and the ⋯ opens rename, duplicate and archive.
Give the brand a mark (an icon or your logo) and a name or a __logotype: the rail shows the mark, and resting the pointer on it reveals the expand button.
Start each page in the main with a Page header.
Add a __resize handle when people have long names to read, and save the width from onResize / ayy-resize.
Open settings in a Dialog with size="full", sections grouped, each starting with a Top bar.
dont: Don't use it for a marketing site (use Navbar) or to switch views of one object (use Tabs).
Don't put a Navbar in it or nest a second app shell.
Don't nest links deeper than one level.
Don't rely on the sideways row for a real app: it hides links. Use a bottom nav, a __bar, or the --drawer modifier.
Don't make the detail pane the only place to do something: on phones it covers the screen, so give it a back button.
Don't show or hide the sidebar with your own media queries; the shell switches at 48rem.
Don't scroll the page body as well, or cap the main width.
Don't put settings in Tabs or a small Dialog.

element.children: A <div class="ayy-app-shell">. Wires the phone drawer when the shell has a __toggle in its __bar or its .ayy-bottom-nav: the toggle opens and closes the sidebar; Esc, the scrim, a link in the drawer or widening past 48rem close it. On wide screens, wires sidebar collapsing and optional hover-preview. On a settings shell, Esc follows the __back. A __row with a __more button is an ordinary button after the link: wire its menu with <ayy-menu>. A sidebar toggle's data-ayy-label-expanded / data-ayy-label-collapsed, also on its .ayy-tooltip__content, keep its label and tooltip text on the action it now performs.

components.name: Bottom nav
components.description: The tab bar of a phone app. It keeps the main destinations at the bottom of the screen where a thumb can reach them, each with an icon and a short label. Inside an App shell it replaces the sidebar on phones.

classes.ayy-bottom-nav: The <nav>. Equal-width columns, one per link. Sticky to the bottom of its scroll container (the page, or the box it scrolls in), with the safe-area inset added below. As a direct child of .ayy-app-shell it shows below 48rem only; from 48rem the sidebar carries the same links.

classes.ayy-bottom-nav--md: Medium height (32px) with 20px icons and medium padding.
classes.ayy-bottom-nav--lg: Large height (40px, default) with 20px icons and generous touch padding.
classes.ayy-bottom-nav--compact: Compact layout with tighter padding and narrower pills so five or more tabs fit side-by-side without overflowing.
classes.ayy-bottom-nav--icon-only: Icon-only layout, visually hiding tab labels while keeping them accessible for screen readers.
classes.ayy-bottom-nav__link: A tab: icon over label. An <a> for a destination, or a <button> for a tab that acts ("More", which opens the app shell's drawer when it also has ayy-app-shell__toggle). aria-current="page" (or aria-expanded="true" on the button) draws a pill behind the icon and a heavier label.
classes.ayy-bottom-nav__label: The tab's text, one line, cut with an ellipsis if it's too long.

default.looks: Surface bar pinned to the bottom with a hairline on top; each tab is a muted icon over an xs label.

hover.looks: Label turns text colour; a wash pill appears behind the icon.

pressed.none: No pressed look (touch highlight is off); the page change is the feedback.

focus.looks: 2px ring inset by 2px.

disabled.none: Tabs are never disabled; show the screen and explain inside it.

selected.looks: Text colour, semibold label and a wash-hover pill behind the icon. Forced colours: Highlight pill.

error.none: No error state.

loading.none: No loading state.

scale.sm: Small height (28px compact, 32 comfortable, 40 touch) with 16px icons.
scale.md: Medium height (32px compact, 40 comfortable, 44 touch) with 20px icons.
scale.lg: Large height (40px compact, 48 comfortable, 52 touch) with 20px icons and generous touch padding.

sizes.density: Each tab follows the control height scale (sm 28px, md 32px, lg 40px compact); the bar adds the safe-area inset at the bottom.
sizes.width: Full width, tabs share it equally (three to five in default, five to seven or more in compact).

props.icon: ReactNode — the icon above the label (an <Icon>).

props.icon: ReactNode — the icon above the label.

a11y: It's a <nav>: give it an aria-label ("Main" by default in React). Inside an App shell only one of it and the sidebar shows at a time, so they can share the label.
Mark the current page with aria-current="page". It also gets a pill and a heavier weight, so colour isn't the only cue; High Contrast mode fills the pill with the system highlight.
Visible labels are recommended. When iconOnly is used, screen reader text is preserved via visually hidden labels.
A "More" tab is a <button> with aria-expanded (set for you when it's an app shell toggle), not a link to "#".
Each tab is at least the control height of its size tier (sm 28px, md 32px, lg 40px), maintaining comfortable touch targets.
Outside an App shell, content above it needs bottom padding (or to end before it) so the last line isn't hidden behind the bar.
do: Use a bottom nav for top-level destinations of a phone app, so they're one thumb-tap away.
Use compact mode or sm/md sizes when accommodating five or more destinations.
Put it inside the App shell, after the main: it shows on phones and the sidebar takes over from 48rem, with no media query of yours.
Give it the same destinations, icons and order as the sidebar's top-level links.
Keep labels to one short word: Home, Search, Inbox, Account.
With many destinations, end with a "More" tab that opens the sidebar as a drawer (a BottomNavButton with the ayy-app-shell__toggle class).
dont: Don't use a bottom nav for actions (compose, share) — use a Button, or a bottom-sheet Dialog for a list of actions. The one exception is a "More" tab that opens the drawer.
Don't use it to switch views of one thing inside a page — use Tabs or a Segmented control.
Don't show it next to the sidebar on wide screens, and don't hide it with your own media query when it's inside an App shell.
Don't nest menus in it or change its tabs from page to page.

a11y: The title is the page's <h1>, so a screen reader user knows where they landed after navigating.
A chevron-only back button is named "Back" (translate it); with a visible name ("Lists") the text names it.
Icon buttons in __actions each need an aria-label. Keep to three; put the rest in a Menu behind a More button.
The chevron is directional, so it points right in RTL, where "back" is.
do: Use it at the top of every phone screen below the tab bar's first level, with a back button to where the user came from.
Use large on a tab's first screen (Inbox, Notes), plain on the screens pushed from it.
Put the screen's own search in the __row so it scrolls away with the bar or stays, as you choose.

Start each section of a settings shell (App shell in settings mode, in a size="full" Dialog) with one: onBack (or backHref) to the section list, backLabel "Settings", the section's name as the title. Its back button shows on phones only, and on wide screens its title lines up with the section's column.
dont: Don't use it as a site's header on wide screens — that's the Navbar (or the App shell's sidebar).
Don't put the brand or navigation links in it; it names the screen.
Don't add more than three actions.

components.name: Breadcrumb
components.description: A trail of links that shows where the current page sits in the site, from the top level down. It lets people jump back to any page above it.

classes.ayy-breadcrumb--pill: Bordered, blurred capsule that stays readable over hero images and grids.

hover.looks: Link turns text colour.

pressed.none: No pressed look.

focus.looks: 2px ring, 2px offset.

disabled.none: Every ancestor is a link; the current page is plain text, not a disabled link.

error.none: No error state.

loading.none: No loading state.

scale.md: --ayy-text-sm (14px).
scale.lg: --ayy-text-md (16px).

sizes.density: Text sizes are fixed at every density; link targets grow to a control tall.
sizes.width: Hugs its items and wraps. pill puts it in a blurred, bordered capsule for heroes.

The current page is plain text with aria-current="page", not a link to itself.
do: Use a breadcrumb on pages that sit two or more levels deep: an index page, a case study, an article.
Use the page titles as they appear in their own headings.
Use pill over imagery or the ambient grid; plain elsewhere.
dont: Don't add one to the home page or a single-level site.
Don't use it for steps in a process — use Steps; a breadcrumb is a location, not progress.
Don't include the current page as a link.
Don't use it as the only navigation.

components.description: Controls for moving between the pages of a long table or list: previous, next and page numbers. On phones it shrinks to the essentials.

The current page has aria-current="page"; it's outlined and bolder as well as tinted.
Previous and next say so in words; their arrows are decorative and mirror in right-to-left text.
An end you can't go past is aria-disabled (or disabled): screen readers hear it's unavailable.
After a page change in place, move focus to the top of the updated table or list, or announce the new range.
do: Use pagination under a table or list that has more rows than fit, when people need to reach a specific page or share its URL.
Give pages URLs (href) when you can, so back and reload work.
Offer a page size picker (pageSize, onPageSizeChange) on long tables so people choose how much they scan.
Show the range next to it ("41–60 of 1,280") in muted text.
dont: Don't use pagination for a feed people only scroll through — load more as they scroll, or add a Load more button.
Don't use it to step through a sign-up or checkout — use Steps.
Don't show it when everything fits on one page.

error.none: No error look; put the problem in the step's content (Alert, FieldError).

loading.none: No loading look.

scale.md: Markers the sm control height (28px compact, 32 comfortable, 40 touch), --ayy-text-sm labels.
scale.lg: Markers the md control height (32px compact, 40 comfortable, 44 touch), --ayy-text-md labels.

Done steps say so in text, not only with a tick: put an .ayy-sr-only "Done: " before their label (React does it).
The markers are generated content with empty alt text, so numbers aren't read twice.

Name steps by what happens in them (Account, Team, Billing), in one or two words.
Use the vertical version beside a long form on wide screens, or when the row wouldn't fit a phone.

Don't use them for pages of results — use Pagination.

classes.ayy-toc__link: Section link (href="#id"). aria-current (set by the scrollspy) shows the accent bar; its parent link lights up too.
classes.ayy-toc__number: Optional section number (01, 02…) before the label, in the accent while current.

default.looks: A hairline rail with muted sm links; nested links indent and get smaller. On phones, a sticky pill showing the active section.

hover.looks: Link turns text colour; toggle pill border and background lighten.

pressed.none: No pressed look.

disabled.none: No disabled links.

selected.when: .ayy-toc__link[aria-current] (not "false"), kept in sync by <ayy-toc> or connectToc
selected.looks: Section being read: text colour and a 2px --ayy-spot bar on the rail; its number takes the accent; a parent of it turns text colour too. Forced colours: underline and Highlight bar.

error.none: No error state.

loading.none: No loading state.

sizes.density: Links follow the control height scale (var(--ayy-size-control-sm)), so comfortable or touch density expands their tap target to 40px without changing the rail spacing.
sizes.width: Fills its column. sticky stays in view under the navbar and scrolls on its own when taller than the viewport.

The current section is aria-current="location", announced by screen readers, not only drawn as a colour bar.
Links are ordinary in-page anchors: they work without JS, and the navbar's scroll-padding keeps targets clear of the sticky header.
Links grow to a 40px target at touch density. On phones the visible title is hidden but still names the nav, and the sticky toggle pill is labeled via aria-label.
do: Use a table of contents on long pages with named sections: case studies, docs, articles, settings pages.
List sections in page order; the scrollspy assumes it.
Set --ayy-spot on the page (or the nav) to tint the bar and number with the content's accent.
Make the page layout put it above the content on phones (a wrapping flex row does, as in the example); --sticky then turns it into a sticky pill with a dropdown menu.
dont: Don't add one to short pages with two or three sections.
Don't use it to navigate between pages — use Navbar or links.
Don't nest more than one level.
Don't list every heading — sections and their direct sub-sections only.

components.name: Tree
components.description: A hierarchical list of folders, files or records: groups that open and close with a chevron, one selected row and arrow-key navigation. Use it to browse a folder or file structure, or as a picker inside a card.

classes.ayy-tree: Root <ul role="tree">. Its aria-label names it ("Folders"). <ayy-tree> wraps it with display: contents.
classes.ayy-tree__item: One <li role="treeitem">. Carries aria-level, aria-selected on every node, aria-expanded only on parents, and a roving tabindex: exactly one visible item is 0, the rest -1. aria-disabled="true" makes it unselectable.
classes.ayy-tree__row: The clickable row inside the item: toggle, optional icon and label. Hover and selected washes sit here, and so does the focus ring.
classes.ayy-tree__toggle: The decorative <span aria-hidden="true"> holding the chevron. Clicking it opens or closes the group without selecting the row; the treeitem's aria-expanded carries the state.
classes.ayy-tree__icon: An optional decorative icon before the label (an <svg class="ayy-icon ayy-tree__icon"> drawn by Icon or iconSvg). Muted, and text colour on the selected row.
classes.ayy-tree__label: The node's label. It takes the leftover width, wraps anywhere so a long unbroken name never scrolls the tree sideways, and is not the accessible name: the item's aria-label is.
classes.ayy-tree__group: A nested <ul role="group"> of child items, indented by --ayy-space-5 (--ayy-space-4 with --compact). Put hidden on it while its parent is aria-expanded="false"; connectTree keeps the two in step.
classes.ayy-tree--compact: Tighter rows at the sm control height, small control text, a 16px indent and a 16px toggle.

default.looks: Rows at the md control height, with a muted chevron and icon, the label in the text colour, and --ayy-space-0-5 between rows.

hover.looks: A --ayy-color-wash behind the row and, over the chevron, a --ayy-color-wash-hover and the text colour. A selected row keeps its stronger wash.

pressed.none: No pressed look: the click selects the row at once.

focus.looks: A 2px --ayy-color-ring outline on the row, inset by 2px. Hidden after pointer use by trackInputModality()'s pointer mode.

disabled.looks: --ayy-opacity-disabled and a not-allowed cursor; clicking selects and activates nothing. Forced colours: GrayText.

selected.when: aria-selected="true" on the treeitem, set by a click, Space, or your selectedId
selected.looks: A --ayy-color-wash-hover behind the row, the text colour and a medium weight; its icon takes the text colour. Forced colours: a Highlight outline.

error.none: No error state; show problems beside the tree (Alert or FieldError).

loading.none: No loading state; put Skeleton rows in the tree's place while it loads.

expanded.looks: Its group is not hidden and the chevron turns down: rotate(90deg) in LTR, the mirror in RTL (--_ayy-dir). The treeitem's aria-expanded, not the decorative toggle, carries the state.

sizes.density: Rows are at least the md control height (32px compact, 40px comfortable, 44px touch) with --ayy-control-text-md; --compact uses the sm height (28, 32, 40) and --ayy-control-text-sm. The toggle is 20px (16px compact), so touch density keeps a comfortable target.
sizes.width: Fills its container. Child groups indent by --ayy-space-5 (--ayy-space-4 compact) using padding-inline-start, so they indent from the right in RTL. Labels take the leftover width and wrap anywhere.

components.js: treeClass({ compact?, className? }) → root classes; treeItemClass, treeRowClass, treeToggleClass, treeIconClass, treeLabelClass, treeGroupClass constants; treeChevronIcon (the ArrowRight01Icon SVG, directional); connectTree(root, { onSelect?, onActivate?, onToggle? }) → { focus(id?), destroy() } — expansion, single selection, roving tabindex and keyboard movement on plain markup.

element.children: Wraps the <ul role="tree"> and makes it work: the toggle opens and closes a group, a row selects, double-click or Enter activates, and the arrow keys, Home and End move the roving tab stop. focus(id) moves to a node from code.

events.ayy-select: { id } — a row was clicked or Space was pressed on it.
events.ayy-activate: { id } — a row was double-clicked or Enter was pressed on it (open the file or folder).
events.ayy-toggle: { id, expanded } — a group was opened (true) or closed (false).

Tree.renders: <ul class="ayy-tree" role="tree" aria-label> with a <li class="ayy-tree__item" role="treeitem"> per node, a __row inside it, and a nested <ul class="ayy-tree__group" role="group" hidden> for children

props.label: string — accessible name of the tree ("Folders")
props.nodes: TreeNode[] — { id: string; label: string; icon?: ReactNode; children?: TreeNode[]; disabled?: boolean }, nested in display order
props.expandedIds / defaultExpandedIds: string[] — open group ids; expandedIds makes it controlled, defaultExpandedIds sets the starting ones
props.onExpandedChange: (ids: string[]) => void — a group opened or closed
props.selectedId / defaultSelectedId: string — the selected node; selectedId makes it controlled, defaultSelectedId sets the starting one
props.onSelectedChange: (id: string | null) => void — a row was selected
props.onActivate: (id: string) => void — a row was double-clicked or Enter was pressed
props.compact: boolean — tighter rows, a smaller indent and the small control text

a11y: The tree is a <ul role="tree"> with a name (label in React, aria-label in HTML); each node is a <li role="treeitem"> with aria-level, and children sit in a <ul role="group">.

aria-expanded is only on parents and aria-selected is on every node, so the state is announced rather than drawn only as a wash. The toggle is decorative (aria-hidden) and the item's aria-label is the node label, never the toggle.

One visible item has tabindex="0" and the rest -1 (a roving tab stop). Tab enters the tree on the selected node, then the arrow keys, Home and End move through the visible nodes: Right closes an open group or opens a closed one and steps into its first child, Left closes an open group or moves to the parent.
Enter activates a node and Space selects it. Double-click activates too. A composing IME and fields inside a row (a rename input) keep their keys.
aria-disabled="true" keeps a node readable and reachable by the keyboard while it refuses selection and activation; colour is backed by opacity and, in High Contrast, GrayText.
Long labels wrap inside the row instead of scrolling the tree sideways, and touch density raises the rows to the 44px target.
do: Use a tree to browse a nested structure: folders and files, a page hierarchy, categories or a project's contents.
Keep ids stable and pass them as expandedIds/selectedId when the rest of the screen shows the same folder (a picker in a card, a split view).
Pair the chevron with the label on the same row and let the label wrap; never truncate a folder name to make a narrow tree fit.
dont: Don't use a tree for a flat list — use List; for sections that collapse in place use Accordion.
Don't use it as the app's main navigation — use App shell or Navbar.

Don't pack several controls into a row: the tree ignores clicks inside a button, link or field, but the row's job is selection. Put a bigger set of actions in a detail pane or a menu outside the tree.
Don't nest more than four or five levels; show a breadcrumb or a detail pane instead.

components.name: Field
components.description: A wrapper that ties a label, an input and its hint or error message together with consistent spacing. Use it around any form control.

classes.ayy-field--inline: Label and control side by side (Switch, checkbox).
classes.ayy-label: The <label>. Usable on its own too.
classes.ayy-field__hint: Muted helper text under the control.

default.looks: Label (control md text, medium weight, text colour) above the control; hint below in muted control sm text.

hover.none: The control inside shows hover.

pressed.none: The control inside handles presses.

focus.none: The control inside shows the focus ring.

disabled.looks: Label dims to --ayy-opacity-disabled with a not-allowed cursor; the control dims itself.

selected.none: Selection belongs to the control (Checkbox, Radio, Switch).

error.when: aria-invalid="true" on the control plus .ayy-field__error, linked with aria-describedby (React: FieldError)
error.looks: Error message in --ayy-color-destructive, control sm text, replacing or after the hint; the control draws a red border.

loading.none: Fields don't load; show a Skeleton for the whole form while its data loads.

sizes.density: Label text follows control md, hint and error control sm, so they grow with data-density.
sizes.width: Fills its column; the control inside stretches to it. inline puts the control and label side by side (checkboxes, switches).

components.js: fieldClass({ inline?, className? }); labelClass, fieldHintClass, fieldErrorClass constants

react.import: import { Field, Label, FieldHint, FieldError } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";

a11y: Label htmlFor/for must match the control id.
Link hint/error to the control with aria-describedby; set aria-invalid="true" on the control when there's an error.
The label dims automatically when the control inside the field is disabled.
do: Wrap every labelled form control in a Field: Input, Input group, Textarea, Select, Switch, Checkbox.
Keep hints to one short sentence.
Show errors after the user leaves the field or submits, not on every keystroke.
dont: Don't wrap search boxes in toolbars — an aria-label on the Input is enough.
Don't show a hint and an error at the same time — the error replaces the hint.

components.name: Input
components.description: A single-line text field for names, emails, passwords, search and other short text. It can hold icons, addons and buttons inside the field.

classes.ayy-input-group: Root for an input with inline addons, icons or buttons. Draws the field (border, fill, radius, height) and the focus ring while its .ayy-input is focused.
classes.ayy-input-group__addon: Text beside the input: a prefix (https://), a suffix (USD, %) or a Kbd hint. Muted, one line.

default.looks: Wash fill, 1px line-strong border, control radius; placeholder in muted at 70%. In an input group, addons and icons are muted and the input loses its own border.

hover.looks: Border turns line-hover.

pressed.none: Text fields have no pressed look; the caret shows where you are. Trailing buttons keep their own pressed look.

focus.looks: 2px ring drawn just inside the edge (-1px offset); the border goes transparent. In an input group, the ring moves to the group container.

disabled.looks: --ayy-opacity-disabled, not-allowed cursor.

selected.none: Not a choice control.

error.looks: Border 60% destructive; the focus ring turns destructive. Forced colours: dashed border.

loading.none: No loading look. While a value is checked (a username), use an Input group with a small Spinner as its addon.

scale.sm: Control sm height (28px compact, 32 comfortable, 40 touch), tighter padding, sm text.
scale.md: Control md height (32px compact, 40 comfortable, 44 touch).
scale.lg: Control lg height (40px compact, 48 comfortable, 52 touch), more padding, lg text.

sizes.density: Height and text size follow data-density; touch keeps md text at 16px so iOS doesn't zoom.
sizes.width: Fills its container (inline-size 100%); set a max-inline-size in rem for short values.

components.js: inputClass({ size?, className? }) → string; inputGroupClass({ size?, className? }) → string; inputGroupAddonClass constant.

props.size: "sm" | "md" | "lg" (visual size; native size attr not exposed)

a11y: Every input needs a label: wrap in a Field with a Label (for/id), or aria-label for search boxes.
The input inside an InputGroup still needs its own label; icons and addons do not name it.
Errors: aria-invalid="true" + aria-describedby pointing at the error text.
Action buttons inside an InputGroup (show password, clear) must have an accessible aria-label and aria-pressed where applicable.
do: Use an input for short free-text entry: names, URLs, search, API keys, passwords.
Use an InputGroup when an input needs a leading icon, a prefix/suffix unit, or a trailing action button.
Match the input size to neighbouring buttons in a toolbar (sm with sm).
dont: Don't use an input for multi-line text — use Textarea.
Don't use an input for on/off — use Switch.
Don't use placeholder as the label.
Don't hardcode widths in px inside flexible layouts — the input fills its container.
Don't use an input for picking dates or times — use Date & time picker (DatePicker, DateRange, TimePicker, DateTimePicker).
Don't stack more than one addon on each side of an InputGroup.
Don't put a primary action button inside an InputGroup — place a Button next to it.

components.name: PIN input
components.description: One box per character for verification codes, two-factor authentication tokens and passcodes. Typing advances to the next box, Backspace steps back, and pasting or SMS autofill fills the whole code at once.

classes.ayy-pin-input: Root group (role="group", direction ltr so codes always read left to right).
classes.ayy-pin-input__group: Tighter cluster of slots when a code is split into halves (e.g. 3 + 3).

default.looks: Square wash boxes with 1px line-strong borders, centred monospace digits.

hover.looks: Slot border turns --ayy-color-line-hover.

pressed.none: Text slots have no pressed look; clicking focuses and selects the slot.

focus.looks: 2px --ayy-color-ring outline (-1px offset); the slot border goes transparent.

disabled.looks: --ayy-opacity-disabled, not-allowed cursor. Forced colours: GrayText.

selected.none: Not a choice control.

error.looks: 60% destructive border and destructive focus ring. Forced colours: dashed border.

loading.none: Disable the slots and show a Spinner on the verify Button while checking the code.

scale.sm: Square at --ayy-size-control-sm (28px compact, 32 comfortable, 40 touch), sm text.
scale.md: Square at --ayy-size-control-md (32px compact, 40 comfortable, 44 touch), field text.
scale.lg: Square at --ayy-size-control-lg (40px compact, 48 comfortable, 52 touch), lg text.

sizes.density: Slot width, height and text size follow data-density across all steps.
sizes.width: Hugs its slots and separators.

element.description: Wires an .ayy-pin-input of .ayy-pin-input__slot inputs: auto-advance, Backspace, arrows, paste, SMS autofill, optional hidden form input, and change/complete events.
element.children: An .ayy-pin-input containing .ayy-pin-input__slot <input> elements (optionally grouped in .ayy-pin-input__group with .ayy-pin-input__separator).

attributes.name: Form field name: syncs a hidden input with the combined code.

events.ayy-change: { value: string } — fired whenever the code changes.
events.ayy-complete: { value: string } — fired once every slot is filled.

props.length: number — total slots when groups is omitted (default 6).
props.groups: number[] — split slots into groups with a dash between them, e.g. [3, 3].
props.mask: boolean — hide entered characters as password dots.
props.onComplete: (value: string) => void — called once all slots are filled.
props.invalid: boolean — sets aria-invalid="true" on the group and slots.
props.name: string — renders a hidden input carrying the combined code.
props.autoFocus: boolean — focuses the first slot on mount.

a11y: Wrap in a Field with a Label (or aria-labelledby on the group), and keep each slot's aria-label ("Digit 1 of 6").
The first slot carries autocomplete="one-time-code" so SMS and password-manager autofill populate the whole code.
Digits always read left to right even in RTL layouts; ArrowLeft and ArrowRight move visually between slots.
do: Use a PIN input for fixed-length verification codes, authenticator tokens, backup codes and numeric PINs.
Group 6- or 8-character codes as [3, 3] or [4, 4] so people can scan and compare them at a glance.
Accept pasted codes containing spaces or dashes — connectPinInput strips them automatically.
dont: Don't use a PIN input for variable-length passwords or API keys — use Input.
Don't auto-submit destructive actions on completion without a way to review or cancel.

components.name: Filter bar
components.description: A bar that brings together everything needed to filter a list, table or feed: quick filter tabs, filter menus, search, and the filters currently applied with a way to clear them all.

ReactNode — number of active values selected for this facet

a11y: Quick filter tabs form a role="tablist" with an aria-label. Tabs announce aria-selected="true" when active.
Faceted filter triggers carry aria-haspopup="menu" (set by DropdownMenuTrigger) and aria-expanded for open/closed state.
Active filters provide removable chips with accessible remove labels ("Remove Status: Draft").
Visible :focus-visible rings on all interactive tabs, triggers, and action buttons.
High Contrast mode fills active tabs and outlines active triggers using system Highlight.
do: Use a filter bar above tables, cards, lists, and feeds that support filtering by multiple criteria.
Use quick filter tabs for primary mutually exclusive statuses (All, Drafts, Published) with live counts.
Use faceted filter triggers for secondary multi-select dimensions (Assignee, Priority, Label).
Display applied filters as removable chips with a Clear all button so users see and modify current filters in one glance.
dont: Don't build custom button rows or ad-hoc active classes for status filters — use FilterBarTabs and FilterBarTab.
Don't hide active filters inside menus without showing badges or active removable chips.
Don't disable the filter bar when there are zero results — let the user adjust filters to recover.

classes.ayy-sorting--sm: Compact size variant for tight toolbars and mobile viewports.
