components.name: Block editor
components.description: A document editor made of blocks: headings, lists, tables, callouts, code, images and files. Type / to add a block, and drag the gutter handle to reorder.

classes.ayy-block-editor: Root. The editor renders its blocks inside it, then the floating menu, formatting bar and caret anchor. Leave room at its inline start for the gutter (about 3.25rem of padding in its container), or use --inset.
classes.ayy-block-editor--inset: Keeps the gutter inside the editor's own box, for containers with no padding to hang it in.
classes.ayy-block-editor__block:
One block. data-type says what it is; data-indent (1–4) nests it, data-checked marks a done to-do, data-open a toggle showing the blocks nested under it (a closed one hides them), data-tone (info, success, warning, destructive) colours a callout, data-rendered an equation whose renderer returned HTML, data-selected a block in a block selection, data-dragging one being carried. In plain HTML you can write just
Title
; the editor builds the rest.
classes.ayy-block-editor__gutter: The + and the drag handle at the block's inline start; shown while the pointer is over the block (on touch screens, next to the line being written).
classes.ayy-block-editor__add: The + button: a new line below with / typed, so the block menu opens. Alt-click adds it above.
classes.ayy-block-editor__handle: The drag handle (.ayy-drag-handle): drag to move the block, or every selected block; click for block actions (duplicate, move, delete, turn into, and Colour › on a callout).
classes.ayy-block-editor__text: The editable line of a text block (contenteditable, role="textbox"). Inline content: strong, em, u, s, mark, code, links and mention chips. Shows data-placeholder while empty. An equation's line is named Equation; the TeX is its text. The line is clipped — not removed — while data-rendered math is showing.
classes.ayy-block-editor__marker: A list's bullet or number, drawn by the editor (1. a. i. by nesting level).
classes.ayy-block-editor__toggle: A toggle's arrow button: points along the reading direction, turns down while the toggle is open (aria-expanded). Blocks indented under the toggle (data-indent greater than its own) are hidden while it is closed.
classes.ayy-block-editor__table-wrap: A table block's box: the scrolling table, the row grips at its inline start, the drop line for a dragged row or column, the + at its inline end (add a column), the + under it (add a row) and the fit button in the corner between them. The box is as wide as the table, which is as wide as its columns.
classes.ayy-block-editor__table-scroll: Scrolls the table sideways in a narrow column, with room at the inline start and top for the row and column grips. The hairline is on the table, not this box.
classes.ayy-block-editor__table: The <table>. A header row is a <thead> of <th scope="col">; the rest is a <tbody>. A selected row or column paints data-selected on its cells. In plain HTML a block with data-type="table" can hold a <table> and the editor reads its rows.
classes.ayy-block-editor__cell: The editable plain-text line inside every cell (role="textbox", data-row, data-col). Tab and Shift+Tab move between cells, Enter goes down a row.
classes.ayy-block-editor__col-resize: The handle on a table column's inline-end edge, in the first row (role="separator"): drag it to set the column's width; the table shrinks and grows with it instead of staying as wide as the block. The same widths are set from the column grip's menu (Width) for keyboard users.
classes.ayy-block-editor__table-add: A table's + button (data-axis="column" or "row"): shown while the pointer or focus is in the block, always on touch screens.
classes.ayy-block-editor__table-fit: The table's fit-to-width button, in the corner under and after the table (aria-label="Fit table to width"): stretches or squeezes the columns, keeping their proportions, until the table is as wide as the block. A one-off — the widths stay as they are when the block later resizes. Shown while the pointer or focus is in the block, always on touch screens. Keyboard users get the same from the table menu's Fit to width.
classes.ayy-block-editor__row-grip: The handle at a table row's inline start (data-row, aria-haspopup="menu"): shown while the pointer is over that row, including the lane beside the table (data-hot). It hides when the pointer leaves the table. Click selects the row and opens its menu (insert, duplicate, move, clear, delete); drag reorders the row.
classes.ayy-block-editor__col-grip: The handle over a table column's top (data-col, aria-haspopup="menu"): shown while the pointer is over that column, including the lane above the table (data-hot). It hides when the pointer leaves the table. Click selects the column and opens its menu (insert, duplicate, move, sort, align, width, clear, delete); drag reorders the column.
classes.ayy-block-editor__icon: A callout's icon: a bulb by default, then information, check, alert or cancel as data-tone changes. It takes the tone's colour.
classes.ayy-block-editor__math: An equation's rendered output, a sibling after the TeX line, aria-hidden="true". Shown only while the block has data-rendered and is not being edited. Clicking it focuses the line. The line is named Equation and the TeX is its text; this HTML is hidden from screen readers.
classes.ayy-block-editor__code-bar: A code block's header, over the top of the code: the language at the start, Copy at the end (shown on hover).
classes.ayy-block-editor__code-button: A button in the code header: the language (opens a menu of languages; plain text in read-only) or Copy (a check while copied, data-copied).
classes.ayy-block-editor__media: The <figure> of an image or embed block.
classes.ayy-block-editor__frame: The box around an image, a player or a link card. data-ratio="video|audio|square" sizes a provider's player.
classes.ayy-block-editor__resize: The handle on an image's inline-end edge (role="separator"): drag, or use the arrow keys, to set its width.
classes.ayy-block-editor__caption: An image or embed's editable caption (also the image's alt text). Its placeholder shows on hover and focus.
classes.ayy-block-editor__bookmark: An embed of a page that isn't a player: a quiet card with the site and the address.
classes.ayy-block-editor__bookmark-title: The site's name in a link card.
classes.ayy-block-editor__bookmark-url: The address in a link card, truncated.
classes.ayy-block-editor__file: A file block: a link to download it, with its icon, name and size.
classes.ayy-block-editor__record: A record link: a button card (icon, name, source). Clicking it fires the mention click, in read-only too. With no record yet it says "Pick a record".
classes.ayy-block-editor__record-label: The record's name, stored on the block. Not looked up again if mentions later changes.
classes.ayy-block-editor__record-source: The trigger and id the record was linked from, muted. Empty until one is picked.
classes.ayy-block-editor__empty: An image, embed or file block with nothing in it yet: a muted panel with a link field and an Upload button. aria-busy="true" while a file uploads.
classes.ayy-block-editor__mention: A mention chip inside text (contenteditable="false", data-trigger, data-id, data-label): text with a faint wash, never a loud pill.
classes.ayy-block-editor__mention-trigger: The @ or # of a mention, muted.
classes.ayy-block-editor__menu: The floating list (.ayy-combobox__listbox) for /, mentions, block actions, a table row, column or cell menu, and a code block's language. data-mode="slash|mention|actions|language".
classes.ayy-block-editor__submenu: A menu that opens beside an item (Colour, Language, Row, Column, Sort, Align, Width), rather than replacing the list. A further one can open beside that.
classes.ayy-block-editor__menu-label: A group heading in the menu (Basic blocks, Media, People, Turn into).
classes.ayy-block-editor__option: One menu row (.ayy-combobox__option, role="option"). data-current marks a block's current type, data-destructive Delete.
classes.ayy-block-editor__option-icon: The tile in front of a menu row: the block type's icon, or an Avatar for a person.
classes.ayy-block-editor__option-text: A menu row's name and hint.
classes.ayy-block-editor__option-hint: A menu row's muted second line.
classes.ayy-block-editor__toolbar: The formatting bar (.ayy-toolbar--floating) over a text selection: bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, highlight, code, link. Over a link it shows the link's address.
classes.ayy-block-editor__link-form: The link field in the formatting bar, with Open and Remove.
classes.ayy-block-editor__anchor: A hidden box the script places over the caret or the selection for the menu and the bar to hang from.

default.looks: Plain text on the page: no borders or boxes; headings in --ayy-font-heading; lists, quotes, callouts and code in their own quiet styles. The gutter is hidden.

hover.looks: Its gutter (+ and the drag handle) fades in at the inline start; a hovered image shows its resize handle and its caption placeholder; gutter buttons, link cards, file rows and record cards get --ayy-color-wash.

pressed.none: No pressed look: pressing the handle starts a drag or opens block actions, pressing text places the caret.

focus.when: A line with the caret (:focus inside .ayy-block-editor__text), or the editor itself while blocks are selected; :focus-visible on the gutter buttons, the resize handle, link cards, file rows and record cards
focus.looks: The caret, and an empty line's hint (Type / for blocks). Selected blocks show their tint; buttons and handles get the 2px --ayy-color-ring outline.

disabled.none: Use readOnly to show a document that can't be edited.

selected.when: data-selected on blocks (Esc in a line, Shift+click, Mod+A twice, or the handle's menu) or on a table row's or column's td/th (its grip menu)
selected.looks: A 12% --ayy-color-primary tint behind the block or the selected cells; images, players, files and record cards also get the --ayy-color-ring outline. Forced colours: a Highlight outline.

error.none: No error look on the editor; a link that isn't a valid URL marks the link field (aria-invalid) instead. Say why a save failed in an Alert or a toast.

loading.when: aria-busy="true" on .ayy-block-editor__empty while a dropped, pasted or picked file uploads
loading.looks: The media panel dims to 60% and stops taking the pointer until the file's URL arrives.

checked.when: data-checked on a to-do block (its checkbox, or Mod+Enter in the line)
checked.looks: The checkbox is checked; the text turns --ayy-color-muted with a line through it.

open.when: data-open on a toggle block (its arrow, or Mod+Enter in the line)
open.looks: The arrow turns down and the blocks nested under the toggle show; closed, they are hidden (hidden attribute) but stay in the value.

tone.when: data-tone="info|success|warning|destructive" on a callout (Colour › in its block actions)
tone.looks: The wash becomes an 8% tint of --ayy-color-info, --ayy-color-success, --ayy-color-warning or --ayy-color-destructive, and the icon takes that colour. Default has no data-tone: --ayy-color-wash and a muted bulb. Forced colours: a CanvasText border and icon on Canvas.

resizing.when: data-active on .ayy-block-editor__col-resize while a table column is dragged
resizing.looks: A 2px --ayy-color-primary line shows on the column's edge; the columns follow the pointer live.

hot.when: data-hot on the grip of the row or column under the pointer, including the lanes beside and above the table
hot.looks: That grip fades in. It hides when the pointer leaves the table.

dragging.when: data-dragging on the blocks being carried by the handle, or on the cells of the table row or column being dragged by its grip
dragging.looks: They dim to 40%; a raised copy follows the pointer and drag-and-drop's 2px line (data-drop-edge) shows where they'll land.

empty.when: data-empty on the root: the document is one empty line
empty.looks: The placeholder shows in that line, focused or not.

typing.when: data-typing on the root: set by typing, cleared when the pointer moves or presses
typing.looks: The gutters and code blocks' Copy fade out, so nothing moves beside the words being written.

read-only.when: readOnly / the readonly attribute (aria-readonly="true" on the root)
read-only.looks: No gutter, carets, placeholders or empty media panels; checkboxes are disabled, links, mentions and record cards open on click.

sizes.density: Text follows the type scale (body --ayy-text-md, headings 3xl, 2xl and xl), not density. Menu rows, the formatting bar and the media panel's field and button follow the control sizes, so data-density="touch" makes them bigger; the gutter buttons stay 1.5rem.
sizes.width: Fills its container; images and embeds fill the column (an image can be resized from 20% to 100%). The gutter hangs about 3.25rem outside the inline start, or inside with --inset.

components.js:
blockEditorClass({ inset?, className? }) → string; connectBlockEditor(root, { value?, placeholder?, label?, readOnly?, mentions?, upload?, renderMath?, onChange?, onMentionClick? }) → { getValue, setValue, setOptions, focus, destroy }; blockEditorBlock(type, fields?) makes a block; blockEditorNormalize(value) cleans one; blockEditorToMarkdown, blockEditorFromMarkdown, blockEditorToHtml and blockEditorToText convert (no DOM needed); a callout's tone is info, success, warning or destructive (absent is default; Markdown uses GitHub alerts, [!NOTE] [!TIP] [!WARNING] [!CAUTION], and [!IMPORTANT] imports as info); blockEditorMentionHtml({ trigger, id, label }) is a mention chip for a block's html; blockEditorCodeLanguages lists the languages a code block offers (block.language holds the id, highlighted with Code block's tokenizer); blockEditorEmbed(url) says what an embed block shows; blockEditorCleanHtml(html) keeps only the inline HTML the editor makes. A record block stores { trigger, id, label } and exports as trigger plus label in text and Markdown, and as

label

in HTML; Markdown import does not turn that text back into a record block. An equation block stores escaped TeX; Markdown is a $$ fence, HTML is
\[tex\]
, and renderMath(tex) supplies the shown HTML.

element.description:
Makes the .ayy-block-editor inside it a block editor. The starting blocks are the ones written inside it (short form:
Done
) or a
element.children: A <div class="ayy-block-editor"> of blocks, and optionally a <script type="application/json" data-mentions> with mention lists.

attributes.placeholder: Shown while the document is empty.
attributes.label: Accessible name of the editor (default "Editor").
attributes.readonly: Show the document without editing it.

events.ayy-change: { value } — every block, after each change.
events.ayy-mention-click: { trigger, id, label } — a mention chip or a record card was clicked.

BlockEditor.renders: <div class="ayy-block-editor"> that the editor fills with blocks

props.value: BlockEditorBlock[] — the document, controlled (pass back what onChange gives you).
props.defaultValue: BlockEditorBlock[] — the document to start with, uncontrolled.
props.placeholder: string — shown while the document is empty.
props.readOnly: boolean — show the document without editing it.
props.mentions: BlockEditorMentionSource[] — { trigger, label?, options } per trigger; options is a list of { id, label, hint?, avatar? } or a (query) => list or Promise of one.
props.upload: (file: File) => string | Promise<string> — store a pasted, dropped or picked file, return its URL. Default: a data: URL.
props.renderMath: (tex: string) => string — turn an equation block's TeX into HTML. Without it, the TeX shows as typed. A throw or an empty result shows the TeX.
props.onMentionClick: (mention: { trigger, id, label }, event: MouseEvent) => void
props.inset: boolean — keep the gutter inside the editor's box.
props.aria-label: string — accessible name of the editor (default "Editor").

a11y: Name the editor (aria-label in React, label on <ayy-block-editor>): it's a role="group" of lines, each a role="textbox" named by its type (Text, Heading 1, To-do list).

Everything works from the keyboard: Enter, Backspace and the arrows move through blocks; Tab and Shift+Tab nest; Mod+Enter opens or closes a toggle, whose arrow is not a tab stop; in a table Tab and Shift+Tab move between cells (Tab in the last one adds a row), Enter goes down a row and adds one after the last, Mod+Enter adds a row below, the arrows leave the table at its first and last row, Mod+Shift+arrows move the row or column (dragging its grip does the same), a cell's Mod+/ or right-click opens its menu (Row ›, Column ›, Header row, Header column, Clear every cell, then the block actions), the row and column grips open a menu scoped to that row or column and select it (insert, duplicate, move, clear, delete — columns also sort, align and set width), and the block handle's menu holds the table-wide items (→ opens a group, ← or Esc goes back); a callout's block actions include Colour › (Default, Info, Success, Warning, Destructive); Esc selects the block (then ↑/↓, Shift+↑/↓, Delete, Mod+D, Mod+Shift+↑/↓, Enter to edit again); Mod+/ opens block actions, Mod+Alt+0–8 turns a block into another type, Mod+B/I/U, Mod+Shift+S, Mod+Shift+H (highlight), Mod+E and Mod+K format. Tab nests, so the way out of the editor is Esc twice, then Tab.
Screen readers hear an equation's TeX, not its rendered math: the text line stays available (named Equation) and the rendered HTML is hidden.

The / and mention menus keep focus in the line: ↑/↓ move through aria-activedescendant, Enter or Tab picks, Esc closes without closing a parent Dialog. The block actions menu takes focus and gives it back.

Opening a row or column grip's menu selects that row or column (Esc closes the menu and leaves it selected). Delete or Backspace clears it, Mod+Backspace or Mod+Delete deletes it, Mod+D duplicates it, Mod+Shift+arrows move it (left and right follow the reading direction), Mod+C copies it (a row is tab-separated, a column is one value per line), Mod+X copies then clears it, and Esc puts the caret in its first cell. Clicking a cell clears the selection.
Block selections, moves and failed uploads are read out in a polite live region.
Images take their caption as alt text: write one for every picture that carries meaning.
do: Use a Block editor for documents people write and come back to: notes on a task, a page in a wiki, a spec, a long description with headings, lists, to-dos and media.
Store the value (blocks) as it is, or convert it with blockEditorToMarkdown / blockEditorFromMarkdown when the storage is Markdown, and render it elsewhere with blockEditorToHtml.
Pass mentions for the people and records your app has (@ for people, # for issues), with a function when the list is long or remote.
Pass upload so pasted, dropped and picked files go to your storage instead of the default data: URLs.
Pass renderMath (for example KaTeX's renderToString) so equation blocks show as math, and keep that library in your app so ayywi's bundle stays small.

Keep tables for short, plain facts (a price list, a schedule). Cells are plain text, one line each, up to 100 rows and 12 columns; a spreadsheet pasted into a cell fills the cells from there. A new table is two columns, only as wide as they are; drag a column's edge to size it, and use the corner button to fit the table to the block's width.
dont: Don't use a Block editor for a short reply, a comment or a single field — use Textarea, or Mentions when the text needs @mentions.
Don't wrap it in a bordered box like an input: it's the page. Put it straight in the page or a Card, with room at its inline start for the gutter (or --inset).
Don't trust a value from elsewhere as HTML: pass it through the editor or blockEditorNormalize, which keep only the inline HTML it makes.

components.name: Inline edit
components.description: A value that becomes an input where it sits: a page or card title, a project name, a version, a due date. Click it or press Enter to edit, Enter saves, Esc cancels, blur saves, and a multiline field grows as you type and saves on Mod+Enter.

classes.ayy-inline-edit: Root: one grid cell shared by the display button and the field, both at least the control's height, so swapping them doesn't move the content for a one-line value. Put the raw value in data-value.
classes.ayy-inline-edit__display: The value at rest, as a <button type="button"> named by aria-label ("Rename the project"). It is hidden while the field is open.
classes.ayy-inline-edit__text: The value inside the display button. It may be formatted (24 Oct 2026 while data-value is 2026-10-24); when empty, data-placeholder shows as muted text.
classes.ayy-inline-edit__input: The field: .ayy-input for one line or .ayy-textarea with rows="1" for more. Hidden until editing starts.
classes.ayy-inline-edit--title: Title variant: the display and the field take --ayy-font-heading at --ayy-text-xl, semibold.

default.looks: The value as plain text on a transparent button; a small wash appears on hover. The field is hidden in the same grid cell.

hover.looks: A --ayy-color-wash behind the value, so it reads as editable. The field keeps Input's or Textarea's own hover border.

pressed.none: No pressed look: the click opens the field, which is the feedback.

focus.looks: The display gets the 2px --ayy-color-ring outline at 2px offset; the field uses Input's or Textarea's own ring.

disabled.when: disabled on the display button and the field
disabled.looks: --ayy-opacity-disabled and a not-allowed cursor. Forced colours: GrayText.

selected.none: Not a choice control.

error.when: aria-invalid="true" on the field (passed through inputProps or textareaProps)
error.looks: Input's or Textarea's destructive border and focus ring. Say why in a FieldError.

loading.none: No loading look. Disable the field while a save is in flight and show a Spinner or a Toast when it fails.

editing.when: editing / defaultEditing, or a click or Enter on the display button
editing.looks: The display is hidden and the field takes the same grid cell at the control's height, focused with all its text selected (caret at the end on a textarea). A textarea then grows with its content.

sizes.density: The display button and the field both keep --ayy-size-control-md (32px compact, 40px comfortable, 44px touch), so a one-line value doesn't move the row when an edit starts or ends; the field's text is --ayy-control-text-field. The title variant's --ayy-text-xl type stays the same at every density.
sizes.width: Fills its container. The display text wraps long words, keeps the author's line breaks and never scrolls sideways; a multiline field grows to its content.

components.js: inlineEditClass({ variant?, className? }) → root classes; inlineEditVariants; isComposingEvent(event) → true during IME composition; commitsOnEnter(event, multiline?) → whether that Enter saves; growInlineEdit(textarea) → size a textarea to its content; connectInlineEdit(root, { onCommit?, onCancel?, onEditingChange?, trim? }) → { start, commit, cancel, isEditing, destroy } wires plain markup.

element.description: Wraps an .ayy-inline-edit and makes it work: the display button opens the field, Enter saves (Mod+Enter in a textarea), Esc cancels and blur saves. The markup decides whether the field is an <input> or a <textarea>. A commit writes the value back to data-value and .ayy-inline-edit__text only when it changed; an app showing formatted text listens for ayy-change and rewrites the text itself. startEditing(), commit() and cancel() drive it from code.

events.ayy-change: { value } — after a commit, only when the value changed. Update any formatted display text from it.
events.ayy-edit: { editing } — true when the field opens, false however it closes.

InlineEdit.renders: <div class="ayy-inline-edit" data-value> <button class="ayy-inline-edit__display"><span class="ayy-inline-edit__text"> + <input class="ayy-input ayy-inline-edit__input"> (or <textarea class="ayy-textarea ..." rows="1">)

props.value / defaultValue: string — the raw value; value makes it controlled
props.onValueChange: (value: string) => void — after a commit, only when the value changed
props.label: string — the display button's and the field's aria-label, written as the action ("Rename the project")
props.displayValue: ReactNode — what the display shows at rest; defaults to the value (a formatted date, a price)
props.placeholder: string — shown when the value is empty, in the display and in the field
props.multiline: boolean — use a growing <textarea>; saves on ⌘Enter / Ctrl+Enter
props.disabled: boolean — disables the display button and the field
props.editing / defaultEditing: boolean — edit mode, controlled, or the starting one
props.onEditingChange: (editing: boolean) => void — when edit mode starts or ends
props.onCancel: () => void — Esc threw the draft away
props.trim: boolean — trim the value on commit. Default true
props.inputProps: props for the single-line <input> (id, aria-describedby, aria-invalid, autoComplete…)
props.className: string — on the root, never on the field

a11y: The display is a real button and the field is a real input: give both the same aria-label (label in React), written as the action ("Rename the project"), and keep it when the value changes.
Enter saves, Esc cancels and puts focus back on the display button; blur and Tab save without pulling focus back.
Enter while an IME is composing is left to the IME, so a Japanese, Chinese or Korean word can be confirmed without saving.
The empty value shows the placeholder as text, not as the only name: the button keeps its aria-label.
do: Use inline edit for a short value people rename in place: a page title, a project or file name, a version, a due date.
Write the label as the action ("Rename the project"), and keep a formatted displayValue in React when the raw value isn't what people should read.
Keep the raw value in data-value (plain HTML) and format only the .ayy-inline-edit__text.
dont: Don't use it for long-form content or a value filled once in a form — use Field + Label with a Textarea or Input.
Don't put formatted text in data-value: the field edits the raw value, and the app rewrites the display from ayy-change.
Don't use it for a value that needs more than one field — open a Dialog or use Settings rows.

components.name: Select
components.description: A dropdown for choosing one option from a list. It's the native select with a nicer list on desktop, and the system picker on touch devices.

classes.ayy-select: Wrapper element. Draws the chevron and sets the height.
classes.ayy-select__list: The options list (role="listbox" popover) that React Select and "@danitesler/ayywi/elements" build from the <option>s while it's open. Don't write it yourself.
classes.ayy-select__option: One option in the list (role="option"); aria-selected="true" on the chosen one, aria-disabled for a disabled <option>.
classes.ayy-select__picture: A picture for one option (a theme thumbnail, "Aa" in a font, a colour): a <span aria-hidden="true" data-value="<the option's value>"> after the <select> in the wrapper, one per option, all but the chosen one hidden. The chosen one shows at the control's inline start (32×20px); the list shows each before its option's text (88px wide, 16:10). It's a frame (border, tint, rounded) and a size container, so what's inside can size itself in container units.

default.looks: Native <select> with a wash fill, line-strong border and a muted chevron at the inline end.

hover.looks: Border turns line-hover; an option in the list gets the wash-hover background.

pressed.none: Pressing opens the options list (the OS picker on touch screens); the list shows the state.

focus.looks: 2px ring just inside the edge; the border goes transparent. In the list the focused option gets the wash-hover background, plus a 2px ring inset by 2px from the keyboard. Forced colours: Highlight fill.

disabled.when: .ayy-select__control:disabled; a disabled <option> (aria-disabled on its list option)
disabled.looks: Control and chevron dim to --ayy-opacity-disabled, not-allowed cursor; a disabled option dims the same way and the arrow keys skip it.

selected.looks: The chosen option shows as the control's text (and its picture, when the select has pictures); in the list it's semibold with a check at the inline end.

error.looks: Border 60% destructive, destructive focus ring. Forced colours: dashed border.

loading.none: No loading look; disable it with a "Loading…" option until the options arrive, or use a Skeleton for the form.

open.looks: Border turns line-hover and the chevron points up; the list fades in and scales up from 97% under the select (above it when there's no room), at least as wide, at most 20rem tall with its own scroll.

multiple.looks: Renders a list box: no fixed height, no chevron, no options list.

scale.sm: Control sm height (28px compact, 32 comfortable, 40 touch), sm text.
scale.md: Control md height (32px compact, 40 comfortable, 44 touch).
scale.lg: Control lg height (40px compact, 48 comfortable, 52 touch), lg text.

sizes.density: Height and text follow data-density.
sizes.width: Fills its container; long option text is cut with an ellipsis. The list is at least the select's width and at most 24rem; its options are the md control height, or as tall as their picture (up to 32rem of list) with pictures.

components.js: selectClass({ size?, className? }) → string for the wrapper; selectControlClass, selectListClass, selectOptionClass, selectLabelClass constants; openSelectListFrom(event) opens the list from a mousedown or keydown on a select (what React Select and "@danitesler/ayywi/elements" call); openSelectList(select) opens it directly; usesSelectList(select) says whether a select gets the list here; selectPictureClass, selectPicture(select, value) and syncSelectPicture(select) (shows the chosen option's picture; @danitesler/ayywi/elements calls it on change). Choosing from ayywi's list fires input and change when the value changes, then a bubbling ayy-choose event (detail.value) on the select for every choice, the option already chosen included

props.pictures: Record<string, ReactNode> — a picture per option value: rendered as .ayy-select__picture spans after the <select>; the chosen one shows before the text and the list shows each
props.onChoose: (value: string) => void — every choice from ayywi's list, the option already chosen included (onChange only fires for a new one), for an option that acts each time, such as Custom colour
props....rest: All native <select> attributes and events (onChange fires when an option is chosen from the list too); className goes to the <select>.

a11y: Label it like any input (Field + Label with for/id); the list takes the same name.
The list is a role="listbox" of role="option"s: arrows, Home/End and type-ahead move, Enter, Space or a click chooses, Esc, Tab or a click outside closes, and focus goes back to the select.
Touch screens keep the OS picker, which suits them better. Don't build your own dropdown for choosing a value: this is it.
Pictures are aria-hidden: an option's text names it, in the list and in the OS picker.
do: Use a select to choose one option from a longer list (country, time zone, role).
Put a sensible default first, or a disabled placeholder option.
Write a plain <select> with <option>s (or React Select): the list comes with it. In plain HTML load elements.global.js (or import "@danitesler/ayywi/elements").

Give options pictures when the choice is visual (a theme, a font, a colour): one .ayy-select__picture per option (React: pictures). Phones keep the OS picker with text only, so the option text must still say what it is.
dont: Don't use a select for 2–5 options that should all be visible — use Radio, or a Segmented control when the choice changes a view.
Don't use a select for actions — use a Dropdown menu.
Don't build a custom dropdown (a button opening a div of choices, a Dropdown menu used as a picker) — use Select, or a Combobox when people should type to filter.
Don't use a select to search thousands of options — put a search Input group above a List of results instead.
Don't use a select for yes/no — use a Switch or Checkbox.

components.name: Combobox
components.description: A text field that filters a list as you type, for picking one option from a long set like a city, a customer or a time zone. The options open under the field and follow the standard accessible pattern.

classes.ayy-combobox: Wrapper: the .ayy-input (role="combobox"), a chevron <svg> and the listbox.
classes.ayy-combobox__listbox: The <ul role="listbox" popover="manual"> of options, placed under the input.
classes.ayy-combobox__option: An <li role="option">. data-value is what it stands for, data-label what goes in the input, data-keywords more words that match. aria-selected="true" on the one the arrow keys are on; aria-disabled for one you can't pick.
classes.ayy-combobox__meta: Extra text at the end of an option (a country, a count). Not put in the input.
classes.ayy-combobox__empty: The "No matches" line (role="none"), shown when nothing matches.

default.looks: An Input with a muted chevron at the inline end; the list is a raised popover with the overlay shadow.

hover.looks: Option gets the wash-hover background (the input hovers like Input).

pressed.none: Options have no pressed look: clicking picks one and closes the list.

focus.looks: Input's ring. Focus stays in the input while the arrow keys move through options (see selected).

disabled.looks: Option dims to --ayy-opacity-disabled with a not-allowed cursor; a disabled input dims like Input.

selected.looks: The option under the arrow keys gets the wash-hover background. Forced colours: Highlight fill.

error.looks: Input's red border and ring.

loading.none: No loading look; while results load, show .ayy-combobox__empty with "Searching…".

open.looks: The list fades in under the input, at most 18rem (or half the viewport) tall, then scrolls.

empty.looks: Muted "No results" row when every option is filtered out.

scale.sm: The input at Input sm.
scale.md: The input at Input md.
scale.lg: The input at Input lg.

sizes.density: Input height (md control height, 32px compact, 40 comfortable, 44 touch) and options (sm control height, 28px compact, 32 comfortable, 40 touch) follow data-density.
sizes.width: Fills its container; the list is at most 28rem wide.

components.js: connectCombobox(input, listbox, { onSelect?(option | null), filter? }) → { open, close, refresh, destroy } wires the pattern on plain markup; comboboxOptionLabel(option) and comboboxOptionByValue(listbox, value) read options; comboboxChevronIcon (SVG markup) and part class constants.

element.description: Wraps an .ayy-combobox and wires typing, filtering, the arrow keys, Enter and Esc on its input and listbox.

attributes.manual: Don't filter: replace the options yourself as people type (a search API), then call refresh().

events.ayy-select: { value, label, option } when an option is chosen — value is its data-value, else its label.

props.options: ({ value, label, meta?, icon?, keywords?, disabled? } | string)[]
props.onValueChange: (value: string, option: ComboboxOption | null) => void — ("", null) once when the field is cleared
props.onInputChange: (text: string) => void — every keystroke, e.g. to fetch options
props.filter: boolean, default true; false when you fetch the options yourself
props.name: string — a hidden input carries the chosen value in forms

a11y: Focus stays in the input: Down opens the list and moves through it, Up goes back, Enter picks, Esc closes (and a second Esc clears), Alt+Down opens without moving. Screen readers follow aria-activedescendant.
Label the input with a <label for> its id; the chevron is decoration.
Typing highlights the first match, so Enter picks it; options that don't match are hidden, and "No matches" shows when none do.
do: Use a combobox to pick one of many known values: more than ten or so, where people know what they're looking for (a city, a customer, a time zone).
Give options keywords for the other words people type (the country for a city, the email for a customer), and meta for what helps tell them apart.
For results from a server, set filter={false} (or manual on <ayy-combobox>) and replace the options on each keystroke.
dont: Don't use a combobox for fewer than about ten options — use Select, or a Segmented control for two to five.
Don't use it for actions — use a Dropdown menu.
Don't use it for free text that may not be in the list — use an Input (a datalist can suggest).

components.name: Tag input
components.description: A field that turns what you type into removable chips, for tags, labels or email recipients. It can also suggest options as you type.

classes.ayy-tag-input: Root: looks like an .ayy-input, holds the chips then the input, and grows to more lines as needed. Clicking its empty space focuses the input. With suggestions add ayy-combobox and put an .ayy-combobox__listbox inside.
classes.ayy-tag-input__tag: A tag, on an .ayy-chip.ayy-chip--removable <span data-value> with its .ayy-chip__remove button (aria-label "Remove design").
classes.ayy-tag-input__input: The borderless <input type="text"> after the chips; the field's id, label and aria-describedby go on it.

default.looks: An Input-like wash field with a line-strong border, holding removable chips and a text box that grows onto more lines as tags are added.

hover.looks: Border turns line-hover.

pressed.none: No pressed look; a click puts the caret in the text box.

focus.looks: A 2px ring around the whole field; each chip's × has its own. Forced colours: Highlight.

disabled.looks: --ayy-opacity-disabled, not-allowed cursor. Disable the chips' × buttons too.

selected.looks: The suggestion under the arrow keys gets Combobox's wash; suggestions that are already tags are aria-disabled.

error.looks: A destructive border (and ring while focused). Say why in a FieldError.

loading.none: No loading look in the field. While suggestions load, show the Combobox's "Searching…" row.

open.looks: Suggestions open under the field like a Combobox's list.

scale.sm: At least the sm control height (28px compact, 32 comfortable, 40 touch), sm text.
scale.md: At least the md control height (32px compact, 40 comfortable, 44 touch).
scale.lg: At least the lg control height (40px compact, 48 comfortable, 52 touch), more padding, lg text.

sizes.density: The first line's height follows data-density (above); each line of tags adds a chip's height.
sizes.width: Fills its container; tags wrap.

components.js: splitTags(text) → tags split at commas and new lines; addTags(values, add, { max?, caseSensitive? }) → values with the new ones appended (no duplicates, ignoring case); tagChip(value, removeLabel?) → a chip element; tagInputClass({ size?, suggestions?, className? }); tagRemoveIcon (SVG markup). connectTagInput(root, { name?, max?, caseSensitive?, onChange?, removeLabel?, addedText?, removedText? }) → { values, setValues, destroy } wires plain markup and draws the chips.

element.description: Wraps an .ayy-tag-input and makes it work: it draws a chip for each added tag (chips already in the HTML are the starting tags), keeps one hidden input per tag for forms, wires the suggestions listbox if there is one, and announces each change. The values property reads and sets the tags.

attributes.name: Form name: a hidden input per tag carries it.
attributes.case-sensitive: Keep tags that differ only in case apart.

events.ayy-change: { values } — every tag, after one is added or removed.

TagInput.renders: <div class="ayy-tag-input"> chips + <input class="ayy-tag-input__input"> (+ a listbox with suggestions); other props go on the input, className on the root

props.suggestions: string[] — known tags listed as you type; added ones show disabled
props.emptyText: ReactNode — in the suggestions list when nothing matches. Default "Press Enter to add it"
props.name: string — a hidden input per tag

a11y: Label the inner input with <Label htmlFor> on its id and describe how to add a tag in a FieldHint ("Press Enter or type a comma").
Each chip's × is a real button named "Remove design"; Backspace in the empty field removes the last tag too.
Adding and removing are announced in a polite live region ("design added"), and focus stays in the input.
With suggestions the input is a combobox: arrows move through them, Enter adds the highlighted one, and ones already added are aria-disabled.
do: Use it for a short open list of free text: tags, labels, keywords, email recipients.
Offer the tags people already use as suggestions so they don't create near-duplicates.
Set max when there's a limit, and say it in the hint.
Check each tag (an email address) in onValueChange and show a FieldError for a bad one.
dont: Don't use it to pick from a fixed set — use Checkbox chips (Chip) or a multi-select list.
Don't use it for a single value — use an Input or a Combobox.
Don't colour tags by meaning without a word for it.

components.name: Record picker
components.description: A tag field whose chips are records picked from a list: one person to assign, many labels to apply. Type to filter, Enter picks the active record, Backspace in the empty field removes the last, and a create row turns new text into a record.

classes.ayy-record-picker: Root: an ayy-tag-input and ayy-combobox holding the chips, the input, the clear button and the listbox.
classes.ayy-record-picker--multiple: Several records: chips wrap, and the list stays open after each pick (aria-multiselectable).
classes.ayy-record-picker__tag: One picked record, an .ayy-chip--removable.ayy-tag-input__tag <span data-value> with a named .ayy-chip__remove button; the label shrinks so the × stays inside.
classes.ayy-record-picker__tag-label: The record's name inside a chip: it shrinks and ellipsises when the name is longer than the field, instead of pushing the × out.
classes.ayy-record-picker__input: The borderless <input role="combobox"> after the chips; the field's id, label and aria-describedby go on it.
classes.ayy-record-picker__clear: The icon button after the input that clears every chip, named by aria-label ("Clear"); hidden while nothing is picked.
classes.ayy-record-picker__listbox: The .ayy-combobox__listbox: records, the create row and the empty row. At least as wide as the field; at most 24rem unless the field is wider.
classes.ayy-record-picker__option: One record, an .ayy-combobox__option[role="option"] with data-value, data-label and data-keywords. Active: data-active="true"; picked: aria-selected="true" and a check.
classes.ayy-record-picker__option-body: The two lines after the icon: name and description. Takes the row's leftover width.
classes.ayy-record-picker__option-label: The record's name, one line with an ellipsis.
classes.ayy-record-picker__description: The muted second line (an email, a role, a key), one line with an ellipsis.
classes.ayy-record-picker__create: The last option: "Create “Maya”" when creatable, the query isn't empty and no record matches exactly.
classes.ayy-record-picker__create-label: The create row's text, written by the controller from createLabel.
classes.ayy-record-picker__empty: The muted, centred row when nothing matches ("No people").

do: Use it to attach records to something: an assignee, labels, projects, reviewers.

a11y: Grids and time columns are single Tab stops. Arrow keys move selection within grids or columns.
State is reflected in aria-pressed, aria-selected, aria-current="date", and aria-disabled.
Month headers use aria-live="polite" so page changes are announced to screen readers.
Buttons have full accessible labels (e.g. "Wednesday, 7 October 2026").
High contrast mode (forced-colors: active) renders solid system borders and highlight backgrounds.
do: Use DatePicker or DatePickerGrid for picking a single date near today.
Use DateRange or DateRangePicker for date spans (stays, bookings, analytics intervals).
Use TimePicker or TimePickerTrigger for picking discrete hours and minutes.
Use DateTimePicker or DateTimePickerTrigger when both date and time must be chosen together.
dont: Don't build custom month grids or time dropdowns by hand.
Don't use DatePicker for birth dates (native <input type="date"> is faster to type).
Don't put a single date picker into a full-screen modal; keep it in a popover.

components.js: colorPickerClass({ className? }) → string; connectColorPicker(root, { value?, alpha?, swatches?, onChange? }) → { setValue, update, destroy } wires the 2D area, sliders, hex input and preset swatches; hsvToRgb(hsv), rgbToHsv(rgb), rgbToHex(rgb), hexToRgb(hex) conversion functions.

element.description: Wraps an .ayy-color-picker: wires its 2D saturation/brightness area (pointer drag and arrow keys), hue and alpha sliders, hex input, and preset swatch buttons ([data-color]).

attributes.value: Hex colour code ("#2563eb"). Updated when the colour changes.
attributes.name: Form name: a hidden input inside carries the hex colour.

props.onValueChange: (color: string) => void — called when the colour changes
props.alpha: boolean — whether to show the alpha slider and allow opacity changes
props.swatches: string[] — list of preset colour hex codes
props.addon: ReactNode — optional text or element beside the hex input (e.g. "HEX")
props.addonPosition: "start" | "end" — placement of the addon beside the input (default "end")
props.copyable: boolean — whether to show a copy button inside the hex input group

a11y: The 2D saturation/brightness area is a focusable role="slider" with aria-label, aria-valuetext, and arrow key navigation (Shift for 10% steps).
Hue and alpha sliders are native range inputs with accessible labels, keyboard stepped navigation, and Home/End support.
The hex input allows typing exact hex color codes with keyboard and screen reader support.
In Windows High Contrast mode, the panel, sliders, swatches, and handle keep clear outlines using CanvasText and Highlight system colors.
do: Use ColorPicker when people need to pick any custom colour or fine-tune hues, saturation, and transparency (e.g. in graphic design tools, theme customizers, or canvas drawing apps).
Provide preset swatches for common or brand-approved choices so users don't have to start from scratch.
Enable alpha only when transparency is supported by the underlying target.
dont: Don't use ColorPicker when users only choose between a small, fixed set of options — use Swatch or Segmented control instead.
Don't use ColorPicker for status or severity selection (e.g. error, warning) — use Badge or Select.
Don't hide what the color applies to — label the field with a clear label or preview.

components.name: Icon picker
components.description: A searchable grid of icons and emoji with a remove button, for marking a column, project, page or label with a symbol. It sits in a Popover or as the submenu panel of a Menu.

classes.ayy-icon-picker: Root: a flex column, 17rem wide at most, holding the header, the scrolling body and the empty message.
classes.ayy-icon-picker__header: Row with the search field and the remove button.
classes.ayy-icon-picker__search: The <input type="search" class="ayy-input ayy-input--sm"> that filters options by aria-label, data-keywords and data-value. ArrowDown moves into the grid, Enter picks the first match.
classes.ayy-icon-picker__remove: A ghost sm Button that clears the icon (picks "").
classes.ayy-icon-picker__body: The scrolling area (15rem tall at most) holding the sections.
classes.ayy-icon-picker__section: One <div role="group" aria-labelledby> per kind (icons, emoji). Hidden while a search leaves it no options.
classes.ayy-icon-picker__grid: The grid of options: as many sm-control-sized columns as fit.
classes.ayy-icon-picker__option: One <button type="button" aria-label aria-pressed data-value> holding an Icon SVG or an emoji character. data-keywords adds search words.
classes.ayy-icon-picker__empty:
The

shown when a search matches nothing.

default.looks: Options are transparent squares at the sm control height, icons and emoji in --ayy-color-text-soft, under muted section labels.

hover.looks: A --ayy-color-wash-hover fill and the text colour.

pressed.looks: The --ayy-color-wash-hover fill, also on touch screens.

focus.when: .ayy-icon-picker__option:focus-visible; the search field and remove button use Input's and Button's
focus.looks: A 2px --ayy-color-ring outline with a 2px offset.

disabled.looks: --ayy-opacity-disabled and a not-allowed cursor; skipped by the arrow keys. GrayText in High Contrast.

selected.looks: A --ayy-color-primary tint at 16% with a 1px primary ring at 60%, and the text colour. A Highlight outline in High Contrast.

error.none: Picking can't fail; a search with no matches shows the empty message instead.

loading.none: Options are local; nothing to wait for.

sizes.density: Options are the sm control height (28px compact, 32px comfortable, 40px touch) and the search field is an sm Input, so data-density grows the targets.
sizes.width: 17rem at most (shrinks with its container); the grid fits as many columns as the width allows and the body scrolls past 15rem.

components.js: iconPickerClass({ className? }) → string; iconPickerOptionClass and the other part constants; iconPickerEmojis (a starter set of { value, label, keywords }); connectIconPicker(root, { onChange?, manageSelection? }) → { setValue, filter, refresh, destroy } wires search, the roving tab stop, arrow keys and picking. Every pick dispatches a bubbling "ayy-pick" event ({ value, kind, option }) from the root; a Menu around the picker closes on it.

element.description: Wraps an .ayy-icon-picker: search filters the options, the arrow keys, Home and End move through the grid, and clicking an option or the remove button picks it and sets aria-pressed.

attributes.value: The picked option's data-value ("" for none). Updated on pick.
attributes.name: Form name: a hidden input inside carries the value.

events.ayy-change: { value, kind } — kind is "icon", "emoji", or null when removed.

IconPicker.renders: <div class="ayy-icon-picker"> with a search Input, a remove Button and a section per kind

props.value / defaultValue: string — the picked icon value or emoji; "" for none
props.onValueChange: (value: string, change: { value, kind, option }) => void
props.icons: { value: string; label: string; icon: IconData | ReactNode; name?: IconName; keywords?: string[] }[] — the Icons section; omit for emoji only. name is the glyph's name ("star"), written as data-ayy-icon so an icon pack can replace it
props.emojis: { value: string; label: string; keywords?: string[] }[] — the Emoji section (iconPickerEmojis by default; [] hides it)
props.searchable: boolean — show the search field (default true)
props.removable: boolean — show the remove button (default true)
props.iconsLabel / emojisLabel / searchLabel /: string — the visible and accessible text

a11y: Every option is a <button> with an aria-label naming the icon or emoji (an emoji character alone is read inconsistently) and aria-pressed for the picked one, so the choice is announced, not only tinted.

Each section is a role="group" labelled by its heading. One option is the tab stop (the picked one, or the first): Tab moves search → grid → remove, and the arrow keys, Home and End move inside the grid, mirrored in RTL.

ArrowDown from the search field enters the grid and ArrowUp from the first row returns to it; Enter in the search field picks the first match. A no-match search announces the role="status" empty message.

Keys stay inside the picker except Esc, so a Menu or Popover around it still closes on Esc and returns focus. As a menu's submenu panel, give the panel role="dialog" and an aria-label, put it after the menu rather than inside it (a menu holds only items), and give the trigger aria-haspopup="dialog".
do: Use an icon picker to let people mark a column, project, page or label with an icon or emoji of their choice.
Offer a short, relevant icon set (the same Hugeicons the app uses) and keep the emoji section for personal flair.
Give every option a plain label and keywords, so search finds "money" under Dollar and 💰.
dont: Don't use an icon picker to choose a status, category or other fixed value with meaning — use Select, Segmented control or Swatch.
Don't list icons as one menu item each once there are more than a handful — the grid and search scale, a menu doesn't.
Don't show the picked icon without its label elsewhere when the icon carries meaning; icons are a hint, not the name.

components.name: Checkbox
components.description: A box for turning an option on or off, or for picking several items from a list. It's the native checkbox with a clearer look, and it can show a mixed state when only some of a group is selected.

classes.ayy-checkbox: On <input type="checkbox">. Draws the box and mark; size follows density.
classes.ayy-checkbox--sm: Small box (--ayy-size-check-sm). The label that wraps it, or sits beside it in an inline Field, takes the small control text.
classes.ayy-checkbox--lg: Large box (--ayy-size-check-lg) and large label text.

default.looks: A box --ayy-size-check square with a line-hover border (or --ayy-check-color) on a wash fill.

hover.looks: Border turns text-soft.

pressed.none: No pressed look; it toggles on release.

focus.looks: 2px ring, 2px offset.

disabled.looks: --ayy-opacity-disabled, not-allowed cursor. Forced colours: GrayText border (and fill when checked).

selected.looks: Primary fill and border (or --ayy-check-color) with a primary-fg tick (or --ayy-check-fg) that springs in.

error.looks: Destructive border. Forced colours: dashed.

loading.none: Toggles are instant; if saving fails, revert it and say so in a toast.

indeterminate.looks: Primary fill with a bar instead of the tick: some of a group selected.

scale.sm: --ayy-size-check-sm: 14px compact, 16 comfortable, 18 touch.
scale.md: --ayy-size-check: 16px compact, 18 comfortable, 20 touch.
scale.lg: --ayy-size-check-lg: 20px compact, 22 comfortable, 24 touch.

sizes.density: Each size grows a step with data-density. Wrap the box in a .ayy-label so the label is part of the hit area.
sizes.width: Fixed square.

components.js: checkboxClass constant; checkboxSizeClass(size?) → string | undefined (the --sm / --lg class; md adds nothing)

props.size: "sm" | "md" | "lg" (visual size; the native size attribute is not exposed)

a11y: A colour alone doesn't say what it means: keep the priority or status in the label too.
Wrap it in a <label class="ayy-label"> with the text, or pair with <label for>.
Indeterminate is announced as "mixed" automatically.
Group related checkboxes in a <fieldset> with a <legend>.
do: Use a checkbox for choices submitted with a form (terms, preferences saved with a Save button).
Use checkboxes to select several items in a list or table, with an indeterminate select-all.
Phrase labels positively: "Email me updates", not "Don't email me".
Match the size to the controls around it: sm beside sm buttons and inputs, lg in forms made for touch.
dont: Don't use a checkbox for settings that apply instantly — use Switch.
Don't use checkboxes to pick exactly one option — use Radio.
Don't use a checkbox to trigger an immediate action.

components.name: Radio
components.description: A set of options where exactly one can be chosen. It's built on native radio buttons, grouped under a legend.

classes.ayy-radio: On <input type="radio">. Size follows density. aria-invalid="true" tints the ring destructive (dashed in High Contrast).
classes.ayy-radio--sm: Small circle (--ayy-size-check-sm) and small label text. Wins over the size of its group.
classes.ayy-radio--lg: Large circle (--ayy-size-check-lg) and large label text. Wins over the size of its group.
classes.ayy-radio-group: On the <fieldset> holding the radios. Vertical stack.
classes.ayy-radio-group--sm: Every radio, label and the legend in the group small, with tighter rows.
classes.ayy-radio-group--lg: Every radio, label and the legend in the group large, with looser rows.

default.looks: A circle --ayy-size-check wide with a line-hover border on a wash fill.

hover.looks: Border turns text-soft.

pressed.none: No pressed look; it picks on release.

focus.looks: 2px ring, 2px offset. Arrow keys move the choice within the group.

disabled.looks: --ayy-opacity-disabled, not-allowed cursor. Forced colours: GrayText border.

selected.looks: Primary fill and border with a primary-fg dot that springs in.

error.when: aria-invalid="true" on each radio of the group
error.looks: Destructive border. Forced colours: dashed.

loading.none: Choosing is instant.

scale.sm: --ayy-size-check-sm: 14px compact, 16 comfortable, 18 touch.
scale.md: --ayy-size-check: 16px compact, 18 comfortable, 20 touch.
scale.lg: --ayy-size-check-lg: 20px compact, 22 comfortable, 24 touch.

sizes.density: Each size grows a step with data-density.
sizes.width: Fixed circle. The group stacks (vertical) or wraps in a row (horizontal).

components.js: radioClass, radioGroupLegendClass constants; radioSizeClass(size?) → string | undefined (the --sm / --lg class); radioGroupClass({ orientation?, size?, className? }) → string

props.label: ReactNode — legend text
props.name: string — generated if omitted
props.size: "sm" | "md" | "lg" — every radio, label and the legend in the group
"sm" | "md" | "lg" — this radio only; wins over the group (the native size attribute is not exposed)

a11y: Arrow keys move between radios in a group natively — no JS needed.
Always give the group a legend (label prop) and each radio a wrapping <label class="ayy-label">.
do: Use radios to pick exactly one of 2–6 visible options (plan, visibility, region).
Pre-select the most common option when there's a sensible default.
Set the size on the RadioGroup so every option, label and the legend change together.
dont: Don't use radios for more than ~6 options — use Select.
Don't use radios to switch views — use Tabs.
Don't use radios for independent on/off choices — use Checkbox.
Don't use a single radio on its own — use a Checkbox.

components.name: Segmented control
components.description: A short row of options where one is always selected, for switching a view, a range or a setting that changes what you see. It looks like tabs but works like radio buttons.

classes.ayy-segmented-control: Root, a role="radiogroup" with an aria-label. The pill track.
classes.ayy-segmented-control--sm: Small height, for toolbars and card headers.
classes.ayy-segmented-control--lg: Large height and text, for a main choice on a phone or a settings screen.
classes.ayy-segmented-control--full: Fills its container with equal segments.
classes.ayy-segmented-control__option: A <label> around a native <input type="radio">, which stays in the page (focus, forms) but draws nothing. The checked one is filled; the focused one gets the ring.

default.looks: A pill track (wash fill, line border); options in text-soft, medium weight.

hover.looks: Option text turns full text colour.

pressed.none: No pressed look; it picks on release.

focus.looks: 2px ring inset by 2px; on the chosen segment the ring takes the page colour so it shows on the fill.

disabled.looks: Option dims to --ayy-opacity-disabled, not-allowed cursor.

selected.looks: Filled with the text colour, label in the page colour, small shadow. Forced colours: Highlight fill.

error.none: One option is always chosen, so there's nothing to be invalid.

loading.none: Switching is instant; show loading in the content it controls (a Skeleton).

scale.sm: Control sm height (28px compact, 32 comfortable, 40 touch), tighter padding, sm text.
scale.md: Control md height (32px compact, 40 comfortable, 44 touch).
scale.lg: Control lg height (36px compact, 44 comfortable, 48 touch), 16px side padding, lg text.

sizes.density: Height and text follow data-density.
sizes.width: Hugs its options and scrolls sideways when they don't fit. full (ayy-segmented-control--full) fills the container with equal segments.

components.js: segmentedControlClass({ size?, full?, className? }) → string; segmentedControlOptionClass constant.

props.name: Shared radio name, for forms. Generated if omitted.
props.full: boolean — equal segments across the container.

a11y: It's a radio group: give the root an aria-label ("Date range"). Arrow keys move the choice, Tab leaves the group — the browser does it.
The checked segment is filled and bolder, not only coloured; High Contrast mode fills it with the system highlight.
An icon-only segment needs text for screen readers: an .ayy-sr-only span or aria-label on the input.
do: Use a segmented control for two to five mutually exclusive options that apply at once: a date range above a chart, list vs grid, monthly vs yearly.
Keep labels short and parallel (7 days · 30 days · 90 days).
Use size sm in a toolbar or card header, and full on a phone when it's the main control of the screen.
dont: Don't use it to show different panels of content — use Tabs.
Don't use it for more than five options or long labels — use Select or a Radio group.
Don't use it for an on/off setting — use Switch.
Don't use it for navigation between pages — use links.

components.name: Chip
components.description: A compact pill for filters and choices. Chips can be switched on and off, work as single or multiple choice, or be removable when they stand for filters that are applied.

classes.ayy-chip: A <label> around a native <input type="checkbox"> or radio (which stays in the page but draws nothing), or a <button aria-pressed>. On when the input is checked or aria-pressed="true".
classes.ayy-chip--sm: Small: a step under the default (24px compact), sm text, tighter padding. For a dense toolbar.
classes.ayy-chip--lg: Large: a medium control tall (32px compact), md text, more padding. For a main filter row or touch.
classes.ayy-chip--removable: An active filter: a <span> with its text and an __remove button. Not a control itself.
classes.ayy-chip__count: Number of results after the label, muted, tabular digits.
classes.ayy-chip__remove: The remove (×) button of a removable chip. Needs an aria-label ("Remove Status: Open").
classes.ayy-chip-group: Wrapping row of chips: role="group" with an aria-label, or role="radiogroup" for radio chips.
classes.ayy-chip-group--scroll: One line that scrolls sideways instead of wrapping (a phone toolbar).

default.looks: Pill with a line-strong border, transparent fill, text-soft label at the sm control height.

hover.looks: Wash fill, line-hover border, full text colour. A removable chip keeps its border; its × gets a wash-hover circle.

pressed.none: No pressed look; it toggles on release.

focus.looks: 2px ring, 2px offset (1px on the remove button).

disabled.looks: --ayy-opacity-disabled, not-allowed cursor.

selected.looks: Text-colour border, wash-hover fill and a tick before the label (not colour alone); the count turns text-soft. Forced colours: Highlight fill.

error.none: Chips are filters and choices; show validation on the group with a FieldError.

loading.none: Filtering shows its loading in the results (Skeleton), not on the chip.

scale.sm: Control sm height minus 4px (24px compact, 28 comfortable, 36 touch), control sm text minus 1px, 8px side padding.
scale.md: Control sm height (28px compact, 32 comfortable, 40 touch), control sm text, 12px side padding.
scale.lg: Control md height (32px compact, 40 comfortable, 44 touch), control md text, 16px side padding.

sizes.density: Every size follows data-density with the control scale.

components.name: Color swatch
components.description: Round colour options for picking one colour, as for a tag, a list or a drawing tool. It can include a "no colour" option and an "any colour" option that opens the colour picker.

classes.ayy-swatch: One colour: a <label> around a native radio (which stays in the page but draws nothing), or a <button aria-pressed>. classes.ayy-swatch--none: "No colour": the surface with a red diagonal stroke. No --ayy-swatch.
classes.ayy-swatch--custom: Any colour: a <label> around an <input type="color">, drawn as a ring of the chart colours around the picked colour. Clicking it opens ayywi's built-in ColorPicker in a floating popover instead of the OS picker (React and @danitesler/ayywi/elements keep --ayy-swatch in step with the input).
classes.ayy-swatch-popover: Popover container for ayywi's ColorPicker opened by a custom swatch: top layer (popover="auto"), positioned next to the swatch dot.
classes.ayy-swatch-group: Wrapping row of swatches: role="radiogroup" with an aria-label or aria-labelledby. Padded so the picked ring and focus ring aren't clipped.
classes.ayy-swatch-group--track: On a pill-shaped wash, like a toolbar's colour row.

default.looks: A round dot in --ayy-swatch with a hairline so light and dark colours both show. none is the surface crossed by a red stroke; custom is a rainbow ring around the current colour.

hover.looks: Grows to 110%.

pressed.none: No pressed look; it's picked as soon as it's clicked (see selected).

focus.when: :focus-visible on the button, or on the radio inside
focus.looks: 2px ring, 5px offset, outside the picked ring.

disabled.looks: --ayy-opacity-disabled, not-allowed cursor.

selected.looks: A gap in the surface colour, a ring in the text colour, and a tick on the dot, not colour alone. Forced colours: Highlight outline.

error.none: A colour can't be invalid. Pick a default instead of leaving none picked.

loading.none: Colours are local; no loading look.

scale.sm: 0.6 × the sm control height: about 17px compact, 19 comfortable, 24 touch.
scale.md: 0.75 × the sm control height: 21px compact, 24 comfortable, 30 touch.
scale.lg: The sm control height: 28px compact, 32 comfortable, 40 touch.

sizes.density: Dot size follows data-density (above); the hit area always reaches the sm control height.
sizes.width: Square. A group wraps onto more lines; track (ayy-swatch-group--track) puts them on a pill.

props.label: string — the colour's name, required ("Blue")
props.name: string — the same for every swatch in the group

props.label: string — required ("Custom colour")
Every <input type="color"> prop: value, defaultValue (hex), onChange.

a11y: Radio swatches are native: Tab enters the group, arrow keys move the pick, and screen readers say the colour's name and "checked". Every swatch needs a name (label prop / aria-label) because a dot has no text.
Name the group ("Tag colour") with aria-label or aria-labelledby.
The picked swatch has a ring and a tick, not just a colour; light and dark dots keep a hairline edge in every theme. High Contrast outlines the picked one with the system highlight.
The dot is smaller than a touch target, but its hit area reaches a control's height (bigger at touch density).
do: Use swatches to pick a colour from a short, fixed set: a tag, a list, a calendar, an annotation pen.
Colour them with tokens (--ayy-chart-1…6 are made to be told apart and meet 3:1 on every surface), and name each one.
Offer a none swatch when "no colour" is a real choice, and a ColorSwatchCustom when people may need any colour (an image editor).
Use a track group in a toolbar, size sm.
dont: Don't use swatches to choose a theme or a status — use a Segmented control or a Select; colour alone doesn't say what a status means.
Don't hardcode hex values in --ayy-swatch; use tokens, or the app's own colour variables when people pick colours (stored values belong in data, not in markup).
Don't show more than about ten swatches in a row — group them, or add a ColorSwatchCustom.
Don't use colour names that only make sense in one theme ("Black" turns white in dark mode) — name the role ("Ink").

Group them in a <fieldset> with a <legend> (ChoiceGroup legend) so the question is announced with each option.
Chosen is a thicker border (and a filled card when compact), not colour alone; High Contrast outlines it with the system highlight.
A full slot stays in the group as disabled, struck through, so people see what isn't available.
do: Use choice cards when each option needs more than a word: a plan with its price, a delivery option with its date, an add-on with what it costs.
Use compact cards for a grid of short options: time slots, sizes, seat counts. Say what's left in the description. A day strip is compact cards in a scroll group.

Use type checkbox for add-ons that combine, radio for one choice.

components.name: Slider

Don't use it for a choice between a few named options — use a Segmented control or Radio buttons.
Don't hide what min and max mean: label the ends or the value.

Set min and max (min 1 for guests, 0 when zero removes the line) and say the limit in a hint.
Use size sm in a cart line or a table row.
dont: Don't use it for large or exact numbers (a price, a phone number, a year) — use an Input; for a rough amount use a Slider.

Space toggles it; that's native checkbox behaviour.
The thumb direction flips automatically in RTL.
do: Use a switch for settings that take effect instantly (enable sync, dark mode).
Make the label describe the 'on' state: 'Sync on save', not 'Toggle sync'.
dont: Don't use a switch for choices submitted later with a form's Save button — a checkbox reads better there.
Don't use a switch to choose between more than two options — use Tabs or a select.
Don't require a Save click after flipping a switch.

components.name: Shortcut
components.description: Keyboard shortcuts written once and shown correctly for each device. It also includes a recorder that lets people set their own shortcut, and a list for help screens.

classes.ayy-shortcut: A shortcut's keys: a row of .ayy-kbd keycaps (aria-hidden) after an .ayy-sr-only label in words. data-keys holds the shortcut ("Mod+Shift+K") so @danitesler/ayywi/elements redraws it for Apple devices. Always left to right, as in the OS menus, RTL included.
classes.ayy-shortcut-recorder: A <button> that records a shortcut: shows the current keys or a placeholder, aria-pressed="true" while listening (a pulsing ring). aria-label names the action and the keys.
classes.ayy-shortcut-recorder__placeholder: The muted text inside the recorder while no shortcut is set, or while listening ("Press keys…").
classes.ayy-shortcut-list: A <dl> of shortcuts: what each does, then its keys.
classes.ayy-shortcut-list__row: One <div> in the list holding a <dt> (the action) and a <dd> (an .ayy-shortcut, or typed text like "#tag").

default.looks: Keycaps (.ayy-kbd) left to right in every language; the recorder is a wash field with a line-strong border showing the keys or a muted placeholder.

hover.looks: The recorder's border turns line-hover.

pressed.none: No pressed look; a click starts listening (see selected).

focus.looks: 2px ring, 2px offset.

disabled.looks: --ayy-opacity-disabled, not-allowed cursor: managed, or the platform doesn't allow it.

selected.looks: Listening for keys: a ring-colour border with a slow pulse around it, and "Press keys…". Esc cancels, Backspace clears. Forced colours: Highlight outline.

error.looks: A destructive border. Say what it clashes with in a hint.

loading.none: Recording is instant; no loading look.

sizes.density: The recorder is the md control height (32px compact, 40 comfortable, 44 touch); keycaps follow the text around them.
sizes.width: Keycaps hug their keys. The recorder is at least 9rem; the list fills its container.

components.js: Shortcuts are strings like "Mod+Shift+K" (Mod = ⌘ on Apple devices, Ctrl elsewhere; also Ctrl, Alt, Shift, Meta). shortcutFromEvent(event, { bare? }) → the shortcut a keydown makes, or null for modifiers alone; matchShortcut(event, "Mod+K") → boolean, for your own handlers, by physical key, so it works on any layout (Russian Cmd+У is Mod+E); shortcutKeys(s, platform?) → ["⌘", "K"] (Super on Linux, Win on Windows); shortcutLabel(s, platform?) → "Command K"; shortcutHtml(s, platform?) → markup; syncShortcuts(root?, platform?) redraws static .ayy-shortcut[data-keys] for Apple and Linux devices (@danitesler/ayywi/elements does it on load); getPlatform(); isApplePlatform(); isWindowsPlatform(); isLinuxPlatform(); keyFromCode(code). connectShortcutRecorder(button, { value?, label?, bare?, onChange?, onRecordingChange? }) → { setValue, destroy }. shortcutClass, shortcutRecorderClass({ className? }).

element.description: Wraps a button.ayy-shortcut-recorder and makes it record: click, press the keys, and the button shows them. Esc or Tab cancels, Backspace or Delete clears, leaving the button stops listening.

attributes.value: The shortcut, "Mod+Shift+2". Updated when one is recorded; removed when cleared.
attributes.label: What the shortcut does ("Capture area"); names the button "Capture area: Ctrl Shift 2".
attributes.bare: Allow a key without modifiers (a single letter, as in an app's own single-key shortcuts).

events.ayy-change: { value } — the new shortcut, or null when cleared.
events.ayy-recording: { recording } — true when it starts listening, false when it stops. Pause your own shortcuts meanwhile.

react.import: import { Shortcut, ShortcutRecorder, ShortcutList, ShortcutListItem } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";

Shortcut.renders: Ctrl K …

ShortcutRecorder.renders: <button type="button" class="ayy-shortcut-recorder" aria-pressed aria-label> with a Shortcut or the placeholder

props.onValueChange: (value: string | null) => void — null when cleared
props.label: string — what the shortcut does; names the button
props.onRecordingChange: (recording: boolean) => void — pause your own shortcuts meanwhile
props.bare: boolean — allow a key without modifiers
props.placeholder: ReactNode — shown while none is set. Default "Record shortcut"
props.recordingText: string — shown while listening. Default "Press keys…"

props.label: ReactNode — what it does
props.keys: string — the shortcut; or pass children instead (typed text, two shortcuts)

a11y: Keycaps are aria-hidden and a visually hidden label says the keys in words ("Command Shift K"), so screen readers don't read "place of interest sign".
The recorder is a toggle button: aria-pressed="true" while listening, and its aria-label says the action, the keys and how to cancel ("Capture area: Press keys, or Escape to cancel").
While it listens it takes every key, Tab included (Tab cancels and moves on), so it can never trap focus.
Pause the app's own shortcuts while recording (onRecordingChange / ayy-recording), or pressing one would run it.
A clash is shown with aria-invalid on the recorder and a hint saying which action already uses it; the border is not the only cue.
do: Store shortcuts as "Mod+…" strings and show them with Shortcut, so Mac and Windows users each see their own keys.
Put recorders in Settings rows: the action as the label, the recorder as the control.
Check a new shortcut against the others and set aria-invalid with a hint when it clashes.
Use ShortcutList for a keyboard help sheet (in a Dialog on "?").
dont: Don't hard-code "⌘" or "Ctrl" in your copy; use Shortcut.
Don't allow bare keys for global shortcuts; they'd fire while typing.
Don't show a shortcut as a tooltip only; put it next to the menu item or in a help list too.
