components.name: Settings
components.description: A layout for preferences as rows, with a label and a short hint on one side and the control on the other, grouped under headings. A row can also link to a sub-page or run an action like signing out.

classes.ayy-settings: A group: <section aria-labelledby> holding a title, an optional description and the list. Groups after each other get space between them.
classes.ayy-settings--plain: No card around the rows (inside a dialog, a sheet, or a page already on a surface); rows lose their inline padding.
classes.ayy-settings__title: The group's heading, an <h2> ("Notifications") that labels the section.
classes.ayy-settings__description: A muted line under the heading.
classes.ayy-settings__list: The rows, in a card with a line border; hairlines between rows.
classes.ayy-settings__row: One setting: text at the start, the control at the end. Wraps the control under the text when there isn't room (a phone).
classes.ayy-settings__row--stack: The control under the text at full width: a textarea, a radio list, a group of choice cards. The row doesn't wrap.
classes.ayy-settings__label: The setting's name: a <label for> pointing at the control, or a <span> when the control is labelled otherwise.
classes.ayy-settings__hint: One muted line explaining the setting; give it an id and point the control's aria-describedby at it. With ayy-field__error it's an error.
classes.ayy-settings__control: The control's box at the end of the row. Inputs and selects in it get a sensible minimum width.
classes.ayy-settings__link: On an .ayy-settings__row that is an <a href> (opens a sub-page) or a <button> (runs an action): the whole row is the target, with a chevron icon at the end.
classes.ayy-settings__value: The current value in a link row, muted, before the chevron ("English", "System").
classes.ayy-settings__link--destructive: Sign out, Delete account: red text and no chevron.
classes.ayy-settings__picker: A grid of larger pictures to choose from in a stacked row (an appearance setting that should show every choice at once): role="radiogroup" with an aria-label. For a dropdown, use a Select with pictures.
classes.ayy-settings__option: One picture to choose: a <label> around a visually hidden native radio, a .ayy-settings__preview and a .ayy-settings__caption. Chosen: the picture gets a text-colour border and the caption turns the text colour.
classes.ayy-settings__preview: The picture's 16:10 frame in a SettingsOption. Holds a .ayy-settings__screen, or a short sample such as "Aa" in a font. aria-hidden: the caption names the option. (In a Select, the screen goes straight in its .ayy-select__picture.)
classes.ayy-settings__caption: The option's name under the picture ("Dark", "Sharp").
classes.ayy-settings__screen: A miniature app (sidebar, heading, lines, a primary button) drawn from the tokens around it, for Theme, Corners and Text direction: in a Select's pictures (.ayy-select__picture) or a SettingsOption's. Set data-theme, data-density or dir on it, or brand and corner tokens on or around it, to preview them; it mirrors in RTL. Two in one picture split it, the second showing the right half: System as light then dark, Auto density as compact then touch, Auto direction as dir="ltr" then dir="rtl".
classes.ayy-settings__screen--rows: For Density: a list of rows, each a line of text and a control, divided by hairlines; rows are as tall as data-density makes them (exaggerated), so Compact shows about two and a half times the rows Touch does.
classes.ayy-settings__screen--brand: For Brand colour: where the primary colour shows (the chosen sidebar item tinted, a filled progress bar, a ticked checkbox, the primary button). Set --ayy-color-primary on it to preview a colour (a palette token; var(--ayy-color-text) for the monochrome default).

default.looks: A semibold heading and a muted description over a bordered card of rows split by hairlines: a medium label and a small muted hint at the start, the control at the end.

hover.looks: A wash over the link row; an option's picture gets the line-hover border.

pressed.none: No pressed look; a link row opens its page at once.

focus.looks: Link rows get the ring inside the row's edge (outside in plain groups); an option's picture gets the ring 2px outside; controls keep their own ring.

disabled.looks: Reduced opacity and not-allowed cursor on link rows and options.

selected.looks: The picture gets a text-colour border plus a 1px ring, and the caption turns the text colour. Forced colours: a Highlight outline. Rows themselves aren't selectable: a link row shows its current value (.ayy-settings__value).

error.looks: The hint becomes the error, in the destructive colour.

loading.none: Settings apply at once. While they load, show a Skeleton in the shape of the rows.

destructive.looks: Sign out, delete the account: red label, no chevron.

sizes.density: Rows are at least the lg control height (40px compact, 48 comfortable, 52 touch); their controls follow data-density.
sizes.width: Fills its container. A row wraps its control under the label when there's no room; stack does it always. Inputs and popover triggers in a row are at least 11rem, selects 12.5rem (room for a picture). A picker is a grid of 8.5rem-minimum columns with 16:10 pictures. A screen's parts are sized in container units of its picture, so one drawing fits a grid tile and both of a Select's pictures.

components.js: settingsClass({ plain?, className? }), settingsRowClass({ stack?, link?, destructive?, className? }) → class strings; settingsChevronIcon (SVG markup for a link row's chevron, mirrored in RTL); settingsPickerClass, settingsOptionClass, settingsPreviewClass, settingsCaptionClass, settingsScreenClass constants; settingsScreenVariants ("app", "rows", "brand": add ayy-settings__screen--rows or --brand). A custom colour Select: settingsColorInput(select) finds the hidden <input type="color" data-value> right after its wrapper, openSettingsColor(select) opens ayywi's colour picker under the select when that option is chosen (call it on change and on ayy-choose, after the list closes), syncSettingsColor(input) shows the colour in that option's picture; @danitesler/ayywi/elements does all three page-wide. Apply the picks with setTheme(), setDensity() and setBrand(); data-motion="reduce" and dir for motion and direction.

react.import: import { Settings, SettingsRow, SettingsLink, SettingsPicker, SettingsOption, SettingsScreen } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";

props.title: ReactNode — the heading; the section is labelled by it
props.description: ReactNode — a line under the heading
props.plain: boolean — no card around the rows

props.label: ReactNode — the setting's name
props.htmlFor: string — the control's id: the label becomes a <label for>, and the hint gets the id `${htmlFor}-hint` for the control's aria-describedby
props.error: ReactNode — replaces the hint, in red, with role="alert"
props.stack: boolean — the control under the text at full width

SettingsLink.renders: <a class="ayy-settings__row ayy-settings__link" href> with href, else <button type="button">; a directional chevron unless destructive

props.label: ReactNode — what it opens or does
props.hint: ReactNode — a line under the label
props.value: ReactNode — the current value, before the chevron
props.href: string — opens a page: the row is an <a>; without it a <button>
props.type / disabled: Button rows only. type defaults to "button"

props.name: string — shared radio name; generated if omitted

props.label: ReactNode — the caption, which names the radio
props.preview: ReactNode — the picture; a SettingsScreen by default, or a sample like "Aa" in a font or at a text size

SettingsScreen.renders: <span class="ayy-settings__screen" data-theme data-density aria-hidden="true">; two of them for theme="system" (light, dark) or density="auto" (compact, touch)

props.variant: "app" | "rows" | "brand" — what it draws: the app (Theme, Corners, Text direction), rows (Density) or the primary colour's places (Brand colour; set --ayy-color-primary in style)
props.theme: "system" | "light" | "dark" | "dark-contrast" | "light-gray" — the theme it's drawn in; omit for the one around it
props.density: "compact" | "comfortable" | "touch" | "auto" — the density it's drawn in; omit for the one around it

a11y: Each group is a <section> labelled by its <h2>, so screen-reader users can jump between groups.
Every control needs a name: give SettingsRow htmlFor and the control that id, so the label is a real <label for>. For a Switch, put the id on the switch's input.
Point the control's aria-describedby at the hint (`${htmlFor}-hint`) so the explanation is read with it.
A link row is one <a> or <button>: its whole text, value included, is its name. Use <a href> when it opens a page, <button> when it does something.
Controls wrap under the label on narrow screens instead of shrinking below a usable size.
A picker is a radiogroup of native radios: arrow keys move between options, and each option is named by its caption. The pictures are aria-hidden.

A custom colour's <input type="color"> is hidden and out of the tab order: choosing Custom opens the colour picker as a labelled dialog under the select with focus in it, and Esc or Enter closes it and puts focus back on the select.
do: Use it for any settings or preferences screen: group related rows under short headings (General, Notifications, Shortcuts). They open in a near-full-screen Dialog (size="full") holding the App shell in settings mode (the Settings pattern): a sidebar of sections and one section's groups in the main.
Keep labels short and put the why in the hint ("Show a badge with the number of tasks due today").
Use a Switch for on/off that applies at once, a Select for one of several, a Shortcut recorder for key bindings.
On phones, use link rows with the current value for anything with more than a few choices, and open a sub-page.
Put Sign out or Delete account last, in its own group, as a destructive link row.

For appearance settings, use the same two controls in every product: Mode (System, Light, Dark) as a Select whose pictures are SettingsScreens, applied with setTheme(); and Theme as a Select of THEME_PRESETS whose pictures are a Swatch (ayy-swatch) with the theme's accent as --ayy-swatch, applied with setBrand(), setThemeCustomization() and setIconPack(). A theme carries the accent, surfaces, corners, fonts and icons, so don't offer them as separate settings: a cog button beside Theme opens a dialog with them (Accent colour swatches, Surface and Corners segmented controls, Font, Icons and Density selects) and a live preview, filled in with the current theme, and saving a change makes it the Theme select's last option, Custom. Text direction is a Select with SettingsScreen pictures (dir on the screen). Reduce motion as a Switch, Language as a Select, and Reset appearance as a destructive link row. Apply each at once.
dont: Don't add a Save button for switches and selects that apply at once; save as they change and confirm with a Toast if needed.
Don't put two controls in one row; split the setting.
Don't use a checkbox for a setting that applies at once — that's what a Switch says.
Don't nest a card inside the list; use another group.

Don't draw your own theme thumbnails, or use a Select without pictures or a button opening a popover for Mode, Theme or Text direction: a Select whose pictures are SettingsScreens draws each choice from its real tokens. Don't add separate settings for brand colour, surfaces, contrast, corners, fonts, icons, density or text size: the theme decides them.
Don't open settings in a small or side Dialog, or switch sections with Tabs; use a size="full" Dialog with the App shell's settings mode. --plain is for a sheet with a couple of quick options.

components.name: Page header
components.description: The top of a screen in an app: the page title, a line of description and the page's main actions, with an optional breadcrumb above. On phones the actions move below the title.

classes.ayy-page-header: Root <header>. A two-column grid: everything stacks in the first column, __actions sits in the second and spans them. One column below 48rem, actions last. A Breadcrumb or .ayy-eyebrow can go first.
classes.ayy-page-header__title: The page's <h1>: heading font, 28px, semibold. Smaller than marketing headings on purpose — app screens are for work.
classes.ayy-page-header__description: One sentence under the title, muted, at reading width.
classes.ayy-page-header__actions: The page's buttons, at the inline end (under the title on phones). One primary at most; the rest outline or ghost.

default.looks: An h1 (2xl heading font, semibold) with a muted md description under it, actions at the inline end.

hover.none: Static text; the buttons in __actions have their own states.

pressed.none: Not interactive.

disabled.none: Not interactive.

selected.none: Not interactive.

error.none: Show a failed load under it in an Alert.

loading.none: Render the title at once; put Skeletons below it for the content.

sizes.density: Doesn't follow data-density.
sizes.width: Fills its container; the description stops at --ayy-size-measure. Below 48rem the actions drop under the description, aligned to the start.

components.js: pageHeaderClass, pageHeaderTitleClass, pageHeaderDescriptionClass, pageHeaderActionsClass constants.

react.import: import { PageHeader, PageHeaderTitle, PageHeaderDescription, PageHeaderActions } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";

a11y: The title is the page's only <h1>; sections below it start at <h2>.
Keep the actions after the title in the source, so screen readers hear what the page is before what it can do.
A breadcrumb above the title is its own <nav aria-label="Breadcrumb">.
do: Use a page header at the top of every screen in the App shell's main: title, one line of description, the page's actions.
Put the one thing people come to the page to do in the actions as the primary button (New project, Invite); filters and exports are outline or ghost.
Add a Breadcrumb above the title once pages are more than one level deep.
Keep the description to one sentence that says what the page is for.
dont: Don't use it on marketing pages — use .ayy-display or headings for a hero.
Don't put tabs, search or filters in it — put them in a toolbar row (.ayy-spread) under it.
Don't put more than three actions in it; move the rest into a DropdownMenu.
Don't add a second h1 elsewhere on the page.

components.name: Showcase
components.description: A container for previewing a design at different screen sizes. It has a toolbar for switching devices and can show the code behind the preview.

classes.ayy-showcase: Root container: flex column holding the header and preview stage.
classes.ayy-showcase__header: Top bar containing the title and action controls.
classes.ayy-showcase__title: Title or label for the previewed component or screen.
classes.ayy-showcase__actions: Cluster of action controls (device switcher, props, copy button).
classes.ayy-showcase__stage: The canvas holding the previewed element, with a line border, card radius, and an ambient dot pattern.
classes.ayy-showcase__viewport: The responsive viewport container that smoothly transitions width.

default.looks: A surface container with a line border, card radius, and a subtle pattern on the preview stage.

hover.none: Container; interactive elements inside handle hover.

pressed.none: Container; interactive controls handle active states.

focus.none: Not directly focusable; child controls receive focus.

disabled.none: Showcase is not disabled.

selected.none: Container; device items show selection.

error.none: No error state.

loading.none: No loading state.

sizes.density: Toolbar controls follow data-density.
sizes.width: Fills its container width; the viewport transitions max-inline-size to match the active device.

Device switchers must have accessible labels describing the active viewport.
do: Use Showcase to demonstrate component variations and responsive layouts in docs and style guides.
Use the device switcher when previewing components with distinct phone or tablet layouts.
dont: Don't hardcode fixed heights that balloon small inline components.
Don't show device controls for components with no responsive variation.

components.name: Card
components.description: A surface that groups related content so it reads as one unit, like a project, a summary or a block of settings. It can react to hover when it's clickable, and it has a media version for captures, recordings and pictures.

classes.ayy-card--sm: Tighter: 12px padding on the header, content and footer, a sm title and an xs description.
classes.ayy-card--lg: Roomier: 24px padding and an lg title.
classes.ayy-card--interactive: Lifts on hover (mouse and trackpad only, so a tap doesn't leave it lifted). Use when the whole card is clickable.
classes.ayy-card--spotlight: Pointer-following glow + lit border. Colour via the --ayy-spot custom property.
classes.ayy-card--transparent: No fill and no rest shadow: the page shows through. The line border, radius and padding stay. Pairs with spotlight for rows on a plain page.
classes.ayy-card--featured: The one to pick: the recommended plan in a pricing grid, or the option someone chose. A 2px border in the text colour (High Contrast: a highlight outline). One per group.
classes.ayy-card__title: Heading. Use an h2–h4 that fits your outline.
classes.ayy-card__footer: Actions row, pinned to the bottom.
classes.ayy-card__media: Edge-to-edge image, screenshot or video. Rounds the card corners it touches (first or last child); zooms slightly when an interactive card is hovered with a mouse.
classes.ayy-card__link: Put on the title's <a>: it stretches over the whole card, so the card is one link and one tab stop. Other links and buttons inside stay clickable.
classes.ayy-card--view: View type: a capture, recording or picture to open. The picture fills the card and clips to its corners; Hover actions float in its corners.
classes.ayy-card__view-media: View: the picture's box at --ayy-ratio (default 16 / 10). A <button> or <a> when opening it is the card's main action.
classes.ayy-card__view-backdrop: View: a blurred copy of the picture filling the box around the letterboxed picture (aria-hidden).
classes.ayy-card__view-image: View: the picture itself, letterboxed (object-fit: contain), never cropped.
classes.ayy-card__view-badge: View: frosted pill in the top start corner — a recording's kind and length ("0:42").
classes.ayy-card__view-play: View: frosted round play glyph in the top end corner. Fades when the card is hovered so the actions can take the corner.
classes.ayy-card__view-body: View: title, details and badges on a gradient over the bottom of the picture. Revealed on hover; clicks go through to the picture.
classes.ayy-card__view-text: View: column of the title and the details; truncates.
classes.ayy-card__view-title: View: the card's name in sm semibold, one line.
classes.ayy-card__view-meta: View: details in xs soft text with tabular figures — size, length, age.
classes.ayy-card__view-badges: View: row of Badges at the end of the body (Edited, Uploaded).

default.looks: Surface fill, line border, card radius and the rest shadow; header, content and footer padded --ayy-space-5. transparent drops the fill and the rest shadow.

hover.when: :hover; on a view card also [data-hover] (hover tracked elsewhere)
hover.looks: Border turns line-hover. interactive also lifts 2px with the lift shadow and zooms its media 3%; spotlight lights a glow and border that follow the pointer. A view card takes the lift shadow, its body fades up from 6px below, a --reveal Hover actions row fades in and the play glyph fades out.

pressed.none: No pressed look, even when interactive.

focus.looks: The ring goes around the whole card (2px, 2px offset) when its title link has keyboard focus. On a view card the ring sits inside the picture's edge, and focus anywhere in it reveals the body and actions like hover.

disabled.none: Cards aren't disabled; dim nothing. For an unavailable option use a Choice card with a disabled input.

selected.looks: Text-colour border plus a 1px ring, so it reads as 2px without moving. For a picked option use a Choice card instead. Forced colours: Highlight outline.

error.none: Put an Alert inside the card's content.

loading.none: No loading look; show Skeletons in the card's content shape (aria-busy on the region) — 16 / 10 for view cards.

menu-open.when: view card :has([aria-expanded="true"]), a menu inside it is open
menu-open.looks: Stays revealed while its ⋯ menu is open.

scale.sm: 12px padding on the header, content and footer; --ayy-text-sm title, --ayy-text-xs description.
scale.md: 20px padding; --ayy-text-md title, --ayy-text-sm description.
scale.lg: 24px padding; --ayy-text-lg title, --ayy-text-sm description.

sizes.density: Padding and text don't follow data-density.
sizes.width: Fills its grid cell or container; height follows content, and the footer sits at the bottom of a stretched card. A view card is as tall as its picture's box: --ayy-ratio of its width. Put view cards in .ayy-grid with --ayy-min (14–16rem).

components.js: cardClass({ size?, interactive?, spotlight?, transparent?, featured?, view?, className? }) → string; cardHeaderClass, cardTitleClass, cardDescriptionClass, cardContentClass, cardFooterClass, cardMediaClass, cardLinkClass constants; trackSpotlight(pointerEvent) sets --ayy-mx/--ayy-my.

react.import: import { Card, CardHeader, CardTitle, CardDescription, CardContent, CardFooter, CardMedia, CardLink, CardViewMedia, CardViewImage, CardViewBadge, CardViewPlay, CardViewBody, CardViewText, CardViewTitle, CardViewMeta, CardViewBadges } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";

props.size: "sm" | "md" | "lg" — padding of the header, content and footer, and the size of the title
props.spotlight: boolean — tracks the pointer for you
props.spotColor: CSS colour for the spotlight, e.g. "var(--ayy-accent-product)"
props.transparent: boolean — no fill, no rest shadow (ayy-card--transparent).
props.featured: boolean — the recommended or chosen card (ayy-card--featured).
props.view: boolean — the view type (ayy-card--view): a capture, recording or picture to open

props.children: An , ,

CardViewMedia.renders: <button class="ayy-card__view-media"> when given onClick, <a> with href, otherwise <div>

props.ratio: number | string — the box's shape, width ÷ height (1.6, or "1440 / 900"); default 16 / 10 so a grid lines up

CardViewImage.renders: + (src, alt, width and height go on the picture)

props.backdrop: string — a smaller copy for the blurred fill; default src

CardViewPlay.renders: <span class="ayy-card__view-play" aria-hidden="true"> with a play icon

a11y: If the whole card is a link, put ayy-card__link on the title's <a> — don't wrap the card in <a>. Screen readers then announce just the title, not the whole card.
Media images are content: give them alt text, or alt="" when the title already says it all.
Spotlight layers are pseudo-elements, invisible to assistive tech.

View cards: when the picture opens something, CardViewMedia is a <button> or <a> with an aria-label that names the item and the action ("Annotate the pricing page capture from 2 minutes ago"); the body is decoration on top of it.
View cards reveal their body and actions on focus as well as hover, and always show them on touch screens, so nothing is hover-only. The backdrop is aria-hidden.
do: Use a card to group a unit of content: a project, a person, a plan, a stat.
Add interactive for clickable tiles in a grid.
Use accent tokens (--ayy-accent-*) as spotColor to tie a card to a category.
Keep one level of cards; use hairline dividers inside.
Mark the recommended plan in a pricing grid with featured (and a Badge that says why), not a coloured background.

Use the view type (view) for captures, recordings and pictures people open — a screenshot history, a media library — in .ayy-grid; pass the picture's real width and height, and keep the box at 16 / 10 so rows line up (portrait pictures letterbox over the blur).
On a view card, group three or more actions in one Hover actions bar (top end, group, reveal) ending in a ⋯ DropdownMenu; show a recording's length in CardViewBadge and add CardViewPlay.
dont: Don't wrap page sections in a card — use plain layout.
Don't nest cards inside cards.
Don't set background colours on cards; the surface token keeps both themes correct. For no fill at all, use transparent.
Don't use spotlight on dense lists of small rows — it's for showcase grids and a few large rows.
Don't use view cards for records people select in bulk — use Grid with GridItemSelect and an Action bar.

Don't crop a view card's picture (object-fit: cover) — captures must show whole; the blurred copy fills the gap. Don't put essential information only in its body: it hides until hover on pointer devices.

components.name: Tabs
components.description: Tabs for switching between panels of related content on the same page. They can be used fully from the keyboard.

classes.ayy-tabs--sm: Small: the track is a small control tall, tab text is control sm, tighter padding. Reaches only its own list, not tabs nested in a panel.
classes.ayy-tabs--lg: Large: the track is a large control tall, tab text is control lg, more padding.
classes.ayy-tabs__panel: role="tabpanel". Hide inactive panels with the hidden attribute.
classes.ayy-tabs__count: Small count after a tab's label (items in a filter). Inverts with the selected tab.

default.looks: A pill track (wash fill, line border) with text-soft tab labels.

hover.looks: Tab label turns full text colour.

pressed.none: No pressed look; it selects on click.

focus.looks: 2px ring, 2px offset.

disabled.looks: --ayy-opacity-disabled, not-allowed cursor; arrow keys skip it. Forced colours: GrayText.

selected.looks: Filled with the text colour, label in the page colour, small shadow; its count gets a 15% page-colour tint. Forced colours: Highlight.

error.none: No error look; show it in the panel.

loading.none: Show loading in the panel (Skeleton), not on the tab.

scale.sm: Track at the sm control height (28px compact, 32 comfortable, 40 touch), control sm text, 8px side padding.
scale.md: Track at the md control height (32px compact, 40 comfortable, 44 touch), control md text, 12px side padding.
scale.lg: Track at the lg control height (36px compact, 44 comfortable, 48 touch), control lg text, 16px side padding.

sizes.density: Every size follows data-density with the control scale.
sizes.width: The list hugs its tabs and scrolls sideways when they don't fit; panels fill the container.

components.js: tabsClass/tabsListClass/tabsTabClass/tabsPanelClass/tabsCountClass constants; tabsSizeClass(size?) → string | undefined (the --sm / --lg class for the root; md adds nothing); nextTabIndex(key, current, count, rtl) for custom keyboard handling.

attributes.value: The selected tab's data-value (or index). Two-way.
attributes.class: Put ayy-tabs on it for block layout.

events.ayy-value-change: { value: string } — the user picked a tab

element.children: A [role=tablist] of [role=tab] buttons and [role=tabpanel] panels, paired by data-value (or by order). Ids, aria-controls/labelledby, tabindex and hidden are managed for you.

react.import: import { Tabs, TabsList, TabsTrigger, TabsContent } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";

props.size: "sm" | "md" | "lg" — the height of the tab list and its labels.

props.icon: ReactNode — optional icon before the label.

props.keepMounted: Keep children mounted while hidden. Default false.

a11y: Arrow keys move between tabs (flipped in RTL), Home/End jump to first/last. Activation follows focus.
Only the selected tab is in the tab order (roving tabindex).
Give the tablist an aria-label when there's no visible heading.
do: Use tabs to switch views of the same object (Overview / Activity / Members) or as segmented filters with 2–6 options.
Keep tab labels to one or two words.
Keep the tab set stable — don't add/remove tabs based on content.
dont: Don't use tabs for page-level navigation between routes — use links.
Don't use tabs for sequential steps — use Steps and separate pages. For a filter that changes one view (Today / Upcoming), use a Segmented control.
Don't nest tabs inside tabs.
Don't use tabs for more than ~6 options.

components.name: Accordion
components.description: A stack of sections that expand and collapse, for FAQs and for settings with a lot of detail. Only the heading shows until someone opens a section, and opening one can close the others.

classes.ayy-accordion: Root <div>: a column of items with hairlines above, between and below.
classes.ayy-accordion--sm: Tighter rows: 12px above and below the question, sm question text, xs answer text. Reaches only its own items.
classes.ayy-accordion--lg: Roomier rows: 20px above and below the question, lg question text, md answer text.
classes.ayy-accordion__item: A native <details>. Give every item in the accordion the same name attribute to allow only one open at a time. `open` expands it.
classes.ayy-accordion__trigger: The <summary>: the question, medium weight, with a chevron at the inline end that turns over when open.
classes.ayy-accordion__content: The answer below the trigger, in soft text. Paragraphs and lists inside are spaced for you.

default.looks: Items stacked between hairlines; each trigger is md text, medium weight, with a muted chevron pointing down.

hover.looks: Chevron turns text colour.

pressed.none: No pressed look.

focus.looks: 2px ring, 2px offset.

disabled.none: Native <details> can't be disabled; leave out an item that can't open.

selected.none: Open is the only state (see open).

error.none: No error state.

loading.none: No loading state.

open.looks: Chevron points up and the content rolls open in text-soft sm text. With the same name on each item, opening one closes the others.

scale.sm: 12px block padding, --ayy-text-sm question, --ayy-text-xs answer.
scale.md: 16px block padding, --ayy-text-md question, --ayy-text-sm answer.
scale.lg: 20px block padding, --ayy-text-lg question, --ayy-text-md answer.

sizes.density: Doesn't follow data-density.
sizes.width: Fills its container.

components.js: accordionClass, accordionItemClass, accordionTriggerClass, accordionContentClass constants; accordionSizeClass(size?) → string | undefined (the --sm / --lg class for the root; md adds nothing).

props.single: boolean — one item open at a time (a shared name on every <details>).

props.label: The always-visible row: the question or section name.

a11y: It's native <details>/<summary>: Enter and Space toggle it and the open state is announced. Don't add aria-expanded or a click handler.
Keep the summary text short and complete (a question), since it's the only part people see.
Find-in-page opens a closed item that contains the match.
do: Use an accordion for FAQs and for long optional detail people pick from: pricing questions, shipping info, advanced settings.
Use single on FAQ lists so the page doesn't grow into a wall of text.
Open the first item when most people need it.
dont: Don't hide content everyone needs behind it — show it.
Don't use it to switch between views of the same thing — use Tabs.
Don't use it for navigation — use the App shell's collapse inside a sidebar.
Don't nest an accordion inside another.

examples.title: FAQ
examples.html:
Can I cancel any time?

Yes. Your plan runs to the end of the billing period, then your projects switch to read-only. Nothing is deleted for 90 days.

Do viewers need a paid seat?

No. Only people who edit pages count as editors. Viewers and commenters are free on every plan.

Where is my data stored?

In the EU or the US, your choice when you create a workspace. Backups stay in the same region.

Enterprise plans can bring their own storage bucket.

components.name: Carousel
components.description: A row of slides that scrolls sideways, with buttons to move to the next or previous one. It suits galleries, testimonials and featured items. It uses native scrolling, so swiping and the keyboard work without extra code.

classes.ayy-carousel: Root (also on <ayy-carousel>). role="region" aria-roledescription="carousel" and an aria-label. data-slide-label="{index} de {count}" translates the slides' names (default "{index} of {count}").
classes.ayy-carousel__track: The scrolling, snapping row. Give it tabindex="0" so keyboards can scroll it. Gap via --ayy-gap.
classes.ayy-carousel__slide: Each slide: role="group" aria-roledescription="slide". Width via --ayy-slide (default min(22rem, 85%)).
classes.ayy-carousel__controls: Row of the previous/next buttons (outline icon buttons with data-ayy-prev / data-ayy-next). Their arrows are directional Hugeicons (ayy-icon--directional), so they flip in RTL.

default.looks: A track of slides that scrolls and snaps; previous and next Buttons centred below.

hover.looks: As Button.

focus.looks: The track gets a 2px ring, 2px offset (arrow keys then scroll it); buttons as Button.

disabled.when: [aria-disabled="true"] on previous/next at either end (set by <ayy-carousel> or React)
disabled.looks: The Button's disabled look; it stays focusable and does nothing.

selected.none: No current-slide look; the slides' position is the state.

error.none: No error state.

loading.none: Show Skeleton slides while the content loads.

sizes.density: The track doesn't follow data-density; the control Buttons do.
sizes.width: Fills its container; each slide is --ayy-slide wide (default min(22rem, 85%)) and as tall as the tallest.

components.js: carouselClass, carouselTrackClass, carouselSlideClass, carouselControlsClass constants; connectCarousel(root) → cleanup — wires the buttons, aria-disabled at the ends and slide labels.

attributes.class: Put ayy-carousel on it for block layout.

element.children: A .ayy-carousel__track of .ayy-carousel__slide elements, and buttons with data-ayy-prev / data-ayy-next anywhere inside. They scroll one slide at a time (smoothly unless the user prefers reduced motion) and get aria-disabled="true" at the ends. Slides without a label are named "2 of 6".

Carousel.renders: <div class="ayy-carousel" role="region"> with the track and the two buttons

props.label: string (required) — accessible name, e.g. "Team photos".
props.slideWidth: CSS length for every slide. Default min(22rem, 85%).
props.slideLabel: Each slide's name, with {index} and {count}. Default "{index} of {count}" (translate it). HTML: data-slide-label on the carousel.

a11y: The root is a named region with aria-roledescription="carousel"; each slide is a group named "n of total" unless you name it.
The track is focusable, so arrow keys scroll it; the buttons stay focusable at the ends (aria-disabled, not disabled) so focus isn't lost.
Nothing moves on its own, and smooth scrolling turns off under prefers-reduced-motion.
do: Use a carousel for a row of photos, screenshots or cards that doesn't need to be seen all at once: a gallery, feature highlights, personas.
Let the last slide peek in, so it's clear there's more.
Give images inside slides width and height so the strip doesn't jump.
dont: Don't put content everyone must see in a carousel — lay it out in a grid.
Don't hide essential content in later slides.
Don't auto-advance or build rotating banners — ayywi doesn't auto-play, on purpose.
Don't use it to switch between views of one thing — use Tabs.

components.name: Separator
components.description: A thin line that divides blocks of content, between sections of a page or between items in a row.

classes.ayy-separator: Root, on an <hr>. 1px hairline, no margins (spacing belongs to the layout).
classes.ayy-separator--vertical: Vertical rule in a flex row; add aria-orientation="vertical".
classes.ayy-separator--fade: Fades to transparent at both ends.

default.looks: A 1px hairline across its container (vertical: down the row).

hover.none: Decorative.

pressed.none: Decorative.

disabled.none: Decorative.

selected.none: Decorative.

error.none: Decorative.

loading.none: Decorative.

sizes.density: Doesn't follow data-density.
sizes.width: Horizontal fills the width; vertical stretches to the row's height (at least 1em). fade fades both ends.

components.js: separatorClass({ orientation?, fade?, className? }) → string
a11y: <hr> is a separator to screen readers. If the line is purely decorative, use role="presentation" or a CSS border instead.
Vertical separators need aria-orientation="vertical" (the React component adds it).
do: Use a fading separator between the sections of a long page.
Use a plain or vertical separator between groups in a footer, toolbar or card.
Give the separator room with the layout's gap or the sections' padding.
dont: Don't put one around every block — spacing usually separates better than lines.
Don't use it inside menus — use the menu's own separator.
Don't colour it; hairline keeps it quiet in every theme.

components.name: Scrollbar
components.description: A thin scrollbar with no track that is drawn in the text colour, so it follows every theme. Put it on any scroll container, or on the page.

classes.ayy-scrollbar: Root, on the element that scrolls (or <html> for the page). 8px gutter, 4px thumb, transparent track.
classes.ayy-scrollbar--hover: Thumb is hidden until the pointer or focus is inside the container.

default.looks: A rounded thumb in the text colour at 22%, on a transparent track.

hover.when: The pointer is over the thumb (Chromium and Safari only)
hover.looks: Thumb darkens to 40% text. With --hover, the whole thumb appears while the pointer is inside the container.

pressed.when: The thumb is being dragged (Chromium and Safari only)

focus.when: Focus is inside the container, with the hover variant
focus.looks: The thumb shows, as it does on hover. The scrollbar itself isn't focusable: give the scroll container tabindex="0" so the keyboard can scroll it.

disabled.none: A scrollbar can't be disabled; remove overflow instead.

selected.none: Nothing to select.

error.none: Nothing to validate.

loading.none: Nothing loads in a scrollbar.

sizes.density: Doesn't follow data-density.
sizes.width: 8px by default; set --ayy-scrollbar-size on the container for another gutter. The thumb is the gutter minus 4px. Firefox only offers its own thin scrollbar and ignores the size.

components.js: scrollbarClass({ hover?, className? }) → string

props.hover: boolean — show the thumb only while the pointer or focus is inside.

a11y: Scrolling stays native: wheel, touch, keyboard and assistive technology all work. The component only changes how the bar looks.
A scroll container that has no focusable content needs tabindex="0" and a label, or keyboard users can't scroll it. The React component sets tabindex="0".
Forced colours: the thumb is drawn in system colours.
do: Use the scrollbar on scroll containers inside a page: lists, panels, code, menus.
Put it on <html> to thin the page's own scrollbar.
Use the hover variant where the bar would crowd a dense, quiet surface.
dont: Don't use it to hide scrolling — to hide the bar altogether, give the user another way to scroll.
Don't use it as a progress indicator — use Progress, or the reading-progress bar.
Don't make it thicker to match touch targets; touch devices draw their own overlay bars.

components.name: Drag and drop
components.description: Standard drag and drop for reordering items and moving them between areas: a floating preview follows the pointer, drop targets show hover states (ready, over, reject), and a primary line indicates the exact drop position. Fully accessible with arrow keys.

classes.ayy-draggable: An item that can be picked up: grab cursor, dims to 0.4 opacity while dragging ([data-dragging]).
classes.ayy-drag-handle: The six-dot grip button: control-sized square, touch-action: none, grab cursor, takes arrow keys.
classes.ayy-sortable: Flex column container for sortable items with standard gap.
classes.ayy-sortable--horizontal: Horizontal flex layout for sortable strips, toolbars or tabs.
classes.ayy-sortable__item: Row in a sortable list: surface background, line border, dashed when dragged.
classes.ayy-drop-target: An area items can be dropped into: reacts with [data-drop="ready|over|reject"].
classes.ayy-drag-preview: Floating clone or element following the pointer in the top layer.
classes.ayy-drag-preview--chip: Compact pill-shaped preview showing the dragged item's name.

default.looks: Hidden preview; items and drop targets sit at rest.

hover.looks: Grip handle takes wash-hover and text colour.

pressed.looks: Grip handle switches to cursor: grabbing.

focus.looks: 2px ring outline on the handle; takes arrow keys.

disabled.looks: --ayy-opacity-disabled and cursor: not-allowed.

selected.none: No selected state.

error.looks: Rejected target gets dashed destructive border and not-allowed cursor; preview gets dashed destructive outline.

loading.none: No loading state.

dragging.looks: Item is held: dims to 0.4 opacity with dashed line border.

ready.looks: Target accepts the item: dashed text-soft border and wash fill.

over.looks: Pointer is over target: solid primary border, 8% primary tint and 3px glow ring.

edge.looks: A 2px primary insertion line on the target edge (block-start/end, inline-start/end) showing where the item lands.

sizes.density: DragHandle sizes follow control size tokens (--ayy-size-control-sm); list items follow text and padding tokens.
sizes.width: Fills its container. Horizontally oriented lists flow inline.

components.name: Dialog
components.description: A window that opens over the page and asks for attention, for confirmations, forms and short tasks. It can be centred, slide in from the side as a drawer, or rise from the bottom on phones. It's built on the native dialog element, so focus and Esc work properly.

classes.ayy-dialog: On the <dialog> element. Open with dialog.showModal().
classes.ayy-dialog--full: Near full screen: 72rem by 50rem at most, 4rem clear of the viewport on each axis, no padding; what it holds lays itself out (an App shell in settings mode). Fills the screen below 48rem, with no border or radius.
classes.ayy-dialog--side-start: Side modal on the inline-start edge (left in LTR, right in RTL): full height, slides in. Width from the size modifiers.
classes.ayy-dialog--side-end: Side modal on the inline-end edge (right in LTR, left in RTL): full height, slides in. Width from the size modifiers.
classes.ayy-dialog--side-bottom: Bottom sheet: anchored to the bottom edge with a grab handle, slides up. Full width on phones, centred at the size modifier's width on wider screens; clears the home indicator (safe-area inset).
classes.ayy-dialog__title: Heading (h2). Reference it with aria-labelledby on the dialog.
classes.ayy-dialog__body: Content that scrolls on its own, between the header and the footer. Fills the height of a side modal, so the footer sits at the bottom.
classes.ayy-dialog__footer: Actions. Stacked on mobile, end-aligned (right in LTR, left in RTL) from 40rem.
classes.ayy-dialog__close: Icon button in the top-end corner.

default.looks: Closed: not rendered. Open (see open): surface panel, line-strong border, card radius, overlay shadow, over a blurred --ayy-color-overlay backdrop.

hover.looks: Close button gets a wash-hover circle and the text colour.

pressed.none: The panel has no pressed look; its buttons have Button's.

focus.looks: Close: 2px ring, 2px offset. Body: ring inset by 2px.

disabled.none: A dialog isn't disabled; disable the buttons inside it.

selected.none: No selected state.

error.none: Show errors inside the body: a FieldError per field, an Alert for a failed save. Keep the dialog open.

loading.none: No loading look; put the primary Button in loading while it saves, Skeletons in the body while it loads.

open.looks: Fades and scales in (centred); side-start / side-end slide in from that edge (RTL-aware); side-bottom slides up as a sheet with a grab handle. The page behind is inert and stops scrolling.

scale.sm: 24rem wide.
scale.md: 32rem wide.
scale.lg: 42rem wide.
scale.full: Near full screen: up to 72rem by 50rem, no padding. Full screen on phones.

sizes.density: Padding is fixed (--ayy-space-6); its controls follow data-density.
sizes.width: The width above, never more than the viewport minus 2rem; at most the viewport height minus 2rem, the body scrolls. Side modals are full height (the size sets their width); a bottom sheet is full width below 40rem; full is 4rem clear of the viewport on each axis, and the whole screen below 48rem.

components.js: dialogClass({ size?, side?, className? }); isBackdropClick(dialog, event); dialogCloseIcon (the Hugeicons close icon as SVG markup). Without any JS helper: dialog.showModal() / dialog.close(), or natively <button commandfor="id" command="show-modal"> in modern browsers.

attributes.persistent: Backdrop clicks don't close it (Esc still does)

element.children: A trigger with data-ayy-open and a <dialog class="ayy-dialog"> (centred or side). Inside the dialog, data-ayy-close="value" closes it and sets dialog.returnValue.

react.import: import { Dialog, DialogTrigger, DialogContent, DialogHeader, DialogTitle, DialogDescription, DialogBody, DialogFooter, DialogClose } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";

props.side: "center" | "start" | "end" | "bottom" — start/end make a side modal on that inline edge, bottom a bottom sheet
props.hideClose: boolean — hide the corner close button
props.closeLabel: string — accessible name of the close button (translate it). Default "Close"

a11y: Always include a DialogTitle (or aria-label on the dialog).
Focus moves into the dialog on open and returns to the trigger on close (native behaviour).
Esc closes; background is inert while open; page scroll is locked. A side modal is still a modal: same rules.
A body with only text that scrolls needs tabindex="0" so keyboard users can scroll it; form fields inside make that unnecessary.
Opening and closing fade/scale (side modals slide); the closing animation is skipped in browsers without @starting-style and under reduced motion.
do: Use a dialog for short, focused tasks that must finish before continuing (rename, create).
Use a dialog to confirm a destructive action, with the destructive variant on the confirm button.
Use a side modal to edit or inspect a record without leaving the page, and for a few project options, filters or a mobile nav drawer.
Use size="full" for an app's settings: it holds the App shell in settings mode (sections in its sidebar, one section in its main) over the page the user was on.
Put the primary action last in the footer.
Use a bottom sheet on phones for a short list of actions or options on the thing just tapped (share, sort, quick settings): it sits under the thumb.
In a side modal, put the form fields in the body and submit from the footer with <button type="submit" form="form-id">.
dont: Don't use a dialog for long forms or multi-step flows — use a page. App settings are the exception: a size="full" dialog with a settings shell.
Don't use a dialog for non-blocking messages — use an Alert on the page, or a Toast for a confirmation.
Don't use a modal for a panel people keep open while they work with the page — use a layout column.
Don't open a dialog from inside another dialog.
Don't fill a bottom sheet with a long form — it stops being a quick choice; use a page or a side modal.
Don't render DialogContent's children while closed — the React component already skips them for you.

import { useState, type CSSProperties } from "react";
import {
  Button,
  Dialog,
  DialogBody,
  DialogClose,
  DialogContent,
  DialogDescription,
  DialogFooter,
  DialogHeader,
  DialogTitle,
  DialogTrigger,
  Field,
  FieldHint,
  Input,
  Label,
  Select,
  Switch,
  toast,
} from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";

export default function Example() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);

  return (
    <Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
      <DialogTrigger variant="outline">Project settings</DialogTrigger>
      {/* side="end": a full-height panel on the inline-end edge. Only the body scrolls. */}
      <DialogContent side="end">
        <DialogHeader>
          <DialogTitle>Project settings</DialogTitle>
          <DialogDescription>Marketing site. Changes apply to the next deployment.</DialogDescription>
        </DialogHeader>
        <DialogBody>
          <form
            id="project-settings-form"
            className="ayy-stack"
            style={{ "--ayy-gap": "var(--ayy-space-5)" } as CSSProperties}
            onSubmit={(event) => {
              event.preventDefault();
              setOpen(false);
              toast.success("Settings saved");
            }}
          >
            <Field>
              <Label htmlFor="settings-name">Project name</Label>
              <Input id="settings-name" name="name" defaultValue="marketing-site" required />
            </Field>
            <Field>
              <Label htmlFor="settings-region">Region</Label>
              <Select id="settings-region" name="region" defaultValue="fra1">
                <option value="fra1">Frankfurt (fra1)</option>
                <option value="iad1">Washington, D.C. (iad1)</option>
                <option value="hnd1">Tokyo (hnd1)</option>
              </Select>
            </Field>
            <Field>
              <Label htmlFor="settings-build">Build command</Label>
              <Input id="settings-build" name="build" defaultValue="pnpm build" aria-describedby="settings-build-hint" />
              <FieldHint id="settings-build-hint">Runs in the project root after install.</FieldHint>
            </Field>
            <Field>
              <Label htmlFor="settings-output">Output directory</Label>
              <Input id="settings-output" name="output" defaultValue="dist" />
            </Field>
            <Field inline>
              <Switch id="settings-autodeploy" name="autodeploy" defaultChecked />
              <Label htmlFor="settings-autodeploy">Deploy every push to main</Label>
            </Field>
            <Field inline>
              <Switch id="settings-previews" name="previews" defaultChecked />
              <Label htmlFor="settings-previews">Preview deployments for pull requests</Label>
            </Field>
          </form>
        </DialogBody>
        <DialogFooter>
          <DialogClose>Cancel</DialogClose>
          {/* A submit button outside the form reaches it through the form attribute. */}
          <Button type="submit" form="project-settings-form">
            Save changes
          </Button>
        </DialogFooter>
      </DialogContent>
    </Dialog>
  );
}

components.name: Popover
components.description: A small floating panel attached to a button, for extra content or controls that don't need a full dialog. It closes when you click outside or press Esc.

classes.ayy-popover: On the element with the popover attribute. Surface, padding, shadow, fade/scale transition.

default.looks: Closed: hidden. Open: raised surface, line-strong border, control radius, overlay shadow, sm text.

hover.none: The panel has no hover look; the trigger is a Button with its own.

pressed.none: No pressed look.

focus.none: The panel itself doesn't take a ring; focus moves to the controls inside.

disabled.none: Disable the trigger instead.

selected.none: No selected state.

error.none: Show errors inside it (FieldError).

loading.none: Put a Spinner or Skeleton inside while its content loads.

open.looks: Fades in and scales up from 97% next to its trigger (React Popover, <ayy-popover>); light-dismisses on Esc or a click outside.

sizes.density: Padding is fixed; its controls follow data-density.
sizes.width: As wide as its content, at most 22rem (or the viewport minus 1rem).

components.js: popoverClass constant; connectPopover(trigger, content, { side?, align?, offset?, crossAxisOffset?, boundary?, onToggle? }) → { open, close, isOpen, update, destroy }

element.children: A trigger <button> (optionally data-ayy-trigger) and an element with the popover attribute.

props.asChild: boolean — clone child element and merge trigger props

a11y: Give the content an accessible name (aria-label or aria-labelledby pointing at its heading).
The trigger gets aria-expanded automatically; Esc and click-outside close it and focus returns to the trigger.
It's not a focus trap — use Dialog when the user must finish something first.
do: Use a popover for small forms or details next to their trigger (share link, filters, quick edit).
Keep content short; if it scrolls, it probably wants to be a Dialog or a page.
dont: Don't use a popover for a list of actions — use Dropdown menu.
Don't use a popover for anything that must block the page — use Dialog.
Don't open popovers on hover — hover hints are a Tooltip.
Don't nest popovers more than one level.

components.name: Tooltip
components.description: A short hint that appears when someone hovers or focuses an element, for naming icon buttons or giving a little extra detail. It stays inside the screen and never gets clipped.

classes.ayy-tooltip: Wrapper around the trigger. Shows the content on :hover and :focus-within.
classes.ayy-tooltip__content: The bubble (role="tooltip"). Placement via data-side="top|bottom|start|end" (start/end follow text direction).

default.looks: Hidden. The bubble is a raised surface with a line-strong border and s text.

hover.looks: The bubble fades and slides in after 200ms.

pressed.none: No pressed look; the trigger keeps its own.

focus.looks: The bubble shows at once (no delay) while the trigger has keyboard focus. After mouse or touch use (trackInputModality()) only hover shows it.

disabled.none: A disabled button gets no focus and shows no tooltip; explain why it's disabled in visible text instead.

selected.none: No selected state.

error.none: Never put errors in a tooltip; use a FieldError.

loading.none: No loading state.

dismissed.looks: Stays hidden until the pointer and focus leave.

sizes.density: Text size follows data-density (var(--ayy-text-s)); padding is fixed.
sizes.width: As wide as its text, at most 16rem, then wraps.

components.js: tooltipClass, tooltipContentClass constants; generalActionLabel(label) extracts general verbs ("Edit", "Delete", "More actions") from specific aria-labels; enhanceTooltip(host) moves the bubble to the top layer and adds Esc (returns cleanup).

element.children: One focusable trigger and a .ayy-tooltip__content bubble. Ids and aria-describedby are wired for you.

props.children: One focusable element; aria-describedby is added for you

a11y: Trigger must be focusable so keyboard users see it too.
aria-describedby links trigger → tooltip (React does it automatically).
Esc dismisses (WCAG 1.4.13); the bubble stays open while hovered.
do: Use a tooltip to name icon-only buttons visually (they still need aria-label) and for short clarifications: shortcuts, truncated values.
Keep action tooltips general ("Edit", "Delete", "More actions", "Copy"), never specific to an item ("Edit Lumen Labs") — leave the specific item in aria-label for screen readers.
Show a shortcut with <Shortcut keys="Mod+…" /> (or .ayy-shortcut in HTML) so Mac and Windows users each see their own keys as keycaps.
Keep it under ~60 characters.
Use side="start"/"end", not left/right, so RTL works.
Inside overflow:hidden containers, use the React component or <ayy-tooltip> — the CSS-only version can be clipped there.
dont: Don't put specific names or objects in action tooltips ("Edit Project X", "Delete Northwind") — use "Edit" or "Delete" so tooltips stay short and don't duplicate visible context.
Don't put essential information in a tooltip — tooltips are invisible on touch devices.
Don't put interactive content (links, buttons) in a tooltip — use a popover or dialog.
Don't wrap disabled buttons — they can't receive focus or hover events reliably.
Don't write a shortcut as plain text like "(⌘S)" — use Shortcut so it draws keycaps.

components.name: Alert
components.description: A message placed in the flow of a page to tell someone something they should notice, like a warning, an error or a confirmation. It can carry a title, a short explanation and actions.

classes.ayy-alert--sm: Compact: 8px by 12px padding, --ayy-text-xs text, a 16px icon. For a message inside a card or a form row.
classes.ayy-alert--lg: Roomy: 16px by 20px padding, --ayy-text-md text, a 22px icon. For a page-level notice.

default.looks: Wash fill, line-strong border, control radius; semibold title, text-soft description. info, success, warning and destructive tint the icon, an 8% fill and a 35% border in their colour.

hover.none: Static; its action Buttons have their own states.

pressed.none: Not interactive.

disabled.none: Not interactive.

selected.none: Not interactive.

error.when: destructive (ayy-alert--destructive), role="alert" when it appears after an action
error.looks: Red icon, 8% red fill and 35% red border. Add a Try again action for a failed load or save.

loading.none: Not a loading indicator; use a Spinner, Progress or Skeleton.

scale.sm: 8px by 12px padding, --ayy-text-xs (13px), a 16px icon.
scale.md: 12px by 16px padding, --ayy-text-sm (14px), an 18px icon.
scale.lg: 16px by 20px padding, --ayy-text-md (16px), a 22px icon.

sizes.density: Padding and text are fixed at every density.
sizes.width: Fills its container.

The icon is decorative: aria-hidden="true". The text must carry the meaning.
do: Use an alert for page- or section-level messages that stay until they're resolved: a billing issue, read-only mode, maintenance.
Lead with what happened, then say what to do about it.
dont: Don't use an alert for confirmations that can disappear — use Toast.
Don't use an alert for field errors — put a FieldError next to the field.

components.name: Toast
components.description: A short message that appears briefly to confirm something happened. It shows above everything else on the page, including dialogs, and can carry images or previews as well as text.

classes.ayy-toaster: The shared region toast() creates (aria-live). Position via data-position; data-expanded on hover or focus.
classes.ayy-toaster__clear: "Clear all" button in the open stack's top-end corner (bottom-end under a top-positioned stack); shown only while the stack is open with two or more toasts.
classes.ayy-toast: One toast; stacked card with swipe-to-dismiss.
classes.ayy-toast--destructive: Destructive variant with cancel icon; announced with role="alert".
classes.ayy-toast--card: Card toast variant with media preview and action scrim.
classes.ayy-toast--card-split: Split card toast variant with media preview thumbnail and text content details.
classes.ayy-toast--card-split--vertical: Vertical split card toast variant with media preview stacked above text details.
classes.ayy-toast--long: Long text variant with normal text size and copy button.
classes.ayy-toast--inline: Inline feedback pill embedded in a card, toolbar, or form without a toaster region.
classes.ayy-toast--inline--busy: Busy tone for inline toast with spinner.
classes.ayy-toast--inline--error: Error tone for inline toast with alert icon.
classes.ayy-toast__copy: Copy button to copy message to clipboard.
classes.ayy-toast__image: Foreground preview image or video frame.
classes.ayy-toast__thumb: Thumbnail container for split card toast preview image.
classes.ayy-toast__scrim: Action overlay visible on card hover or focus.
classes.ayy-toast__center: Center primary and secondary action buttons.
classes.ayy-toast__status: Inline feedback pill after an action.
classes.ayy-toast__status--error: Error status tone with alert icon.

default.looks: Raised card with line-strong border, overlay shadow, and stacked offset; success, warning, destructive, and info include their status icon.

hover.looks: Deck expands vertically so all toasts fan out into readable view and timers pause across the stack. Card toast reveals action scrim. Close button gets wash-hover.

pressed.looks: Cursor changes to grabbing while dragging.

focus.looks: 2px ring, 2px offset.

disabled.none: Not disabled.

selected.none: No selected state.

error.looks: Destructive icon in destructive colour. Only for errors that need no fixing in place; form errors go inline (FieldError).

loading.none: A toast confirms; for a long task show Progress where the work happens.

leaving.looks: Drifts out to the right (translateX 28px, scale 0.95, fade out) over 280ms.

sizes.density: Doesn't follow data-density.
sizes.width: min(22rem, viewport minus 2rem) or min(28rem, viewport minus 2rem) for long text toasts, stacked in the corner given by position; card toasts are min(17.5rem, 100%).

props.title: ReactNode — message text
props.copyable: boolean — show copy button (default true for long variant)

props.ratio: number | string — the picture's shape, width ÷ height (1.6, or "1440 / 900"): the card follows it between 6.75rem and 14rem tall (sets --ayy-ratio). Default 16 / 10

props.label: string — accessible name and tooltip. Default "Dismiss"
props.tooltip: boolean — false drops the tooltip (the label stays the accessible name). Default true

CardToastAction.renders: button.ayy-hover-action.ayy-toast__action inside a Tooltip (a Hover action)

props.label: string — accessible name and tooltip
props.hint: ReactNode — after the label in the tooltip, e.g. <Shortcut keys="Mod+C" />
props.tooltip: boolean — false drops the tooltip (the label stays the accessible name). Default true

a11y: The region is aria-live="polite"; destructive toasts use role="alert".
Timers pause while the toaster stack or a toast is hovered or focused, so there's time to read it and reach its action.
Messages are set with textContent — never HTML.
do: Use NotificationToast (or toast()) to confirm something happened (Saved, Deployed) or report an async receipt needing no decision.
Say what happened in 2–5 words: "Project deleted".
Offer one Undo-style action instead of a confirmation dialog for reversible actions.
Use CardToast (toast.card()) for content previews that are visual — screenshots, screen recordings, video frames, GIFs, and image downloads.
Use the split CardToast variation when the user needs both an image preview thumbnail and file metadata (filename, dimensions, size) with direct actions.
Use InlineToast for localized contextual feedback (e.g. "Copied to clipboard", loading spinner) embedded directly within a card, toolbar, or form without triggering the toaster region.
dont: Don't use a toast for errors the user must fix — show them inline next to the problem with FieldError.
Don't use a toast for anything needing a decision — use Dialog.
Don't put long or important content in a toast — it disappears.
Don't stack several toasts for one action — reuse an id to update it.
Don't put links the user must follow in a toast.
Don't use CardToast for plain text notifications that do not have a visual preview or thumbnail.
Don't use InlineToast as a floating viewport notification — use NotificationToast in the shared toaster region instead.
Don't stack multiple InlineToasts inside one container — update the status tone and message in place.

components.name: Progress
components.description: A bar that shows how far along something is, or that work is happening when the end isn't known.

default.looks: A 6px pill track in a 10% text tint, filled in the text colour from the inline start to --ayy-value %.

hover.none: Not interactive.

pressed.none: Not interactive.

disabled.none: Not interactive; at 0 it's an empty track.

selected.none: The value is the state (--ayy-value, aria-valuenow).

error.looks: Red fill: a failed upload or an over-limit quota. Say why in text next to it.

loading.looks: A 40% bar slides along the track, unknown duration (RTL reverses it).

scale.sm: 4px track.
scale.md: 6px track.
scale.lg: 10px track.

sizes.density: Doesn't follow data-density.
sizes.width: Fills its container.

components.js: progressClass({ variant?, tone?, size?, indeterminate?, className? }) → string (tone is a deprecated alias of variant)

props.variant: "default" | "success" | "warning" | "destructive" | "ai" — the same prop name as Alert and Badge

a11y: role="progressbar" with aria-valuenow/min/max (React sets them).
Give it an accessible name: aria-label or aria-labelledby.
do: Use a progress bar when you know how far along something is: an upload, an import, a quota, a goal.
Use indeterminate for work of unknown length that takes more than ~1s.
Show the percentage or step as text nearby for anything longer than a few seconds.
For quotas or meters that aren't progress, the look still works — set role="meter" instead of progressbar.
dont: Don't use a progress bar for a short wait of unknown length on a small area — use a Spinner (or <Button loading>).
Don't use it for content that's loading — use Skeleton shapes.
Don't use it for the steps of a flow — use Steps.
Don't animate a determinate bar backwards.

components.name: Progress ring
components.description: Progress shown as a ring that fills up, for goals, timers and uploads in small spaces. It can show a known amount or an unknown one, with a value or an icon in the middle.

classes.ayy-progress-ring: Root: role="progressbar" with aria-valuenow/min/max, an accessible name and --ayy-value (0–100). Clockwise from the top in every direction, like a clock. 2.5rem.
classes.ayy-progress-ring__svg: First child: <svg viewBox="0 0 36 36" aria-hidden="true"> holding the track and the bar circles (cx=18 cy=18 r=16 pathLength=100). progressRingSvg is the markup.
classes.ayy-progress-ring__track: The full circle behind the fill.
classes.ayy-progress-ring__bar: The fill: a round-capped arc as long as --ayy-value. Hidden at aria-valuenow="0".
classes.ayy-progress-ring__label: Optional, in the middle: the value ("3/5"), a time, or an Icon. Scales with the ring; leave it out at sm.
classes.ayy-progress-ring--sm: 1.25rem, next to a line of text.
classes.ayy-progress-ring--xl: Up to 16rem (70% of a phone's width): a timer.
classes.ayy-progress-ring--indeterminate: A quarter arc going round (still under reduced motion); omit aria-valuenow and --ayy-value.

default.looks: A 10% text-colour track and a round-capped arc in the text colour, starting at the top and running clockwise to --ayy-value.

hover.none: Not interactive. Wrap it in a button if it starts or pauses something.

pressed.none: Not interactive.

focus.none: Not focusable; it's a progressbar that screen readers read. Put focus on the control next to it.

disabled.none: Not interactive. A paused timer stays at its value; say "Paused" in the label.

selected.none: Not selectable.

error.looks: The arc turns the destructive colour. Say what failed next to it, not only with colour.

loading.looks: A quarter arc spins; under reduced motion it stays still, so say what's happening in a label.

empty.looks: Only the track shows: no dot of arc at 0.

scale.sm: 20px, a thicker stroke: next to a file name or in a list row.
scale.md: 40px: a goal or a habit's day.
scale.lg: 64px: a card's main figure.
scale.xl: min(16rem, 70vw), a thin stroke and a lighter label: a focus timer's whole screen.

sizes.density: Doesn't change with data-density; pick a size.
sizes.width: Square at its size; the label in the middle scales with it.

components.js: progressRingClass({ variant?, size?, indeterminate?, className? }) → string; progressRingSvg (the SVG markup to put first inside the ring); progressRingSizes. The fill colour can be overridden with --ayy-progress-color, as on Progress.
a11y: role="progressbar" with aria-valuenow/min/max (React sets them). Give it a name with aria-label or aria-labelledby.
What the label in the middle says isn't read (a progressbar's content is presentational): put it in the name too ("Habit: 3 of 5 days this week").
The fill is drawn with the system highlight in High Contrast, the track in GrayText.
do: Use a ring where a circle means something or a bar has no room: a timer, a daily goal, a habit's week, a file's upload in a list row.
Put the number or time in the middle at md and up; next to the ring at sm.
Use success when a goal is reached, with a tick in the middle.
dont: Don't use a ring for a long task's progress across a page — a Progress bar reads more precisely.
Don't use an indeterminate ring where a Spinner fits (a button, a small area).
Don't nest rings for several values; use a Chart.

components.name: Spinner
components.description: A small loading indicator for short waits, like inside a button or beside some text. For loading a larger area, use a skeleton instead.

classes.ayy-spinner: The ring, 1.25em (matches an icon beside text), in the current text colour. Spins; stops still under reduced motion.

default.looks: Loading is its only look: a ring in currentColor (20% track, solid top) turning once a slow duration; under reduced motion it stops as a still ring.

hover.none: Not interactive.

pressed.none: Not interactive.

disabled.none: Not interactive.

selected.none: Not interactive.

error.none: Replace it with an Alert or FieldError when the work fails.

loading.when: always (it is the loading state); give it role="status" and a label, or aria-hidden inside a busy Button

scale.sm: 16px (--ayy-size-icon-sm).
scale.md: 1.25em, matching an icon beside text.
scale.lg: 32px (--ayy-size-icon-xl), 3px ring.

sizes.density: Doesn't follow data-density; md follows the font size around it.
sizes.width: Square.

components.js: spinnerClass({ size?, className? }) → string. Buttons: add aria-busy="true" and put an aria-hidden .ayy-spinner first inside (React: <Button loading>).

props.label: What's loading, for screen readers. Default "Loading" (translate it). "" makes it decorative (aria-hidden) when nearby text already says it.

a11y: A spinner on its own is a role="status" with an aria-label that says what's loading ("Loading invoices").
Inside a button, hide it (aria-hidden) and set aria-busy="true" on the button; the button's text still names it.
Mark the region that's refreshing with aria-busy="true" until the new content is in.
Under reduced motion it stops as a still ring; the label and aria-busy still say it's working.
do: Use a spinner for waits under a few seconds on a small area: a button that's saving, a panel refreshing, a lazy menu.
Put it inside the button that started the work (<Button loading>), not somewhere else on the page.
Pair a large spinner with a line of text when the wait may be longer ("Importing 2,400 contacts…").
dont: Don't use a spinner for a page or list that's loading — use Skeleton shapes of the content.
Don't use it when you know how far along the work is — use Progress.
Don't show several spinners at once; load the region as one.
Don't disable a loading button; aria-busy keeps it focusable and <Button loading> ignores repeat clicks.

components.name: Skeleton
components.description: A placeholder shaped like the content that's loading, so the page doesn't jump when the real content arrives.

classes.ayy-skeleton: Block placeholder. Set its size to match the content.

default.looks: Loading is its only look: a wash-hover block with a quiet shimmer that stops under reduced motion.

hover.none: Not interactive.

pressed.none: Not interactive.

disabled.none: Not interactive.

selected.none: Not interactive.

error.none: Replace Skeletons with an Alert and a retry when loading fails.

loading.when: always; set aria-busy="true" on the region it fills and aria-hidden on the skeletons
loading.looks: Shimmers. Forced colours: a dashed outline instead.

sizes.density: Doesn't follow data-density.
sizes.width: Size it like the content it stands in for. block fills the width at 1rem tall; text is 0.75em tall; circle is 2.5rem (an avatar).

components.js: skeletonClass({ shape?, className? }) → string
a11y: Skeletons are aria-hidden. Put aria-busy="true" on the container while loading, and remove it when content arrives. To name the loading region, give it role="status" and an aria-label — aria-label on a plain div is ignored.
The shimmer stops under prefers-reduced-motion.
do: Use a skeleton for content that takes more than ~300ms and has a predictable layout (cards, lists, profile headers).
Match the real layout closely so nothing jumps when content arrives.
dont: Don't use skeletons for unknown layouts or long jobs — use Progress.
Don't use skeletons for instant loads — skeletons that flash are worse than nothing.
Don't show skeletons for errors or empty states.

components.name: Empty state
components.description: What a list, table or page shows when it has nothing to display yet, or nothing matches a search. It explains why it's empty and offers the action that fills it.

classes.ayy-empty-state: Root. Centred column with generous block padding.
classes.ayy-empty-state--bordered: A dashed outline around the empty area (a board column, a drop target).
classes.ayy-empty-state--compact: Less padding: inside a card, a table body or a side panel.
classes.ayy-empty-state__title: What's empty, as a heading ("No projects yet").
classes.ayy-empty-state__description: One sentence: why it's empty, or what will appear here.
classes.ayy-empty-state__actions: The button that fixes it (primary), maybe a secondary link.

default.looks: Centred: an optional Icon tile, an lg heading-font title, a muted sm sentence (at most 42ch) and the action that fills it.

hover.none: Static; its action Buttons have their own states.

pressed.none: Not interactive.

disabled.none: Not interactive.

selected.none: Not interactive.

error.none: A failed load isn't empty: show an Alert with a retry instead.

loading.none: While loading show Skeletons, never an empty state.

sizes.density: Doesn't follow data-density.
sizes.width: Fills its container. compact has less padding (in a card, table cell or sidebar); bordered adds a dashed card outline for an area that will hold content.

components.js: emptyStateClass({ bordered?, compact?, className? }) → string; emptyStateTitleClass, emptyStateDescriptionClass, emptyStateActionsClass constants.

react.import: import { EmptyState, EmptyStateTitle, EmptyStateDescription, EmptyStateActions } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";

a11y: The title is a real heading at the level that fits the page (h2 under the page's h1, h3 inside a card).
The icon tile is decorative: the title carries the meaning.
When results change because of a search or filter, put the empty state inside a role="status" region (or announce the count) so screen reader users hear that nothing matched.
do: Use an empty state wherever a list, table or page can have nothing in it: first run, a finished inbox, a search with no results.
Say what will be here and give the one action that fills it (Create project, Import contacts, Clear filters).
Use the compact version inside a Card or a Table's body; the full one when it's the whole page.
Match the icon to the thing that's missing, in an IconTile.
dont: Don't use an empty state while data is loading — use Skeleton rows (or a Spinner for a small area).
Don't use it for errors — use an Alert with a retry action.
Don't leave a table with only headers and nothing under them.
Don't blame the user ("You haven't…"); say what's next.

components.name: Badge
components.description: A small label that marks the status, category or count of something, like "New" or "Paid". It can include a status dot for things that are live.

classes.ayy-badge--sm: Small: text a pixel under the default, tighter padding. For counts and tags inside dense rows.
classes.ayy-badge--lg: Large: text a pixel over the default, more padding. For a status next to a title.
classes.ayy-badge__dot: Leading status dot (first child). Pulses. Colour follows the variant, or set --ayy-dot.

default.looks: An s pill: wash fill, line-strong border, text colour. muted: hairline and muted text; outline: no fill. success, warning, destructive, info and ai: 10% tint, 30% border and text in their colour. A __dot pulses unless --static.

hover.none: A badge is a label, not a control. For a removable filter use a Chip.

pressed.none: A badge is a label, not a control. For a removable filter use a Chip.

disabled.none: A badge is a label, not a control. For a removable filter use a Chip.

selected.none: A badge is a label, not a control. For a removable filter use a Chip.

error.looks: Red text on a 10% red tint: a failed run, an overdue invoice. Pair the colour with a word.

loading.none: No loading look; a pulsing __dot shows a live state, not progress.

scale.sm: --ayy-text-s minus 1px (12px compact, 13 touch), 8px side padding.
scale.md: --ayy-text-s (13px compact, 14 touch), 10px side padding.
scale.lg: --ayy-text-s plus 1px (14px compact, 15 touch), 12px side padding and 4px block padding.

sizes.density: Text size follows data-density via --ayy-text-s; every size steps with it.
sizes.width: Hugs its text, never wraps.

components.js: badgeClass({ variant?, size?, className? }) → string
a11y: Colour is never the only signal — the label text must say the status.
The dot is aria-hidden; it's decorative.
do: Use a badge for the status of an item (Synced, Error, Beta), a category or tag next to a title, or a live indicator (dot).
Keep labels to one or two words.
Use the status variants for status, accent spotlights for categories.
dont: Don't make a badge clickable — use Button (ghost/outline, sm).
Don't put long text in a badge — badges never wrap.
Don't stack more than three badges in a row.
Don't put buttons inside badges.
