components.name: Status dot
components.description: A small coloured dot that shows the state of something, like someone being online, a live stream or a server's health.

classes.ayy-status-dot--pulse: Animated pinging ring for live/active statuses (keyframes ayy-status-dot-ping).

default.looks: A circular dot with hairline ring for contrast against light and dark backgrounds. Neutral muted colour by default.

hover.none: A status dot is a static indicator, not an interactive control.

pressed.none: A status dot is a static indicator, not an interactive control.

disabled.none: A status dot is a static indicator, not an interactive control.

selected.none: A status dot is a static indicator, not an interactive control.

error.none: Static indicator; use destructive variant (ayy-status-dot--destructive) for error or failed status.

loading.none: Static indicator; use pulse (ayy-status-dot--pulse) for live or active statuses, or Spinner for pending operations.

sizes.density: Fixed dot dimensions (6px, 8px, or 10px); does not scale with data-density.
sizes.width: Fixed square footprint matching dot dimensions.

scale.sm: 6px diameter for dense table rows or nested badges.
scale.md: 8px diameter standard dot for status rows and presence.
scale.lg: 10px diameter prominent dot for live indicators and headers.

components.js: statusDotClass({ variant?, size?, pulse?, className? }) → string

props.pulse: boolean — animated pinging ring for live/active status
props.label: string — accessible label (sets role="status" and aria-label; without it, aria-hidden="true")

a11y: Colour is never the only signal — accompany standalone status dots with a text label or pass the label prop so screen readers announce it.
When label is provided, sets role="status" and aria-label; when omitted, aria-hidden="true" treats the dot as decorative.
do: Use a status dot to indicate online presence, server or service health, or active streaming status.
Place the status dot beside a descriptive label or table cell value.
Use the pulse modifier for active or real-time statuses like live streams or ongoing recordings.
dont: Don't rely on color alone to convey meaning without an accompanying label or tooltip.
Don't make a status dot clickable directly — wrap in a button or link if interaction is required.
Don't use a status dot for counts or numerical badges — use Badge instead.

components.name: Keyboard hint
components.description: A small keycap for showing a keyboard key or shortcut in help text, menus and tooltips. Shortcuts adapt to the platform, so Mac users see their own symbols.

classes.ayy-kbd: The <kbd>: monospace, 0.75em of the surrounding text, a hairline border with a heavier bottom edge.
classes.ayy-kbd--sm: Small keycap: 0.6875em of the surrounding text. For a hint inside a small control or a menu row.
classes.ayy-kbd--lg: Large keycap: 0.875em of the surrounding text. For a hint in a help page or an empty state.

default.looks: A small keycap: wash fill, line-strong border with a 2px bottom edge, mono text-soft at 0.75em.

hover.none: A key label, not a control.

pressed.none: A key label, not a control.

disabled.none: A key label, not a control.

selected.none: A key label, not a control.

error.none: No error state.

loading.none: No loading state.

scale.sm: 0.6875em of the surrounding text (11px in 16px text).
scale.md: 0.75em of the surrounding text (12px in 16px text).
scale.lg: 0.875em of the surrounding text (14px in 16px text).

sizes.density: Scales with the text around it (1.6em tall); scales when surrounding text uses --ayy-text-s.
sizes.width: At least 1.6em wide, grows with the key name.

components.js: kbdClass and keyboardHintClass constants; kbdSizeClass(size?) → string | undefined (the --sm / --lg class; md adds nothing). platformKeyLabel(key, platform) maps modifier names to platform symbols/names ("mod" → ⌘ on Mac, Ctrl on Windows/Linux; "meta" → ⌘ on Mac, Win on Windows, Super on Linux); platformKeyName(key, platform) gives its spoken name ("Command" for ⌘).

props.size: "sm" | "md" | "lg" — stepped from the text around it
props.keyName: string — a modifier or key drawn for the platform ("mod", "meta", "alt", "ctrl", "shift", "enter", "backspace"). Symbols get an aria-label with the key's name. The server and first render draw Windows names, then the user's platform.
props.platform: "mac" | "windows" | "linux" — force a target platform instead of detecting it

props.keyName: string — optional modifier/key name to adapt ("mod", "meta", "alt", "ctrl", "shift")
props.platform: "mac" | "windows" | "linux" — force a target platform instead of detecting it

a11y: Use the <kbd> element: screen readers and search know it's a key.
Write modifier names out where symbols may not read well ("Ctrl" rather than "^"), or add aria-label="Command K" to a <kbd>⌘K</kbd> (screen readers pronounce "⌘" as "place of interest sign").
A shortcut hint doesn't replace aria-keyshortcuts on the control it triggers.
do: Use a kbd for keys people press: "Press / to search", shortcuts in a menu or tooltip, a hint in a search field (InputGroupAddon).
Use one kbd for a whole shortcut (⌘K), or one per key with a plus between them (Ctrl + Shift + P).
Adapt modifiers to the user's OS: ⌘ / ⌥ / ⇧ / ⌃ on macOS, Ctrl / Alt / Shift / Win on Windows, and Ctrl / Alt / Shift / Super on Linux (or use <Shortcut keys="Mod+K" /> / <Kbd keyName="mod" />).
Listen to event.code (physical key like 'KeyE') or use matchShortcut(event, 'Mod+E') rather than event.key === 'e' so hotkeys work across keyboard layouts and languages (e.g. Russian Cyrillic Cmd+У).
dont: Don't use a kbd for code or file names — use .ayy-code or <code class="ayy-code">.
Don't use it as a badge or a tag — use Badge.
Don't show shortcuts on touch-first screens, where there's no keyboard.
Don't hardcode Mac-only symbols (⌘) or Windows-only names (Ctrl) when targeting multiple operating systems.

scale.md: 20px.

Icons come from `npm i @hugeicons/core-free-icons`: import { Search01Icon } from "@hugeicons/core-free-icons". Plain HTML: paste the SVG with class="ayy-icon". name writes data-ayy-icon, which a pack replaces: import "@danitesler/ayywi/icons/<pack>.css" and call setIconPack(pack) (or set data-ayy-icons on any element) to draw named icons in Lucide, Tabler, Material Symbols or Feather. strokeWidth only affects the inline Hugeicons paths; a pack keeps its own stroke.

props.size: "auto" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl" — auto follows the text; the rest are 16/20/24/32px
props.directional: boolean — mirror in right-to-left text; for arrows and other icons that point along the reading direction
props.name: IconName — the glyph's name ("x", "search"…), written as data-ayy-icon so an icon pack can replace it; leave it off for your own icons
props.label: string — accessible name; without it the icon is decorative (aria-hidden)

a11y: Icons are decorative by default (aria-hidden): the text next to them carries the meaning.
When the icon is the only thing saying something (a status, a verified mark), give it a label: <Icon label="Deployed">, or role="img" + aria-label on the <svg>.
Icon-only buttons: aria-label goes on the button, the icon stays decorative.
Strokes use currentColor, so icons follow the theme and Windows High Contrast colours with no extra CSS.
do: Use an icon next to its text to help people recognise an action or item: buttons, menu items, list rows.
Use an icon with an accessible label for compact status where a word would be too long.
Import icons one by one from @hugeicons/core-free-icons; named imports tree-shake.
Let the component size icons inside buttons, menu items and alerts; use size for icons on their own.
Colour an icon through its text colour: .ayy-muted, or color: var(--ayy-color-success) on the <svg>.
Mark icons that point along the reading direction (arrows, chevrons, send, undo) directional so they mirror in RTL. Leave the rest alone: a clock or a check mark reads the same both ways.
dont: Don't use an icon for people and workspaces — use Avatar.
Don't use Icon for illustrations and logos — use an or your own SVG.
Don't rely on an icon when its meaning isn't obvious — write the word instead of (or next to) it.
Don't mix in another icon set by hand. Hugeicons' 1.5px rounded stroke is the default look; an icon pack switches every named icon at once.
Don't keep a fixed colour (color, fill or stroke set to a hex value) on an SVG you paste in: a black icon disappears in the dark theme.
Don't use colour as the only signal: pair a status icon with a label.

components.name: List
components.description: Rows of people, records or settings, each with an image or icon, a title, a description and something at the end like a value or a control. A row can be a link.

classes.ayy-list: Root <ul>. Rounded rows with a small gap between them.
classes.ayy-list--divided: Flush rows with hairlines between them: settings rows, records inside a card.
classes.ayy-list--compact: Tight rows without padding and a small icon: an icon checklist (plan perks, what's included, requirements). Rows here usually hold an Icon and plain text.
classes.ayy-list__item: The <li> row: a flex row of leading media, __content and trailing items, vertically centred. Everything but __content keeps its size.
classes.ayy-list__content: The column that holds __title and __description; it takes the free space and can shrink (add .ayy-truncate to cut long text).
classes.ayy-list__title: The row's main text, medium weight. Holds the __link when the row opens something.
classes.ayy-list__description: Supporting text under the title, muted.
classes.ayy-list__meta: Short trailing text: a time, a count, a size. Small, muted, tabular numbers.
classes.ayy-list__link: The <a> inside __title. Its ::after covers the row, so the whole row is one tab stop; other controls in the row stay clickable above it. The row gets a wash on hover, a ring on focus, and a stronger tint and heavier title with aria-current="page" (or "true").

default.looks: Rows of leading media, a medium-weight title over a muted description, and muted xs meta, with 12px padding and lg radius. divided: flush rows between hairlines; compact: tight icon rows.

hover.looks: A row with a __link gets a wash fill. Rows without one don't react.

pressed.none: No pressed look.

focus.looks: The ring goes around the whole row, inset by 2px.

disabled.none: Rows aren't disabled; leave the link out of a row that can't open, and disable controls inside it.

selected.looks: The row you're on: wash-hover fill and a semibold title, as the App shell's current link. Forced colours: Highlight. For multi-select rows put a Checkbox in the row.

error.none: No error look; show a failed load as an Alert in place of the list.

loading.none: No loading look; show Skeleton rows (circle plus two text lines) with aria-busy on the list.

sizes.density: Padding and sm text are fixed; row meta text follows data-density via --ayy-text-s; controls in rows follow data-density.
sizes.width: Fills its container; titles and descriptions wrap, meta stays on one line.

components.js: listClass({ divided?, compact?, className? }) → string; listItemClass, listContentClass, listTitleClass, listDescriptionClass, listMetaClass, listLinkClass constants.

react.import: import { List, ListItem, ListContent, ListTitle, ListDescription, ListMeta, ListLink } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";

props.compact: boolean — tight rows for an icon checklist.

props.htmlFor: The id of the row's Switch or Checkbox: the title becomes its <label>.

a11y: It's a real list: screen readers announce how many rows there are.
One link per row, in the title, so a row is one tab stop with a meaningful name. Buttons and switches in the row are separate tab stops after it.
Mark the open row with aria-current="page" (it's a page) or "true" (a selection in a list-detail view); it gets a tint and a heavier title, not just colour.
A switch or checkbox in a settings row needs its label: make the title a <label for> pointing at it.
Avatars and icons in the leading slot are decorative when the title names the row.
do: Use a list for a feed of similar things people scan and open: conversations, notifications, files, members, search results.
Use List divided for settings: a title and description per row, the Switch or Button at the end.
Use List compact for a short checklist with an icon per row: plan perks, what's included, password rules.
Keep the same slots on every row: if one row has an avatar, they all do.
Put the time or count in ListMeta, and a status in a Badge at the end.
Cut long descriptions to one line with .ayy-truncate in inboxes and pickers.
dont: Don't use a list for data people compare across columns — use a Table.
Don't use it for the site or app navigation — use the App shell or Navbar.
Don't put two links in a row's title, or wrap the whole <li> in an <a>.

components.name: Property list
components.description: A record's attributes as a definition list: a muted term (an icon and a label) and its value, side by side, wrapping under each other when the value doesn't fit.

classes.ayy-property-list: Root <dl>. Rows stack with no gap; the rows own the padding.
classes.ayy-property-list--compact: Tight rows: 6px block padding instead of 12px and a 7rem term basis instead of 8rem.
classes.ayy-property-list__row: The <div> that holds one <dt> and one <dd>: a wrapping flex row with the term at an 8rem basis and the value taking the rest.
classes.ayy-property-list__term: The <dt>: a decorative icon and the label, at an 8rem basis and in --ayy-color-muted. The term never grows; the value takes the remaining width.
classes.ayy-property-list__label: The label inside the term. Wraps inside the term's column.
classes.ayy-property-list__icon: An optional Icon before the label: 16px, muted, never shrinks. Decorative, so the label names the row.
classes.ayy-property-list__value: The <dd>: the value in --ayy-color-text. Long words wrap inside it (overflow-wrap: anywhere) instead of overflowing.
classes.ayy-property-list__empty: What an empty value reads ("Not set"): muted, in place of the value.

default.looks: Muted, icon-led terms in an 8rem column and text-coloured values beside them, each row with 12px block padding and no hairline.

hover.none: Rows aren't interactive; a nested InlineEdit keeps its own hover.

pressed.none: Rows aren't interactive; their nested controls keep their own pressed look.

focus.none: Rows aren't focusable; their nested controls keep their focus rings.

disabled.none: The list doesn't disable; disable the control in a value, or drop the row.

selected.none: Not a choice control; use List or a Table with selected rows.

error.none: No error look; a value that failed validation nests a FieldError or an InlineEdit with aria-invalid on its field.

loading.none: No loading look; show Skeleton rows with aria-busy on the list.

empty.looks: The __empty span takes --ayy-color-muted instead of a blank value; forced colours draw it as GrayText.

sizes.density: Row text follows data-density through --ayy-text-s (13px compact and comfortable, 14px touch). compact swaps the 12px block padding for 6px.
sizes.width: Fills its container. The term takes an 8rem basis (7rem compact) and the value 10rem; when they don't fit together the value wraps under its term. Long unbroken values wrap inside the value.

components.js: propertyListClass({ compact?, className? }) → string; propertyListRowClass, propertyListTermClass, propertyListLabelClass, propertyListIconClass, propertyListValueClass, propertyListEmptyClass constants.

props.compact: boolean — tight rows with a shorter term column, for a dense summary.

props.label: ReactNode (required) — the term's text.
props.icon: ReactNode — an Icon before the label (give it className="ayy-property-list__icon").
props.empty: boolean — there is no value: show emptyText muted instead of children.
props.emptyText: ReactNode — what an empty value reads. Default "Not set".

a11y: It's a real <dl>: screen readers announce a definition list and pair each term with its value.
Each row is a <div> inside the <dl> (valid HTML) with exactly one <dt> and one <dd>, so the rows can wrap and flex.
Icons in the term are decorative; the label names the row.
An empty value says "Not set" in text, not a dash or a blank cell.
A value edited in place keeps the nested InlineEdit's own label ("Change the version"); the term names the attribute, the control names the action.
do: Use a property list for a record's attributes: a project, a server, an order, a person.
Keep terms short and values plain; nest a control only for a value edited in place.
Use PropertyRow empty and emptyText when there is no value, so the row stays and reads as empty.
Use compact inside a card header or a dense summary.
dont: Don't use it for rows that open something or carry actions at the end — use List.
Don't use it for preferences with a control per row — use Settings.
Don't use it for values people compare across columns — use Table.
Don't hand-build the rows: the <dt>/<dd> pairing is what screen readers announce.

components.name: Swipe actions
components.description: A list row that slides sideways to reveal actions, the way phone mail and task apps do. It works with touch, mouse and keyboard, and follows the reading direction.

classes.ayy-swipe: The row: clips its content and holds the trays. Vertical drags still scroll the page (touch-action: pan-y).
classes.ayy-swipe__content: What slides: the row's own content (often with .ayy-list__item). Opaque, with --ayy-swipe-bg (default the page colour) so the trays stay hidden under it.
classes.ayy-swipe__actions: A tray of buttons under the row, after the content in the DOM. Shows over the row while it holds keyboard focus.
classes.ayy-swipe__actions--start: At the inline start: revealed by swiping toward the inline end (right in English). One positive action (Done, Read).
classes.ayy-swipe__actions--end: At the inline end: revealed by swiping toward the inline start. Up to three (Pin, Snooze, Delete), the destructive one last.
classes.ayy-swipe__action: A <button> filling the tray's height: an icon over a short label, on a tint of its colour.

default.looks: The row as it is; its trays are hidden underneath until it slides.

hover.none: No hover look; swiping works with a mouse too, and Tab reaches the buttons.

pressed.none: No pressed look on the actions; they run at once.

focus.looks: Tabbing into a tray shows it over the row, and the action gets a ring inside its edge.

disabled.none: Don't offer an action that can't run; leave it out of the tray.

selected.none: Rows select through the list they're in (aria-selected on the item), not through the swipe.

error.none: If an action fails, close the tray and say so in a toast.

loading.none: Actions run at once (optimistic); undo through the toast.

open.looks: The row has slid to show the start tray (swiped toward the inline end) or the end tray.

dragging.looks: The row follows the finger with no transition.

sizes.density: Actions are at least 4.5rem wide and as tall as the row; the row keeps its own density.
sizes.width: Fills the list's width, like the row it wraps.

components.js: connectSwipe(row, { onOpenChange? }) → { open(side), close(), destroy() } wires the gesture on plain markup: drag past half a tray to keep it open; a tap on the row, a tap elsewhere, Esc or an action closes it. swipeActionClass({ variant?, className? }); swipeActionVariants; swipeClass, swipeContentClass, swipeActionsClass constants.

element.description: Wraps an .ayy-swipe row and wires the gesture. Methods: open("start" | "end"), close().

events.ayy-open-change: { side } — "start", "end" or null when the row closes.

props.startActions: ReactNode — SwipeActions revealed by swiping toward the inline end
props.endActions: ReactNode — SwipeActions revealed by swiping toward the inline start
props.contentProps: HTMLAttributes — props for the sliding content (className="ayy-list__item")

props.icon: ReactNode — an Icon above the label

a11y: Swiping is a shortcut, never the only way: offer the same actions in the row's page or a Menu, since many people can't or don't swipe.
The actions are real buttons after the content in the tab order; a tray with focus shows over the row, and Esc closes an open row.
Labels stay visible under the icons, so the tint isn't the only cue.
Undo destructive actions (a Toast with Undo) rather than asking for confirmation in the middle of a gesture.
do: Use it on phone lists for the two or three things people do to rows most: Done, Snooze, Delete.
Put the positive action at the start and the destructive one last at the end, as mail apps do.
Set --ayy-swipe-bg to the surface the list sits on (a card) so the row hides its trays.

components.name: Timeline
components.description: A list of events in time order, like a history, a changelog or a project's milestones, joined by a vertical line with status markers and timestamps.

classes.ayy-timeline--alternate: Alternates timeline items between start and end sides across a centered vertical track.
classes.ayy-timeline__item: Single event entry row containing the track and content.

classes.ayy-timeline__time: Muted timestamp or date with tabular numbers.
classes.ayy-timeline__title: Heading or summary of the event.
classes.ayy-timeline__body: Supporting text, description, or status badge for the event.

hover.none: Timeline items are non-interactive by default; links or buttons inside content handle their own hover states.

pressed.none: No pressed state on timeline items.

focus.none: Timeline items do not receive focus; place interactive elements like links or buttons inside content.

disabled.none: Timeline events are informational history and cannot be disabled.

selected.none: Use pulse on the current or live event marker instead of a selection state.

error.none: No error state on the timeline itself; use an Alert or status Badge inside the event body.

loading.none: No loading state on the timeline; use a Skeleton or Spinner while events are loading.

pulse.looks: A status ring expands outward from the marker and fades, looping continuously to indicate a live or in-progress event.

sizes.density: Markers and spacing are fixed; timestamp text follows data-density via --ayy-text-s; controls or badges inside event content follow data-density.
sizes.width: Fills its container. In alternate mode, centers the track with 1fr columns on either side above 36rem, collapsing to a single start-aligned column below 36rem.

a11y: Rendered as an ordered list (<ol>) by default so screen readers announce the item count and sequence.
Timestamps use the semantic <time> element with tabular numbers for consistent alignment and screen reader comprehension.
Decorative markers and track lines are marked aria-hidden="true" to prevent screen reader noise; important status information should be in the title or body.
Active pulse rings are visual enhancements; screen readers receive the active status via text in the title, body, or an accessible badge.
Supports Windows High Contrast mode via @media (forced-colors: active) with system CanvasText, Canvas, and Highlight colors.
do: Use a timeline to show a chronological log or sequence of events: deploy history, shipment tracking, audit trails, activity feeds.
Use TimelineMarker pulse on the latest or currently active event in a running process.
Use Timeline alternate for milestones, company history, or changelogs on wide marketing or overview pages.
Include TimelineTime with a semantic timestamp so users can anchor events in time.
Keep markers consistent within a timeline: all dots, or all icons, or all avatars.
dont: Don't use a timeline for a multi-step user task with future steps — use Steps.
Don't use it for navigation or hierarchical page links — use Breadcrumb.
Don't wrap entire items in clickable links — place interactive links or buttons inside TimelineTitle or TimelineBody.
Don't hardcode colors on markers or lines; use semantic tokens or status badges.

components.name: Table
components.description: Data table with quiet hairlines, muted sentence-case headers and hover rows, styled on plain table elements under .ayy-table. Optional frame with toolbar and pager; densities, column lines, sticky header, pinned and resizable columns; sortable, selectable (including drag-to-select across rows), expandable, grouped, linked and disabled rows; column menus with icons, insertion and wrapping; inline editable, empty, truncated and media cells; row actions. Cell content stays inside its column and ends in … unless the column wraps.

classes.ayy-table-container: Optional bordered frame on the page colour: .ayy-table__toolbar, the .ayy-table-wrap, a .ayy-table__pager. With a max-block-size its table scrolls inside.
classes.ayy-table__toolbar: Bar above the table: a __heading and __tools.
classes.ayy-table__tools: Toolbar's end cluster: search, filters, a columns menu, a button.
classes.ayy-table__pager: Bar under the table: the range shown and a Pagination.
classes.ayy-table--sticky: Header and footer rows stick while the wrap or container scrolls.
classes.ayy-table--reorderable: Draggable header cells that reorder columns on drop.
classes.ayy-table__draggable: On a th: indicates this column header can be dragged to reorder columns.
classes.ayy-table__column-header: Flex row holding the column label, optional icon and column menu.
classes.ayy-table__column-label: Column label or sort button; takes the room the menu leaves and ends in … when the column is narrower.
classes.ayy-table__column-icon: Optional icon before a column's label.
classes.ayy-table__add-column: Narrow trailing column with an accessible add-column button.
classes.ayy-table__wrap: On th/td: content wraps within the column instead of staying on one line and ending in ….
classes.ayy-table__num: On th/td with numbers: end-aligned, tabular digits.
classes.ayy-table__sort: A <button> inside a sortable <th> (or, with aria-haspopup="menu", the title that opens the column menu), its label in a __column-label, the whole header cell clickable, an arrow after the text only once sorted. aria-sort on the <th> marks the sorted column.
classes.ayy-table__resize: Column resize separator (<span tabindex="0">) at a header cell's end: drag, arrow keys; double-click resets.
classes.ayy-table__select: On the th/td holding a row's checkbox (and the select-all box): as narrow as the box.
classes.ayy-table__reorder: On the th/td holding a row's .ayy-drag-handle: as narrow as the handle. The row drags by it; a primary line shows where it lands.
classes.ayy-table__pin: On a column's th/td: sticks to the inline start when scrolling sideways.
classes.ayy-table__pin--end: With __pin: sticks to the inline end.
classes.ayy-table__truncate: On a <span> in a cell: one line ending in …, at most --ayy-table-truncate (16rem).
classes.ayy-table__edit: On an Inline edit (.ayy-inline-edit) in a cell: editable text that reads like cell text at rest, outlines on hover, turns into a field in place with the text where it was, saves on Enter or blur and reverts on Escape.
classes.ayy-table__media: Flex row in a cell: an Avatar or icon, then text.
classes.ayy-table__secondary: Muted second line in a cell.
classes.ayy-table__expand: Chevron <button aria-expanded> that shows the __detail row after its row.
classes.ayy-table__detail: The <tr> after an expandable row; hidden while its __expand is aria-expanded="false".
classes.ayy-table__group: A <tr> heading a group: one <th colspan scope="rowgroup"> with its label in a <span>. One per <tbody>.
classes.ayy-table__empty: On the <td colspan> of a body's only row when nothing matches.
classes.ayy-table__row-link: The row's main <a>; its ::after covers the row. Other controls stay above it.
classes.ayy-table__actions: On the trailing th/td holding row actions: end-aligned, narrow.
classes.ayy-table__row-actions: Cluster of row action buttons and the ⋯ menu trigger.
classes.ayy-table__row-actions--reveal: Shows only on row hover, focus, selection or open menu (always on touch).

hover.when: tbody tr:hover; the sort, expand, resize and edit controls; a row link

error.looks: Destructive border on an invalid inline edit field.

loading.looks: Body rows fade to 50%; first loads use Skeleton rows.

sorted.looks: Label turns text colour; only the arrow that applies shows.

expanded.looks: Chevron points up; the detail row shows.

do: Use a table to compare items across the same attributes.
End-align numbers with numeric; a cell keeps to one line, so put the full text in its title and add wrap to a column that must show it all.
Make scanned columns sortable; put the raw value in data-sort-value when the cell shows a formatted one.
Frame a working table with TableContainer: title, search and a columns menu above, Pagination below.

Compose a column menu with TableHead menu and icon, or make the title itself the trigger (a .ayy-table__sort button with aria-haspopup="menu" as the TableHead child, set aria-sort on the th): clicking the title opens the menu, which holds a Sort submenu, Duplicate, Hide and Delete, and dragging it still reorders. data-column-action wires sort-ascending/sort-descending (a Sort submenu), duplicate, hide, delete, freeze, wrap, icon, insert-before/after, add and shared filter/group controls. Return false from onColumnAction or cancel ayy-column-action to own the data changes.
Pin the name column on wide tables; use sticky with a max-block-size on long ones.
Use expandable rows for details that don't deserve a column, and group rows to split a list by status or date.
Put quick actions and a ⋯ DropdownMenu in a trailing actions cell; pair selection with an ActionBar for bulk actions.
Show TableEmpty with an EmptyState when a search matches nothing.
dont: Don't use tables for layout, or for rows with one attribute — use a List.
Don't zebra-stripe; hairlines and hover are enough.
Don't nest controls in every cell — one trailing actions column is plenty.
Don't put a row link in a pinned cell: its cover stays inside the sticky cell.
Don't resize columns under a header with more than one row.

components.name: Grid
components.description: A grid of cards that can be selected, for media, projects, posts and records. It combines card selection, quick actions on each item and a select-all control, and works with the Action bar.

classes.ayy-grid-wrap: Stack wrapper grouping the grid toolbar, the card grid and the floating Action bar.
classes.ayy-grid__toolbar: Header bar above the grid holding the select-all checkbox, count and sorting or view controls.
classes.ayy-grid__select-all: Labelled select-all checkbox control in the grid toolbar.
classes.ayy-grid: Responsive CSS grid container: as many card columns of at least --ayy-min (16rem) as fit.
classes.ayy-grid--compact: Dense variant (--ayy-min: 13rem, tighter gap and card padding) for media libraries and directories.
classes.ayy-grid__item: Selectable record card (<article>). Highlights with a 2px text-colour border and tint when aria-selected="true".
classes.ayy-grid__media: Top preview frame for images, screenshots, social post visuals or video thumbnails. Floating glass corners when .ayy-grid__select or .ayy-grid__actions sit inside.
classes.ayy-grid__header: Top block of the card holding the checkbox, avatar/icon, title, description and item actions.
classes.ayy-grid__select: Wrapper for the card's selection Checkbox (inline in the header or floating in the top-start corner of .ayy-grid__media).
classes.ayy-grid__actions: Cluster of quick action buttons (Edit, Copy) and the ⋯ DropdownMenu trigger (inline in the header or floating in the top-end corner of .ayy-grid__media).
classes.ayy-grid__actions--reveal: Reveals item actions when the card is hovered, focused within, selected or has an open menu (stays visible on touch screens).
classes.ayy-grid__description: Muted subtitle, handle or supporting metadata line.
classes.ayy-grid__body: Card body content between header and footer.
classes.ayy-grid__footer: Bottom bar for status Badges, timestamps or avatars, pinned to the bottom of stretched cards.

default.looks: Responsive grid of surface cards with line borders, rest shadow, optional top media preview, header, body and hairline footer.

hover.looks: Card border turns line-hover and reveals .ayy-grid__actions--reveal.

pressed.none: No pressed look; clicking a selectable card or its checkbox toggles selection on release.

focus.looks: Reveals .ayy-grid__actions--reveal while any checkbox, button or menu trigger inside the card has keyboard focus.

disabled.none: Cards aren't disabled; disable the controls inside them.

selected.looks: Text-colour border plus a 1px ring and a 4% text tint over the surface. Forced colours: Highlight outline.

error.none: Show a failed load as an Alert with a retry instead of the grid.

loading.none: No loading look; render Skeleton cards in the grid layout with aria-busy on the container.

sizes.density: Card padding is fixed (16px, 12px when compact); checkboxes and action buttons inside follow data-density.
sizes.width: Fills its container with auto-fitting columns at least --ayy-min wide (16rem default, 13rem compact).

components.js: gridClass({ compact?, className? }) → string; gridItemActionsClass({ reveal?, className? }) → string; gridWrapClass, gridToolbarClass, gridSelectAllClass, gridItemClass, gridMediaClass, gridHeaderClass, gridSelectClass, gridActionsClass, gridTitleClass, gridDescriptionClass, gridBodyClass, gridFooterClass constants; connectGrid(root, { onSelectionChange? }) wires select-all, card checkboxes, card-body click selection and Shift+click range selection (used by <ayy-grid>).

element.description: Wraps an .ayy-grid-wrap or .ayy-grid. Wires the .ayy-grid__select-all checkbox (including indeterminate state), each card's .ayy-grid__select checkbox, card-body click-to-select, and Shift+click range selection.

react.import: import { GridWrap, GridToolbar, GridSelectAll, Grid, GridItem, GridItemMedia, GridItemHeader, GridItemSelect, GridItemActions, GridItemTitle, GridItemDescription, GridItemBody, GridItemFooter } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";

props.compact: boolean — denser cards and 13rem minimum column width

props.onSelectedChange: (selected: boolean) => void — toggles selection when the card body is clicked

props.reveal: boolean — reveal on card hover, focus-within or selection (stays visible on touch)

a11y: Each selectable card contains a native Checkbox in GridItemSelect with an aria-label naming the item ("Select Hero screenshot").
Selected cards carry aria-selected="true" and a 2px border (Highlight outline in High Contrast mode), never colour alone.
Per-card icon buttons and ⋯ DropdownMenu triggers carry an aria-label naming the item ("More actions for Hero screenshot").
GridItemActions with reveal uses opacity so controls remain in the Tab order and become visible on :focus-within.
do: Use Grid when items are browsed visually or as cards — media assets, screenshots, social media posts, projects and user records — and need multi-select and per-item actions like a Table.
Put GridItemSelect and GridItemActions inside GridItemMedia for visual cards (screenshots, media, social posts), or inside GridItemHeader for record cards (projects, users).
Provide a ⋯ DropdownMenu on each card for targeted secondary actions (Edit, Duplicate, Copy, Archive, Delete) and an ActionBar at the bottom for bulk actions on selected cards.
dont: Don't use Grid for static marketing feature tiles that aren't selectable records — use plain Cards in an .ayy-grid layout.
Don't use Grid for single-choice form inputs (like picking a pricing plan) — use ChoiceCard.
Don't hide the selection checkbox on selected cards.

components.name: Chart
components.description: Charts for reading data at a glance: bars, lines, areas, pies and donuts, scatters, gauges and more. They're drawn with plain markup and CSS instead of a charting library, and each comes with a data table for screen readers. Colours, hover details and a switchable legend are built in.

classes.ayy-chart: Root, usually a <figure>. A grid of the plot, the labels, the legend and the data table.
classes.ayy-chart--stacked: A column's bars sit on top of each other; each bar's --ayy-value is its share of the top of the scale.
classes.ayy-chart--values: Print every bar's data-value above it (otherwise only on hover).
classes.ayy-chart--horizontal: One row per label with the bars along the reading direction: the __labels sit beside the plot, ticks become lines down it with their labels under it. Works with --stacked. Rows are 2rem.
classes.ayy-chart--histogram: Columns touch (1px apart) and fill their bins, so they read as one distribution. Label each column with its bin's start; the labels sit at the start of their column.
classes.ayy-chart--combo: Columns with lines over them: the columns split the width with no gap, so a line from chartPath(values, { band: true }) passes over their centres. Colour each line series with the next chart token (--ayy-chart-color on its __series).
classes.ayy-chart--waterfall: Floating bars, rounded at both ends and fading like any bar: each __bar starts at --ayy-start (the running total before it, 0–100) and is --ayy-value tall. Use with --values so the signed changes show.
classes.ayy-chart--pie: A solid pie: the __slice circles take r="25" and are stroked to the centre. No __total.
classes.ayy-chart--gauge: A half ring over the top (viewBox="0 0 100 50"), filled from the start side: a __track behind one __slice (or a few), with a __total under the arc. Put role="meter" and its aria-value* on the __plot.
classes.ayy-chart--radar: A square plot of an __svg with __grid rings and spokes, a __series per shape (closed __area and __line paths from chartRadar()) and an __label per spoke.
classes.ayy-chart__plot: The drawing area (aria-hidden="true"). Height from --ayy-chart-height (default 12rem); square for a donut, pie or radar, half as tall for a gauge. Holds ticks and __bars, an __svg, __series of __dots or a __ring.
classes.ayy-chart__tick: A value line across the plot, its text the label in the gutter. --ayy-value places it: 0 is the floor, 100 the top. The gutter only appears when there are ticks.
classes.ayy-chart__bars: Row of columns filling the plot.
classes.ayy-chart__column: One label's bars, side by side (or stacked).
classes.ayy-chart__bar: A bar, fading toward its base (a lighter fade when stacked): --ayy-value is its height, data-value its text on hover, --ayy-start lifts it off the floor (a floating bar). Its colour is chart-1, chart-2… by position in the column; --ayy-chart-color overrides.
classes.ayy-chart__bar--up: A waterfall's rise: the success colour.
classes.ayy-chart__bar--down: A waterfall's drop: the destructive colour.
classes.ayy-chart__svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 100 100" preserveAspectRatio="none"> stretched over the plot, for lines and areas. Mirrors in RTL.
classes.ayy-chart__series: One series: a <g> around its area and line in an __svg, or a <div> of its __dots in a scatter. Coloured chart-1, chart-2… in order; --ayy-chart-color overrides.
classes.ayy-chart__series--compare: A comparison series (last period, a target): dashed, quiet, no fill.
classes.ayy-chart__line: <path> of the line, 2px whatever the stretch (vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke).
classes.ayy-chart__area: <path> of the area under the line: a 16% tint of the series colour, or fill="url(#…)" an __gradient in its series to fade out toward the floor (React does).
classes.ayy-chart__gradient: A gradient with two <stop>s in a <defs>, taking the series colour: a <linearGradient x2="0" y2="1"> inside a line or area series fades 32% at the top to none at the floor (50% to 18% when stacked); a <radialGradient> in a radar runs 6% at the centre to 42% at the rim; in a ring, a <linearGradient x2="1" y2="1"> given the slice's colour as --ayy-chart-color is the circle's stroke="url(#…)", full strength to 55% across the ring (React draws all of these).
classes.ayy-chart__labels: The labels under the plot (aria-hidden="true"), one per column (beside it when horizontal); under a line or a scatter they spread from the first value to the last.
classes.ayy-chart__axis: An axis name (aria-hidden="true"): before the plot it names the vertical axis, after the __labels the horizontal one, at the end.
classes.ayy-chart__dot: A scatter point (a <span> in a <div class="ayy-chart__series">): --ayy-x and --ayy-y (0–100) place it, --ayy-z (0–100) makes it a bubble up to 3rem across, filled with a fading tint of the series colour, a __tooltip inside it is its card on hover (data-value alone still prints a one-line label).
classes.ayy-chart__ring: <svg viewBox="0 0 100 100"> of a donut or pie ("0 0 100 50" for a gauge), filling the __plot. Turned so slices start at the top and run clockwise.
classes.ayy-chart__track: <circle cx="50" cy="50" r="40" pathLength="100"> behind a gauge's slices: the empty part, a faint wash.
classes.ayy-chart__slice: <circle cx="50" cy="50" r="40" pathLength="100"> (r="25" in a pie): a dash --ayy-value long that starts --ayy-start along the ring (chartSlices() gives both), with a hairline gap after it. Coloured chart-1, chart-2… in order; --ayy-chart-color overrides.
classes.ayy-chart__total: The number in the middle of a donut, or under a gauge's arc: an __total-value and a caption after it.
classes.ayy-chart__total-value: The total itself, in the text colour and xl.
classes.ayy-chart__grid: <path> of a radar's rings and spokes, a hairline.
classes.ayy-chart__label: A label in the plot at --ayy-x / --ayy-y, set outward from the centre (a radar's spoke names).
classes.ayy-chart__tooltip: The card a hover opens over its parent: a __column, a __hit, a __dot, a radar's __label, a funnel step, a gauge's __plot, or (after a ring, with --ayy-x / --ayy-y over its slice) a donut or pie slice. A __tooltip-title, then a __tooltip-row for each series. data-side="end" puts it on the other side of a column or point, for the later half. Hover only: the drawing is aria-hidden and the data table carries the numbers.
classes.ayy-chart__tooltip--static: A card laid out in the flow and always shown (a ChartTooltip with `static`), for a key or a docs page instead of opening over a chart part.
classes.ayy-chart__tooltip-title: The card's heading (a label, a slice's name): semibold over a hairline.
classes.ayy-chart__tooltip-row: One series in the card: an __swatch, an optional __tooltip-name and a __tooltip-value. --ayy-chart-color sets the swatch.
classes.ayy-chart__tooltip-name: What the number is ("Comments"), followed by a colon.
classes.ayy-chart__tooltip-value: The number, semibold with tabular digits.
classes.ayy-chart__hits: Over a line or area chart's plot: a row of invisible __hit strips, one per label. --ayy-count says how many.
classes.ayy-chart__hit: A strip centred on one label's point (--ayy-x: 0 at the start, 100 at the end): on hover it draws a hairline, shows a __marker per series and opens its __tooltip.
classes.ayy-chart__marker: A ring on a series' line at a hovered __hit, --ayy-y high (0–100), in the series colour.
classes.ayy-chart__legend: List of the series, when there's more than one (aria-hidden="true" when a data table names them, and when its entries aren't buttons).
classes.ayy-chart__legend-toggle: A <button aria-pressed> inside a legend item, in place of its bare content: pressed means the series is on, aria-pressed="false" dims it, strikes its name through and hollows its swatch. Switch the same-numbered series off with data-hidden (React's `toggle` prop and the helper in @danitesler/ayywi/elements do).
classes.ayy-chart__legend-item: A series name with its swatch, coloured in the same order as the series.
classes.ayy-chart__legend-item--compare: Legend entry for a comparison series: a dashed swatch.
classes.ayy-chart__legend-item--line: Legend entry for a line over columns (a combo): a short solid line for a swatch.
classes.ayy-chart__swatch: The colour square in a legend item.
classes.ayy-chart__legend-value: A number at the end of a legend item (a slice's share), tabular digits.
classes.ayy-bar-list: <ol> of ranked rows (top pages, sources) with the bar behind the text. Readable as it is.
classes.ayy-bar-list__item: A row; --ayy-value is the bar's length (100 = the largest). The bar fades along the row.
classes.ayy-bar-list__label: The row's name (or a link), cut with an ellipsis.
classes.ayy-sparkline: A small <svg viewBox="0 0 100 100" preserveAspectRatio="none"> line with no axes, for a stat or a table cell. Uses __line and __area paths.
classes.ayy-heatmap: A grid of cells (aria-hidden="true", in a figure.ayy-chart with a data table): --ayy-columns says how many columns. Its __rows hold a row label and the cells; a last row of an empty span and __labels names the columns.
classes.ayy-heatmap__row: A row: its first child is the row's __label, the rest are __cells (or column __labels). Lays its children on the heatmap's columns.
classes.ayy-heatmap__label: A row's name (first in its row, at the end of its column) or a column's name, centred under it and free to spill into empty neighbours: name every other column when they're narrow.
classes.ayy-heatmap__cell: A cell taking --ayy-value % of the series colour over a faint wash; data-value is its text on hover. --ayy-chart-color changes the colour.
classes.ayy-heatmap__key: "Less □□□□□ More" under the heatmap: two words around a few __cells (--ayy-value 0, 25, 50, 75, 100). aria-hidden="true".
classes.ayy-funnel: <ol> of the steps people drop out of, readable as it is: label, a centred bar, the value and the rate.
classes.ayy-funnel__step: A step; --ayy-value is its bar's width (100 = the first, largest step).
classes.ayy-funnel__label: The step's name, cut with an ellipsis.
classes.ayy-funnel__bar: An empty <span>: the bar, centred, in the series colour.
classes.ayy-funnel__rate: Its share of the step before (or of the first), muted. Add what it's a share of in an .ayy-sr-only span.

default.looks: Bars, lines, areas, dots, slices or cells in --ayy-chart-1… in order, muted s labels, hairline ticks; the drawing is aria-hidden and the numbers live in a table.

hover.looks: A column's bars and a slice mix 20% toward the text colour; a column takes a wash, opens its card and its bars stop printing their data-value; a point on a line shows a hairline and a marker per series; a dot fills solid and a cell takes a text-colour outline; each opens its __tooltip card (a cell, its data-value) on a raised surface.

pressed.none: Not interactive.

focus.looks: A 2px outline in --ayy-color-ring around a legend entry that switches a series off; the plot itself isn't focusable (the data table, the funnel's own text or the gauge's meter carries the numbers).

disabled.none: Not interactive.

selected.looks: A series switched off from the legend: its name in --ayy-color-muted, struck through, with a hollow swatch; the series carries data-hidden and leaves the plot while the scale stays.

error.none: No error look; show an Alert in its place.

loading.none: Use a block Skeleton of the chart's height while data loads; bars, slices and funnel steps grow from 0 when they appear.

sizes.density: The plot is --ayy-chart-height (12rem) tall; a donut or pie is that wide and square, a gauge that wide and half as tall, a radar 16rem square; horizontal rows are 2rem; bar-list rows and funnel bars are the sm control height; a sparkline is 6rem × 1.75rem. Chart labels and legend text follow data-density via --ayy-text-s.
sizes.width: Fills its container; columns share the width (bars at most 2.5rem wide, histogram bins all of it). A donut's legend sits beside it and wraps under it in a narrow box; a radar leaves 5rem each side for its spoke names.

components.js: chartScale(values, { ticks?, min?, max? }) → { min, max, ticks } with a round top; chartPercent(value, max, min?) → 0–100 for --ayy-value; chartPath(values, { min?, max?, smooth?, step?, band?, base? }) → { line, area } path data for the 0 0 100 100 box (step: steps; band: points over column centres; base: the area's floor, for stacking); chartStack(series, { percent? }) → each series' running top; chartBins(values, { bins?, min?, max? }) → { edges, counts } for a histogram; chartSlices(values, { total? }) → [{ start, value }] shares for ring slices; chartRadar(values, { min?, max? }) → a closed path and chartRadarPoint(index, count, share?, radius?) → { x, y } for spokes and labels; chartWaterfall(steps) → [{ from, to, change }]; chartColors(target?, count?) → resolved rgb() strings and chartTheme(target?) → { colors, text, muted, grid, surface, fontFamily } for canvas libraries (Chart.js, ECharts); chartClass({ stacked?, values?, horizontal?, type?, className? }) with type one of chartTypes (histogram, combo, waterfall, pie, gauge, radar), chartSeriesClass({ compare?, className? }), chartLegendItemClass({ compare?, line?, className? }) and part class constants. toggleChartLegend(button) is what @danitesler/ayywi/elements runs when an .ayy-chart__legend-toggle is clicked in plain HTML: it flips aria-pressed and sets data-hidden on the same-numbered bars or series (donuts, pies and stacked areas need React to work their shares out again).

react.import: import { BarChart, LineChart, HistogramChart, WaterfallChart, ScatterChart, DonutChart, GaugeChart, RadarChart, ChartLegend, ChartTooltip, HeatmapChart, FunnelChart, Sparkline, BarList, TableChart } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";

BarChart.renders: <figure class="ayy-chart"> with a plot of __column/__bar, labels, a legend and a visually hidden data table

props.label: string — what it shows ("Signups per day"); the data table's caption
props.stacked: boolean | "percent" — percent makes every column 100% (ticks read 0%–100%)
props.showValues: boolean — print values above the bars
props.horizontal: boolean — one row per label, bars along the reading direction
props.lines: { name, values: number[], color?, compare? }[] — lines over the columns on the same scale (a combo); not with horizontal
props.max: number — top of the scale; rounded up from the data if omitted
props.ticks: number of value lines, default 3; 0 for none
props.format: (value: number) => string — ticks, hover values and the table; default compact (1.2K)
props.legend: boolean — default: more than one series
props.toggle: boolean — make the legend's entries buttons that hide and show their series (the last one on stays on); the scale keeps its range so the rest don't jump
props.hiddenSeries: string[] — names switched off (controlled); with onHiddenSeriesChange
props.defaultHiddenSeries: string[] — names switched off at first

LineChart.renders: <figure class="ayy-chart"> with an __svg of __series paths, labels, a legend and a visually hidden data table

props.label: string — the data table's caption
props.series: { name, values: number[], color?, compare? }[] — compare draws a dashed comparison line
props.smooth: boolean, default true (monotone: never overshoots a point)
props.step: boolean — steps, each value held until halfway to the next
props.stacked: boolean — each area on the series before it, the top line the total; compare series stay apart
props.toggle: boolean — make the legend's entries buttons that hide and show their series (the last one on stays on); the scale keeps its range so the rest don't jump
props.hiddenSeries: string[] — names switched off (controlled); with onHiddenSeriesChange
props.defaultHiddenSeries: string[] — names switched off at first

HistogramChart.renders: <figure class="ayy-chart ayy-chart--histogram"> of touching columns, one per bin, each bin's start under it, and a data table of bin ranges

props.label: string — the data table's caption
props.values: number[] — the raw values, counted into bins
props.bins: number — about how many; edges are rounded. Default about √n, at most 20
props.range: [min, max] — the values the bins cover; default the data's
props.name: string — what's counted, the table's column header; default label
props.max: number — top of the count scale

WaterfallChart.renders: <figure class="ayy-chart ayy-chart--values ayy-chart--waterfall"> of floating bars, signed values above them, and a data table

props.label: string — the data table's caption
props.steps: { label, value, total? }[] — changes (negative for a drop) and totals (from zero)
props.name: string — the table's column header; default label
props.min: number — default 0, or the lowest running total below it
props.format: (value: number) => string — the sign is added for changes

ScatterChart.renders: <figure class="ayy-chart"> with axis names, a plot of __series of __dots, x labels, a legend and a data table of the points

props.label: string — the data table's caption
props.series: { name, points: { x, y, z?, label? }[], color? }[] — z sizes bubbles (by area)
props.zLabel: string — the bubble size's name in the table
props.xMin / xMax / yMin / yMax: number — the scales' ends; the minimums default to 0, the tops are rounded up
props.ticks: number of values along each axis, default 3; 0 for none
props.legend: boolean — default: more than one series
props.toggle: boolean — make the legend's entries buttons that hide and show their series (the last one on stays on); the scale keeps its range so the rest don't jump
props.hiddenSeries: string[] — names switched off (controlled); with onHiddenSeriesChange
props.defaultHiddenSeries: string[] — names switched off at first

DonutChart.renders: <figure class="ayy-chart"> with a __ring of __slices, the __total in the middle, a legend of shares beside it and a data table

props.label: string — the data table's caption
props.items: { name, value, color? }[] — the parts; six at most
props.pie: boolean — a solid pie, no total
props.total: ReactNode — the number in the middle; default the formatted sum
props.name: string — the table's column header; default label
props.size: CSS length — the ring's width, default 12rem
props.toggle: boolean — make the legend's entries buttons that hide and show their parts (the last one on stays on); the ring, the shares and the total are worked out again from what's on
props.hiddenSeries: string[] — names switched off (controlled); with onHiddenSeriesChange
props.defaultHiddenSeries: string[] — names switched off at first

GaugeChart.renders: <figure class="ayy-chart ayy-chart--gauge"> with a role="meter" plot: a half __ring, its __track and a __slice, the value under it

props.label: string — the meter's name ("Ad spend this month")
props.totalLabel: string — under the value and in aria-valuetext ("of $10K")
props.color: CSS colour, default chart-1 (warning past a limit)
props.size: CSS length — the arc's width, default 12rem

RadarChart.renders: <figure class="ayy-chart ayy-chart--radar"> with a square __svg of rings, spokes and __series shapes, spoke __labels, a legend and a data table

props.label: string — the data table's caption
props.axes: string[] — one per spoke, clockwise from the top
props.series: { name, values: number[], color?, compare? }[] — compare: dashed, no fill
props.max: number — the outer ring; rounded up from the data
props.ticks: number of rings counting the centre, default 5
props.size: CSS length — the plot's width, default 16rem
props.legend: boolean — default: more than one series
props.toggle: boolean — make the legend's entries buttons that hide and show their series (the last one on stays on); the scale keeps its range so the rest don't jump
props.hiddenSeries: string[] — names switched off (controlled); with onHiddenSeriesChange
props.defaultHiddenSeries: string[] — names switched off at first

ChartLegend.renders: <ul class="ayy-chart__legend"> of <li class="ayy-chart__legend-item">: a swatch and a name, a button around them (aria-pressed) when onToggle is given

props.items: { name, color?, compare?, line?, value? }[] — the entries; colours follow the chart tokens in order
props.hiddenItems: string[] — names shown as switched off; only with onToggle
props.onToggle: (name: string) => void — makes every entry a toggle button; a chart's own `toggle` prop wires this to its series for you

ChartTooltip.renders: <span class="ayy-chart__tooltip"> with a __tooltip-title and a __tooltip-row (swatch, name, value) for each series

props.title: ReactNode — the card's heading (a label, a slice's name)
props.rows: { name?, value, color? }[] — one per series; color is any CSS colour for the swatch
props.static: boolean — show it in place, always, instead of only over a hovered chart part

HeatmapChart.renders: <figure class="ayy-chart"> with an .ayy-heatmap of rows, a Less–More key and a data table

props.label: string — the data table's caption
props.columns: string[] — column names, every other one shown past eight
props.max: number — the darkest cell; default the largest value
props.legend: [less, more] | false — the key's words, default ["Less", "More"]

FunnelChart.renders: <ol class="ayy-funnel"> of steps with centred bars, values and rates

props.rate: "previous" | "first" — what each rate is a share of, default previous
props.rateLabel: string — read after each rate by screen readers; default "of the step before" / "of the first step"

props.label: string — makes it role="img" with this name; without it the sparkline is aria-hidden

props.max: number — value of a full bar, default the largest

TableChart.renders: <div class="ayy-table-wrap"><table class="ayy-table"> with headers, swatches and numeric cells

props.label: string — what it shows; the table's caption
props.labels: string[] — one per row along the side
props.format: (value: number) => string — cell values; default compact (1.2K)

a11y: The drawing is aria-hidden. The numbers go in a table with a <caption> saying what the chart shows, inside a <div class="ayy-sr-only"> (as React renders it): a table can't be narrower than its content, so hiding the table itself lets a long caption widen the page. Add a visible Table if people need to compare values.
Don't rely on colour alone: a legend names the series in the same order, the comparison series is dashed, and a title or a Stat states the takeaway ("Up 12% on last week").
Series tokens keep 3:1 against every surface in every theme. In High Contrast bars and lines take system colours, alternating between CanvasText and Highlight.
A Sparkline with a label is an image with that name; give it the trend in words ("Revenue, last 14 days, up 12%").

A gauge is one value, so it's a meter: role="meter" with aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax, aria-valuenow, an aria-valuetext in words ("$7.2K of $10K") and a name. A funnel and a bar list are text already and need no table.
Waterfall changes are signed (+$6.4K, −$1.3K) as well as coloured, and a donut's legend gives each share as a number.
do: Use a chart to show a trend or a comparison at a glance: signups per day, revenue against last month, traffic by source. Put it in a Card with the title and the key number (a Stat) above it.

Pick the form from the question: columns to compare amounts across periods (horizontal bars when the labels are long), stacked or 100% columns for parts over time, a line for a trend over many points (stacked areas for a total and its parts, steps for values that jump), a combo for amounts with their average or target, a histogram for how values spread, a waterfall for how one total became another, a scatter for how two measures relate (bubbles for a third), a donut or pie for a few parts of one whole, a gauge for one value against its limit, a radar to compare a few profiles over five to eight measures, a heatmap for activity by two dimensions (day × hour), a funnel for the steps people drop out of, a bar list for a ranking, a sparkline beside a number.
Colour series with the chart tokens in order (React does it). With a chart library, pass var(--ayy-chart-1)… (SVG) or chartColors() (canvas), and chartTheme() for its text, grid and tooltip.
Mark the previous period as a compare series instead of a second bright colour.
Keep the scale honest: bars start at 0; let chartScale() round the top.
dont: Don't use a chart when the exact numbers matter more than the shape — use a Table.
Don't use a donut or pie for more than five or six parts, for parts that are close in size, or to compare wholes — a Bar list or stacked columns are easier to read.
Don't use a radar for more than three series or for measures on different scales — use columns or a Table.
Don't use a gauge for a value with no meaningful maximum — use a Stat with a Sparkline.
Don't pick series colours from the status or accent tokens unless the colour means something (success for a goal line).
Don't draw more than six series; group the rest as Other.
Don't add a second chart library just for a simple bar or line — these cover dashboards. Reach for one (Recharts, Chart.js) for zoom, brushing or maps, themed with the tokens.
